title: Adult Education Instructor
description:
About this Job

This position is a full-time 10-month, unclassified, in-faculty staff position located on-site at our Bossier Campus and the Goodwill location in Shreveport.
This is a grant funded position.

In order to be considered for employment, applicant must attach the required documentation to the application or mail to: BPCC, Attn. HR, 6220 E. Texas St., Bossier City, LA 71111.

Required documentation includes college transcripts and three (3) letters of recommendation for employment. If employed by Bossier Parish Community College, official transcripts must be provided.

Any questions regarding this posting may be directed to hr@bpcc.edu or 318-678-6040.

Bossier Parish Community College is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer.
bpcc.edu

Minimum Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of teaching experience at the high school level or above.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently teach English Language Arts/Writing, Reading Comprehension, Mathematics, Social Studies, and Science to learners with varied academic skill levels.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to work independently, manage multiple responsibilities, maintain accurate records, and meet deadlines in a changing environment.
  • Ability to work a flexible daytime schedule and limited evening hours in response to program needs.
  • Willingness and ability to teach in a correctional facility setting when assigned and to obtain and maintain required facility clearance.
  • Willingness to complete required training after hire and obtain applicable qualifications or authorizations needed to support assigned industry-based credential instruction.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Commitment to ongoing education and continuing professional development.

Preferred

  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience teaching or training adult learners.
  • Experience working with adult learners from diverse educational, cultural, socioeconomic, or linguistic backgrounds.
  • Experience in adult education, higher education, correctional education, workforce training, Integrated Education and Training, or industry-based credential instruction.
  • Experience using educational technology and computer-assisted instruction.

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to communicate effectively with students, staff, partners, and the public in classroom, office, community, and secure institutional settings, as well as by telephone and electronic communication, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Must be able to use standard office and classroom equipment and software, including computers, projectors, copiers, and telephone systems, to perform essential job duties, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Must be able to review, prepare, and interpret written and electronic instructional materials, student records, data, and reports, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • May require occasional lifting or moving of office or classroom materials weighing up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Must be able to stand and actively instruct for extended instructional periods and alternate between standing and remaining in a stationary position during instructional and administrative activities, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Must be able to travel between assigned instructional sites and operate a motor vehicle for required work-related travel, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Must be able to work in secure institutional environments, including correctional facilities, with controlled access and security screening procedures, with or without reasonable accommodation.

The physical and environmental requirements described above are representative of those necessary to perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Specification

The Adult Education Instructor provides comprehensive instruction in English Language Arts/Writing, Reading Comprehension, Mathematics, Social Studies, and Science to adult learners preparing for a state-approved high school equivalency assessment, including HiSET/GED as applicable. The instructor also supports learners who are strengthening foundational academic skills for post-secondary education, workforce training, and employment.

The Goodwill location in Shreveport is the primary worksite for this position. The instructor works collaboratively with College Transition Programs staff and designated Goodwill personnel to coordinate instruction, enrollment support, student progress, and referrals while maintaining BPCC instructional, assessment, documentation, and reporting requirements.

This position requires the ability to independently deliver multi-subject instruction, administer standardized assessments, provide academic advising, maintain accurate program records, and contribute to measurable skill gains, student persistence, high school equivalency attainment, and successful transitions to postsecondary education, training, and employment. The employee may also be assigned to teach at a correctional facility or another College Transition Programs instructional site and may be scheduled for limited evening instruction based on program needs.

Job Duties and Other Information

Instructional Responsibilities

  • Develop, plan, and deliver effective instruction in English Language Arts/Writing, Reading Comprehension, Mathematics, Social Studies, and Science across varying academic levels.
  • Prepare adult learners for the state-approved high school equivalency assessment by aligning instruction with applicable high school equivalency content standards and the College and Career Readiness Standards for Adult Education.
  • Teach the reading, writing, quantitative reasoning, data interpretation, scientific reasoning, source analysis, and critical-thinking skills required across the high school equivalency subject areas.
  • Use whole-group, small-group, individualized, self-paced, tutoring, and computer-assisted instructional strategies to address varied learner needs and academic goals.
  • Select and adapt instructional materials and develop appropriate remediation or acceleration plans based on assessment results and student performance.
  • Contextualize academic instruction, as assigned, to support employability skills, workforce preparation, Integrated Education and Training, and college and career pathways.
  • Evaluate student learning regularly through formative and summative assessment and adjust instruction based on documented results.

Assessment and Student Progress

  • Administer approved adult education assessments, including TABE assessments and HiSET/GED official practice assessments, in accordance with program procedures and applicable testing requirements.
  • Interpret assessment results to identify instructional needs, establish academic goals, monitor progress, and determine readiness for high school equivalency testing.
  • Maintain accurate and timely attendance, assessment, progress, advising, and other student records required by BPCC, the Louisiana adult education system, and state and federal grant requirements.
  • Monitor instructional practices and student outcomes that contribute to measurable skill gains, student persistence, high school equivalency attainment, and transition outcomes.
  • Protect student information and maintain assessment integrity in accordance with institutional policy and applicable requirements.

Advising, Enrollment, and Student Support

  • Conduct individual advising sessions and provide timely feedback regarding academic progress, testing readiness, and college and career transition goals.
  • Participate in student enrollment, orientation, assessment, and placement activities as assigned.
  • Make appropriate referrals to BPCC, Goodwill, and community support services to address barriers and advance individual student goals.
  • Collaborate with College Transition Programs staff and designated Goodwill personnel to coordinate learner support, promote persistence, and improve student access and success.

Workforce and Industry-Based Credential Support

  • Integrate workforce readiness, employability skills, digital literacy, and career-contextualized learning into academic instruction when appropriate.
  • Support instruction connected to approved workforce pathways or industry-based credentials based on program needs and the employee's qualifications.
  • When assigned, complete necessary training and obtain and maintain any instructor qualification, certification, or authorization required to deliver industry-based credential preparation or training.
  • Provide industry-based credential instruction only when appropriately qualified or authorized and in accordance with the requirements of the credentialing body and BPCC.

Schedule and Instructional Environment

  • Maintain the Goodwill location in Shreveport as the position's primary worksite and fulfill the assigned instructional and administrative schedule at that location.
  • Provide limited evening instruction when assigned based on program and learner needs.
  • Provide instruction at a local correctional facility or another off-campus College Transition Programs site when assigned by the Director.
  • Obtain and maintain any clearance required to teach in a correctional facility.
  • Work effectively in secure institutional environments where access, movement, personal electronics, instructional materials, and internet use may be restricted.
  • Adapt to reasonable semester-to-semester changes in instructional schedule, course assignment, or delivery format based on program needs.

Travel Requirements

  • Maintain a valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Travel between the Goodwill location, BPCC locations, correctional facilities, and other assigned instructional sites as needed, including same-day travel.
  • Operate a motor vehicle for required travel between instructional sites. Mileage reimbursement is provided in accordance with institutional policy.

Professional Responsibilities and Grant Compliance

  • Participate in required orientation, professional development, training, departmental meetings, and continuous instructional improvement activities.
  • Maintain current knowledge of adult education instruction, high school equivalency requirements, assessment practices, and applicable state and federal program expectations.
  • Contribute to departmental compliance with institutional, state, federal, and grant requirements related to professional development, student attendance, retention, documentation, assessment, data quality, and program performance.
  • Communicate professionally and maintain effective working relationships with students, BPCC personnel, Goodwill staff, correctional facility personnel, and community partners.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Director, College Transition Programs.

title: Project Manager
description:
About this Opportunity:At Regency Centers, our people are our greatest asset, and we believe that our highly skilled and talented team makes us better. We are seeking a full-time Project Manager (Construction) to join our regional office located in Walnut Creek, California. The Project Manager leads construction across an assigned portfolio of existing shopping centers, with a primary focus on tenant improvements, landlord work, redevelopment, space reconfigurations, and property capital improvements. They manage budgets, schedules, consultants, and contractors from scope development and design through permitting, construction, tenant turnover, and closeout. This position works closely with Leasing, Property Management, Tenant Coordination, and Development Accounting to meet lease obligations and operating needs while coordinating work around existing tenants and customers. The Project Manager handles multiple concurrent projects and may support major ground-up developments as assigned.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Manage construction at existing shopping centers, including landlord work, tenant improvements, white box work, vacant space preparation, space divisions, redevelopment, and facade renovations. Ensure delivery is on time, on budget, and consistent with lease, design, and brand standards.
Assist with ground up development projects.
Collaborate with Leasing, Tenant Coordination, Property Management, and Legal to define landlord delivery obligations, evaluate scopes of work, and align lease language and construction exhibits. Coordinate landlord work with tenant delivery requirements.
Lead budgeting and scheduling for tenant, redevelopment, and property construction projects, including estimates for landlord lease obligations and capital improvements. Monitor and forecast costs, address risks, and track deviations from plan.
Oversee the preparation and execution of construction contracts and change orders in partnership with Contract Administration. Ensure contractor performance, insurance compliance, and lien waiver documentation.
Manage existing condition assessments, design, permitting, and utility coordination for tenant work, redevelopment, and property improvements. Evaluate constructability, support entitlement approvals when needed, and plan construction phasing to limit disruption to tenants and customers.
Manage assigned property capital improvements in coordination with Property Management, including roof replacements, parking lot reconstruction, facade work, HVAC replacements, and major site or building system upgrades.
Track project milestones, landlord completion dates, and closeout requirements. Maintain project reporting tools and internal dashboards, and provide regular updates to construction leadership, Property Management, Tenant Coordination, and Accounting.

Are You Qualified?

Bachelor’s degree in Construction Engineering, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or related field
Minimum five (5) years of retail or commercial construction management experience, to include supervisory experience
Ability to travel regionally & frequently visit all assigned construction sites
Ability to work varying and flexible hours as needed for tenant delivery, construction in operating shopping centers, and public meetings
Experience with tenant improvements, redevelopment, and construction in operating shopping centers preferred
Knowledge of retail construction, tenant improvements, redevelopment, existing building systems, and permitting
Skilled in reviewing documents for conformity to standards of Regency jurisdictions and/or tenants
Ability to comprehend architectural and engineering drawings and complex legal documents
Proficiency with personal computers and MS Office, MS Excel, MS Project, Zoom, & JD Edwards software
Skilled in analyzing construction costs for landlord lease obligations, tenant improvements, redevelopment, and property capital projects and recommending budgetary adjustments as appropriate

  • Regency Centers will not sponsor employment-based immigration petitions or applications for this position, including but not limited to H-1B, TN visa, or permanent residency.

Personal Traits We Value:

Project management skills (planning, organizing, informing, directing others)
Decisiveness, problem-solving, time-management, multi-tasking and presentation skills
Communication skills (interpersonal savvy, customer focus, oral and written communication)
Trust and integrity
Negotiation and conflict resolution skills
Ability to work within a team environment

A Little Bit About Us:

We own and operate premier shopping centers in suburban neighborhoods in the top cities and markets across the country. We live by a strong set of values, which have guided us for more than 60 years.

Our centers thrive with highly productive grocers, restaurants, service providers, and terrific retailers that connect to their communities and customers. We are also active developers of new shopping centers that feature great merchandising, placemaking, and customer engagement as part of our Fresh Look™ program.

We are a vertically integrated real estate company and a qualified real estate investment trust (REIT) that is self-administered, self-managed, and an S&P 500 Index member. Learn more about us at RegencyCenters.com.

Benefits:

Our compensation and benefits package is very competitive and includes the following benefits and more. For additional information visit www.regencycenters.com/careers.

Work/Life Balance

23+ PTO days annually
11 paid holidays (in addition to PTO)
Paid leave programs (parental, compassion, bereavement, jury duty, and military)
Health Advocacy + Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Financial Security

401(k) with a generous company match plus corporate profit sharing
Anniversary stock grant awards
Health Savings Account (HSA), Health Care FSA, and Dependent Care FSA
100% company paid Life Insurance/AD&D and Disability Insurance
Voluntary benefits (supplemental life/AD&D, critical illness, accident, hospital indemnity, and identity theft)
Student loan repayment resources

Health and Wellness

Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
Award winning and incentives-based wellbeing program through Personify Health
Family planning, mental health, and pain management programs

Community Focused

52 hours per year of paid Volunteer Time Off
Company gift matching

Growth and Development

Tuition reimbursement
Continued education opportunities
LinkedIn Learning premium subscription
Professional membership support
Employee Resource Groups

title: Production Utility
description:
General Purpose

Demonstrate proficiency in a range of processes, procedures, and equipment to perform various operator roles in the plant production environment. Serve as a resource to others to solve problems and/or assist with operator activities or production equipment.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform a variety of line duties within the manufacturing environment to machine operator, and/or break relief operator jobs (e.g., Receiver, Blend/Filler/CIP/Retort/ Evaporator/Pasteurizer operators). This may include troubleshooting and performing minor maintenance repairs
  • Clean, set-up, operate, and monitor equipment on the production line
  • Ensure that the proper materials are used for each product being produced
  • Complete all required documentation and scheduled quality checks
  • Review charts, screens, quality check sheets, and specifications that are in both hard copy and electronic format
  • Perform cleaning and sanitation tasks as required to maintain plant equipment; complete cleaning checklist once line has completed run
  • Prepare equipment for next run to include size changes as needed
  • Maintain communication with other departments, supervisor, and employees and notify them of any problems and/or concerns that may restrict the efficiency of production
  • Ensure all paperwork is filled out in a clear, legible, and accurate format and completed with required information. Ensure all required information is documented in accordance with SOP’s
  • Review process data and equipment performance data to improve quality, throughput, and troubleshoot
  • Assist with training efforts in functional area as needed
  • Follow all DFA good manufacturing practices (GMP) and work in a manner consistent with all corporate regulatory, food safety, quality, and sanitation requirements
  • Maintain safe working conditions for employees and compliance with all state and federal regulations regarding health and safety issues
  • The requirements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employee, but is not a complete list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Other duties may be assigned as required

title: Financial Specialist
description:
Who We Are
Join us at the First Nations Financial Management Board (FMB), where we support First Nations to strengthen their governance and financial practices. Since our establishment in 2006 under the First Nations Fiscal Management Act, we have been dedicated to providing fully optional tools and services tailored to meet the unique needs of First Nations communities.
As an independent organization governed by a Board of Directors, the FMB is committed to fostering self-determination and financial sustainability. Be a part of our mission to support First Nations in achieving their financial goals and enhancing their administrative capabilities.
Why Apply

Flexible work hours and a 37.5-hour work week
Above average wellness days, and holidays
Opportunities for professional development and career growth
A talented, diverse, and inclusive team doing transformative work on a national scale
Remote and hybrid work opportunities available

What You Will Do

Support the delivery of the Financial Reporting and Audit Preparation Services (FRAP), an FMB-led initiative designed to help First Nations address overdue financial reporting and audit requirements while strengthening financial governance and supporting economic self-determination.
Develop relationships with assigned clients that have an approved Financial Administration Law.
Build trust and secure buy-in to implement their FAL and ultimately prepare for FMS certification.
Conduct the FMS Support Services needs assessment and identify opportunities for remote accounting and training opportunities.
With the Senior Financial Officer, develop a training plan based on the information provided in the initial needs assessment.
Develop a remote accounting service schedule based on the priorities identified in the FMS Support Services readiness assessment.
Support First Nation FAL clients to achieve FMS certification via full cycle remote accounting services, training, and capacity development.
Complete any other tasks as requested by FMS Support Services management team.

Who You Are

A Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or another business-related field; A CPA designation or progress towards a CPA designation considered an asset.
Must have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in providing financial services including reporting, funding agreements, and internal controls preferably within an Indigenous, government, or not for profit environment.
Demonstrated experience working with Microsoft Office and information and data management systems; Sage 300 an asset.
Strong working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
Must have an understanding, awareness and appreciation of Indigenous culture and history; Willing to participate in ongoing education and training for the role including Indigenous studies.
Must be fluent in English (spoken and written), French (spoken and written) an asset.

Equivalent or relevant education and/or experience may be considered.
What to Expect
FMB aims to keep the recruitment process as open as possible. As such, candidates can expect the following steps:

Initial phone screen
Panel interview with 3 FMB members
Financial knowledge assessment
References, background check, and a trait assessment
Offer

FMB is committed to inclusive practices. As such, please email hr@fnfmb.com should you require any accommodations as a candidate or if would like a copy of the full job description.
FMB is an equal opportunity employer that recognizes and celebrates the diversity of all First Nations and people across Canada. We are an inclusive organization that treats all employees equally. As a First Nations Organization, applicants of Indigenous descent will be given preference.

title: Automotive Dealership Porter Associate Sign-On Bonus
description:
Automotive Dealership Porter Associate – $1,500 Sign-On Bonus

Part-Time | Tuesdays & Thursdays | Approximately 15 Hours Per Week

Typical Start: 8:00 AM
End Time: When the day's assigned work is completed

Area: Idaho Falls, Ammon, Shelley, Iona, Rigby, and nearby communities

Pay: $22.00++ per hour + $1,500 Sign-On Bonus

Hourly compensation includes a base rate and per-vehicle photo payout.

Pay may be flexible depending on experience and qualifications.

A Different Kind of Automotive Job

Looking for work that gets you out of a traditional workplace?

Pro-MotionPix works with automotive dealerships to help them keep their vehicle listings current and ready for online shoppers. We're looking for a dependable part-time team member to visit dealerships in the Idaho Falls area and complete scheduled vehicle assignments.

You'll spend most of your time outside and on your feet. Some days you'll be searching a lot for specific vehicles, while other assignments may involve moving cars, locating keys, checking inventory information, or documenting vehicles for online listings.

You'll also use a company-provided iPhone and mobile application to take standardized vehicle images, 360° views, and videos.

Photography experience isn't necessary. You'll receive paid training and learn our system, equipment, and expectations before working independently.

This position is about following a reliable process and getting assignments completed correctly—not creating artistic photographs.

How the Workday Comes Together

After arriving at a dealership, you may be responsible for:

  • Reviewing the vehicles assigned for that location
  • Finding specific vehicles throughout the dealership property
  • Tracking down keys and confirming vehicle information
  • Coordinating with dealership employees when something is missing or unavailable
  • Moving vehicles into the appropriate location when necessary
  • Photographing vehicles according to Pro-MotionPix standards
  • Creating 360° views and vehicle videos
  • Entering completed work through a mobile application
  • Checking your work for accuracy before moving to the next assignment
  • Updating the team when a vehicle cannot be located or an issue needs attention
  • Traveling to additional dealership locations as assigned
  • Finishing the scheduled workload within the expected timeframe

Because you'll visit customer locations on your own, being dependable and able to manage your time is important.

Your Previous Experience Can Be Valuable

There isn't one specific background we're looking for.

People who have worked in jobs involving vehicles, physical activity, customer locations, or independent work can often transition well into this position.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Automotive dealerships or service departments
  • Vehicle detailing or lot operations
  • Warehouse and inventory work
  • Delivery and route driving
  • Construction and installation
  • Landscaping or grounds work
  • Maintenance and facilities
  • Moving or other physically active jobs
  • Merchandising or field service

If you're used to working with your hands, moving throughout the day, following instructions, and getting things done without someone standing over your shoulder, this may be a good opportunity.

What We Need From You

The ideal candidate is someone who:

  • Can be counted on to show up and complete scheduled assignments
  • Is comfortable working independently
  • Pays attention to details
  • Can stay organized while visiting different locations
  • Doesn't mind walking a large dealership lot
  • Is comfortable being outside in changing weather
  • Can communicate respectfully with dealership employees
  • Knows how to handle unexpected situations without becoming easily frustrated
  • Can learn and consistently use a mobile application
  • Takes responsibility for the quality of their work


Requirements


Qualifications

You should have:

  • A valid driver's license
  • A dependable personal vehicle
  • A consistent employment history; one year or more preferred
  • The ability to travel between assigned dealership locations
  • The ability to walk, stand, bend, and perform routine physical tasks throughout the workday
  • The ability to work outdoors in varying weather
  • Basic comfort with smartphones and mobile technology
  • Good communication and problem-solving abilities
  • Previous hands-on work experience is preferred
  • Manual transmission experience is helpful, but not required
  • The ability to successfully complete a background check and pre-employment drug screening


Benefits

What You Get

  • $22.00++ per hour
  • $1,500 sign-on bonus
  • Base pay plus per-vehicle photo compensation
  • Paid training
  • Company-provided iPhone and equipment
  • Mileage reimbursement between dealership locations
  • Company uniform
  • Consistent Tuesday and Thursday schedule
  • No regular weekend work
  • Independent work environment

See the Job Before You Commit

We want you to know what you're getting into before you apply.

Visit the Pro-MotionPix Careers page and watch our Day in the Life and Pay Plan videos. They provide a better picture of the work, daily expectations, and how the compensation structure works.

Interested?

If you want a part-time job that keeps you moving, gets you out of an office, and gives you the independence to manage your own work at different automotive dealerships, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today and start your next opportunity with Pro-MotionPix.

title: Electronics Engineer
description:
Dawn Aerospace has become the biggest green propulsion provider in the world, and our ambitions are even greater. We’re growing our portfolio of products to be even more performant, reliable and mass-manufacturable.

As an Electronics Engineer, you will directly contribute to the design, qualification, and production of high-reliability electronics for our space propulsion systems. You will play a key role in developing flight-ready propulsion electronics, working across design, testing, and manufacturing in close collaboration with systems, mechanical, and production teams.

This role is open for both Intermediate and Senior Engineers. The scope of responsibility and technical ownership will be aligned to experience and capability.

This role combines hands-on electronics engineering with end-to-end ownership and offers exposure to the full lifecycle of flight hardware, from early concepts and prototypes through qualification and release to production.

If you want a role where you can just do the same thing every day, then this is not for you. We’re looking for a highly motivated, talented Electronics/Aviation Engineer who is unafraid to own complex problems and their solution.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and develop mixed-signal, power, and embedded electronics for space applications
  • Detailed design of in-space electronics including component selection, schematics capture and layout using KiCAD and maintain designs in Git
  • Apply ECSS/NASA design practices to ensure reliability and robustness in the space environment
  • Plan and execute verification, qualification, and acceptance test campaigns
  • Perform hands-on bring-up, debugging, and root-cause analysis using standard lab equipment
  • Support new product development from concept through design, test, and production
  • Contribute to manufacturing support and continuous improvement of released hardware
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver hardware on schedule

What we’re looking for

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electronics or Mechatronics Engineering, or demonstration of equivalent ability
  • Minimum 1–3+ years' experience designing, building, and testing electronics hardware
  • Strong understanding of electric circuit design fundamentals and electrical engineering principles
  • Passion for PCB design and developing high reliability electronics
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills and ability to communicate technical topics clearly
  • Strong PCB schematic and layout design ability using KiCAD, Altium or similar.
  • Practical experience using laboratory test equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads)
  • Familiarity with Python for basic testing or analysis
  • Experience with version control (Git or similar)

What will set you apart

  • Experience with design and testing for EMC
  • Design for high reliability, fault-tolerant systems
  • Experience with electronics radiation tolerance and testing
  • Experience with component selection for extreme environments
  • Familiarity with high-reliability standards (ECSS, NASA, automotive, or medical)
  • Understanding of DFM/DFT principles
  • Experience with robust testing or qualification regimes

We welcome engineers from all industries, especially those from high-performance environments.

Why Dawn?

Our teams are small, highly capable, and move quickly. You’ll work hands-on as part of Dawn’s propulsion team, alongside the engineers developing our spaceplane and in-space hardware, with real ownership from early concepts through to flight-ready systems that actually fly. We expect engineers to solve difficult problems, make decisions, and see their work have a direct impact on the future of space access.

Based in Christchurch, you’ll be part of a globally ambitious aerospace and deep-tech community, with mountains, coastline, and adventure on your doorstep.

Diversity & Inclusion

At Dawn Aerospace, we believe that diverse teams build better solutions. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences are valued and supported to do their best work.

About Dawn Aerospace

Dawn Aerospace is a space transportation company with a purpose.
Our mission is to enable the next generation of space users by providing more sustainable and scalable ways to access and move around in space. We believe this access, in the form of a transportation network, will fundamentally change what’s possible from space. We currently focus on three areas of space transportation:

  • In-space propulsion
    We're a leading supplier of turnkey green propulsion systems for various classes of satellites. Our systems utilise safe, accessible propellants and we have over 170 of these propulsion units on more than 40 operational satellites already. A further 200 units are in production.
  • In-space servicing
    Coupled with our propulsion expertise, we are ensuring that our customers' satellites are refuellable. In the coming years, Dawn will offer a refueling service to enable life extension of customer satellites. This new market is aligned with our sustainability goal to ensue a clean and safe space for everyone!
  • Spaceplane
    We are developing the fastest and highest-flying aircraft ever to take off from a runway, combining the extreme performance of rocket propulsion with the reusability of conventional airplanes to enable high-frequency, low-cost access to sub-orbital space.

Our international teams are distributed across four locations: the Netherlands, France, New Zealand, and the USA.

Apply for this Job

Important!

If you think you have what it takes but are unsure that you check every box, we still want to hear from you.

To all recruitment agencies: Dawn Aerospace does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our job’s alias, our employees, or any other company location. Dawn Aerospace will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Lenape Valley Foundation is seeking a full-time Certified Peer Specialist to join our Bright Path Center, where you will play a critical role in supporting individuals experiencing behavioral health crises. title: Houseperson
description:
Courtyard by Marriott Milwaukee Downtown
Milwaukee, WI 53203

SECTION ONE: MCR Universal Role Standards

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

CLEANLINESS and FRIENDLINESS!
The MCR standard is to provide clean, friendly, well-organized and safe hotels for our guests.

AREAS OF EXCELLENCE

Happy Guests
Spotless Cleanliness
Product Consistency & Quality
Teamwork

Duties and Expectations
1. Happy Guests

Guest Relations: Greet guests happily upon arrival and throughout their stay with a smile.
Name Use: Use the guests’ names whenever possible, ensuring they feel properly welcomed.
Guest Satisfaction: All Team Members work together to contribute to great guest satisfaction scores.
Recovery: Ability to handle challenging guest situations with hospitality and a sense of urgency.
Hotel Knowledge: Strong knowledge of all features of the hotel facility and amenities.
Events: Awareness and support for all groups and events at the hotel.
Technology: Understanding of relevant technology for each role.
Phone Etiquette: Answer all incoming calls with friendly service using the approved greeting.

2. Spotless Cleanliness

Sparkling Clean Workspaces: All areas, both front and back of the house, should be kept clean and well-organized.
Pitching In: Cleanliness is a team effort! Everyone may expect to pitch in to clean guest rooms and public spaces as needed, to ensure the hotel is well-organized and safe.
Hospitality While Cleaning: Always greet every guest happily with a smile, by name if possible, while cleaning.

3. Product Consistency & Quality

Checklists to 100% Accuracy: All operational checklists are completed accurately and at the designated times, every shift.
Shift Handover Reports: Handover reports must be accurate and on time, for effective shift-to-shift communication.
Flawless Uniform: All Team Members must wear a clean, approved uniform and be well-groomed per the Team Member Handbook, while wearing a nametag and smiling at all times.

4. Teamwork

Communication: Communication between Team Members should be clear, honest, and professional.
Can Do Attitude: Willing to stretch beyond traditional role to meet the needs of the business and MCR’s guests.
Collaboration: All Team Members at all levels must be committed to working together to create a welcoming environment for guests and an effective, positive workplace.

SECTION TWO: Houseperson, Role Specific Duties and Expectations

Other Duties and Expectations

Luggage Handling: Store and retrieve luggage or packages for guests in storage areas, as needed.
Cleaning and Trash Management: Clean and maintain the guest hallways, stairwells, service areas and ice rooms. Collect trash from all exterior garbage receptacles, as well as picking up trash and debris from the parking lot, swimming pool area and common grounds. All front and back of house areas should be well-organized and clean. Collect trash and soiled linen from the housekeepers and deliver to laundry room.
Furniture Upkeep: Monitor placement and condition of public space furniture, report issues to management.
Restocking: Maintain stock levels in guest floor linen closets and guest amenities. Replenish amenities and supplies in assigned guestrooms. Stock and maintain housekeeping cart.

SECTION THREE: Success Metrics

Happy Guests

Management Performance Ratings
Guest Satisfaction Scores/Intent to Return

Spotless Cleanliness

GM/AGM Spot Checks
Leadership Walk-throughs (RVP, etc.)
Guest Ratings/Reviews

Product Consistency & Quality

Checklist Tracking
Management Performance Ratings
Guest Ratings

Teamwork

Management Performance Ratings

SECTION FOUR: Qualifications & Requirements

Qualifications & Requirements:

Experience in a hospitality, service, consumer-facing franchise or related field preferred.
Can-Do Attitude: Must have a positive attitude and willingness to learn.
Ability to Follow Guidelines: Must be able to understand and follow established guidelines and procedures.
Handle Pace and Pressure: Must work well in stressful, high-pressure situations.
Listening, Conflict Resolution: Must be effective at listening to, understanding, clarifying, and resolving the concerns and issues raised by co-workers and guests.
Communication Skills: Must be able to convey information and ideas clearly.
Hospitality and Guest Service: Must have a desire to serve all guests.
Age Requirement: Must be 18 years of age or older to perform this job.
Schedule and Travel: Must be willing to work a varied schedule that may include evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays based upon the demands of the hotel.
Clock-in/Out: Arrive and clock in on time for every shift worked and clock out at the scheduled shift ending time, unless otherwise directed by your immediate supervisor. Never work while off the clock.
Breaks: Clock in/out for breaks at the designated time on your schedule.
Call Outs: Provide sufficient notice as directed by your supervisor when calling out for a scheduled shift.

Physical Working Demands & Working Environment:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to carry out physical working demands such as:

Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at waist. Requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.
Climbing: Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms.
Balancing: Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing or crouching on narrow, slippery or erratically moving surfaces.
Kneeling: Bending legs at knee to come to rest on one or both knees.
Crawling: Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
Standing: Remaining upright on the feet, particularly for sustained periods of time.
Walking: Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
Repetitive Motions: Making substantial movements (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.
Lifting: Carrying certain housekeeping items such as linens, trash, or vacuums.

Note:
This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) of this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. Employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily and, if requested, reasonable accommodations will be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their job, absent undue hardship. The Employer retains the right to change or assign other duties to this position.

This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship.

The Equipment Technician will be responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and supporting manufacturing equipment during an assigned shift. This position is ideal for a hands-on technician with experience working with manufacturing machinery and a strong interest in equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.

  • Follow established maintenance procedures, safety requirements, and operational protocols.
  • Assist with the installation, setup, calibration, upgrades, and modifications of new or existing equipment.

Qualifications & Experience

title: Outbound Runner Associate
description:
L and R Distributors is looking for a Full time Outbound Runner Worker to join our team. This position works on the warehouse floor, processing orders by picking and filling boxes/containers. He/she will send and accept shipments while keeping the warehouse clean and safe at all times.

The ideal candidate has experience working in an environment that can be cold and hot during different seasons. This person will need to be able to work safely and quickly, standing for long periods while fulfilling orders.

Responsibilities:

  • Inventory - Pick and pack products as ordered by the customer into bins, boxes, and containers. Maintain an inventory list and assist with restocking products and supplies as needed. title: Amphinicy Technologies - Senior 5G - Ntn Stack Engineer
description:
We are looking for a 5G-Ntn Software Stack Engineer to reinforce our team which has more than two decades of experience in the satellite industry. As our new colleague you contribute to the design, development, integration, and validation of software components that enable standard 3GPP 5G Nr services over satellite links.

This is what you do

  • You will work on disaggregated RAN and core network functions, cloud orchestration, Ntn-aware signal processing, and test environments that emulate real satellite conditions.
  • You will be an integral part of an already existing multidisciplinary team of experienced, friendly, and talented colleagues, who are working across 5G, SATCOM, DSP, Virtualization, and system validation.
  • The work includes developing and integrating software around Openairinterface-based Gnb and 5gc functions, containerized MicroServices, Kubernetes orchestration, traffic simulation, and Ntn channel emulation.
  • The goal is to deliver a robust, scalable, and standards-compliant platform that supports unmodified commercial user equipment in Direct-to-Handheld scenarios.
  • You'll have the chance to work with cutting-edge technologies and take a leading role in ensuring the satellite communications of the future work properly!
  • You will actively participate in a highly innovative project at the intersection of 5G, satellite communications, and cloud infrastructure. At the same time, you contribute to a real system demonstrator, not only to research studies.
  • You collaborate with experts in software architecture, DSP, Ntn, and system validation and help shaping future ground-segment products and next-generation 5G-Ntn capabilities.

This is what you give

  • You hold an MSc or PhD in Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  • You have strong software development skills in C++, Python and Matlab.
  • You have a good understanding of 3GPP 5G Nr, RAN architecture, and 5gc concepts.
  • You have a good understanding of 5G protocol stack layers, including Phy, Mac, Rlc, Pdcp, and Rrc.
  • You are familiar with 3GPP Release 16/17/18 features relevant to 5G Nr and Ntn.
  • You are familiar with satellite channel emulation for Ntn scenarios, including delay, Doppler, and link impairment modelling.
  • You have hands-on experience with Linux-based development and networking.
  • You are familiar with Oai-RAN, Oai-Cn and DSP for wireless systems.
  • You can debug complex distributed systems and work across software, networking, and Radio domains, and have thorough experience with SDR platforms such as Usrp.
  • You communicate easily and enjoy working closely with other software developers, but also product managers, and validation engineers
  • You are a fast learner, eager for new concepts, not afraid when challenged to apply them
  • You can work independently when given tasks, but you also know when to ask for help
  • You produce clean, readable, and well-structured documentation in impeccable English
  • You preferably have a work permit for the country of Luxembourg
This is what's nice to have:
  • Experience with cloud-native tools such as Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Familiarity with AWS, network Virtualization, or MicroServices.
  • Knowledge of Ru/DU/Cu disaggregation, and functional split options such as Option 1, Option 2, Option 7.2x, and Option 8.
  • Familiarity with O-RAN concepts and architecture, including Ric, SMO, and interfaces such as O1, O2, and E2.
  • Familiarity with performance testing, traffic modelling, and automated validation frameworks.
  • Familiarity with ETSI NFV/Mano, OSS, and orchestration concepts for virtualized Telecom platforms.
  • Familiarity with DVB-S2x and DVB-Gse.
  • Familiarity with Difi and Ecpri.
  • Familiarity with CUDA, Hls, and VHDL.

This is what you get

  • An attractive salary and relocation package.
  • A comprehensive training plan, starting with onboarding, which caters to your development needs and helps you achieve your career goals.
  • A supportive environment where people come first.
  • Flexible and partly remote working options.
  • An opportunity to work in a challenging fast-paced environment with the latest technologies which affect the lives of billions of peoplearound the globe.
  • Work-life balance which includes an exciting lifestyle in the heart of Europe, in the multicultural city of Luxembourg.
This is us:
Amphinicy Technologies is a leading provider of complex software solutions for the space industry. We have been delivering solutions to the top players and organizations in the satellite and space industry for over 20 years, from our two offices in both Croatia and Luxembourg. Our engineers are leading experts in the domains of Satellite Communication and Earth Observation, and our unending focus is the perpetual improvement of the quality and efficiency of our state-of-the-art solutions in a creative, enjoyable, and supportive work environment.
This is your place of work:
Luxembourg is situated at the crossroads of Europe, between Germany, Belgium, and France. Despite its small size it sports a powerful economy with several well-paid and diverse job opportunities, and with long-term career prospects. A top-notch infrastructure, one of the best healthcare systems in Europe and a vibrant and multicultural lifestyle complete the puzzle of one of the best countries to live and work in.

title: Communications Officer 2
description:
Description


About the Agency & Division:
The Washington State Patrol is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer and strives to foster an environment in which everyone is encouraged to be their authentic selves, communicate openly, and act with courage. The WSP is dedicated to promoting fair and equitable hiring, training, and promotional practices through innovative recruitment and retention strategies..

The Communications Division operates a 24-hour-a-day, 365-day-a-year statewide emergency communications systems, which includes seven centers. The division provides emergency dispatch services for the Washington State Patrol, and 18 other State, Federal, and Tribal Agencies on contract basis including Department of Fish and Wildlife, Washington State Liquor & Cannabis Board, State Parks, U.S. Marshal and Muckleshoot Tribal Police.

Duties

A CO2’s primary responsibility is to efficiently multi-task technologies answering emergency 911 and business phone calls, entering and updating calls for service and self-initiated activity into a Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) Computer system and transmitting and receiving radio communications from field personnel.

Our new trainer will be able to:

  • Provide on the job training and evaluate new employees in the key work activities.
  • Use formalized training material.
  • Act as a resource.
  • Provide professional customer service using skills learned to manage and control emergency calls.
  • Use resources such as CAD, computer mapping, and access to sensitive databases to provide timely support and service.
  • Consistently provide exceptional customer service.
  • Project a positive attitude, proactively and willingly assist others in performance of their duties or in a responding to requests from customers.
  • Practice situational awareness and be a problem solver.
  • Earn the trust, respect, and confidence of leadership, co-workers and customers.
  • Maintain confidentiality of information accessed or discussed in performing the work of this position.
  • Analyze, troubleshoot, consult, and document emergencies.
  • Transmit, broadcast, control, and operate multi-frequency two-way radio console.
  • Monitor officer safety status constantly.
  • Apply advanced telecommunicator skills to quickly assess and determine the proper course of action to provide the most efficient and appropriate response during mission critical situations.
  • Manage multiple frequencies to provide timely responses to units in the field.
  • Transmit and receive communications.
  • Complete multiple tasks and technologies simultaneously.
  • Explain information.
  • Actively listen.
  • Use call control skills.
  • Identify their need for police, fire, medical aid, traffic control etc. and locate the proper jurisdiction for response.
  • Utilize multi-line phones, 911 line, business lines, computer mapping equipment, and computer aided dispatch (CAD).
  • Dispatch calls for service.
  • Communicate with field units via radio and provide requested support by investigating information through law enforcement sensitive databases, calling tows, coordinating aid, Life Flight, bomb squads, other tactical teams, confirming warrants, missing person records, stolen property, stolen vehicles, and memorializing all information into CAD logs.
  • Perform inquiries and interpret information from law enforcement sensitive databases.
  • Accurately enter alphanumeric data into computer systems.
  • Use computer hardware and software (i.e. data management programs such as CAD, ACCESS, etc.).
  • Making notifications to executive command staff, federal highway personnel and Department of Transportation (DOT) concerning major incidents affecting the highways and other events via email, phone, etc.

Qualifications

  • Current WSP employee with one years experience as a Communications Officer 1 within the last two years.

title: Data Architect
location: Noida, UP, IN; Hyderabad, TS, IN; Bengaluru, KA, IN
description:
About Signant Health
At Signant Health, we help bring life-changing treatments to patients faster. We are a global evidence generation company that supports clinical trials with smart technology, scientific expertise, and hands-on operational support — so better data leads to better decisions in healthcare. We embrace AI and advanced technologies to enhance every aspect of what we do, from data analysis to operational efficiency.
Our teams work at the intersection of science, technology, and patient experience, delivering digital solutions powered by AI innovation that make clinical trials more efficient, more accurate, and more accessible around the world. Trusted by leading pharmaceutical companies and CROs, our platforms and services support studies across more than 90 countries and have contributed to hundreds of new drug approvals.
If you are motivated by meaningful work, global impact, and innovation in clinical research and digital health — including the opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI technologies — you will find purpose and opportunity at Signant Health.

About the Role
The Data Architect will define and lead the enterprise data architecture and strategy that brings data from Signant Health's diverse operational systems into Snowflake, our primary enterprise data platform. As an individual contributor reporting to the Chief Architect, this role combines strategic architectural thinking with hands-on data engineering — building the frameworks and reference pipelines that engineering teams adopt and scale. This is an opportunity to break down data silos, reduce redundant integrations, and enable data-driven decision making and AI across the organization.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES - Function
Data Architecture & Strategy

Define and maintain the target-state enterprise data architecture and multi-year roadmap, with Snowflake as the central data platform.
Document the current-state data landscape across SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, MongoDB, and enterprise SaaS applications; perform gap analysis and develop a prioritized onboarding roadmap.
Establish architectural principles, reference architectures, and standard patterns for data ingestion, storage, transformation, and consumption; evaluate and recommend tooling via build-vs.-buy analysis.

Data Integration & Engineering

Design and build ingestion patterns — CDC, batch, streaming, and API-based — using AWS-native and Snowflake-native services (AWS DMS, Glue, Kinesis/MSK, Snowpipe, dbt) and establish engineering standards for pipelines, CI/CD, observability, and error handling.
Develop source-to-target reconciliation and validation frameworks consistent with ALCOA+ data integrity principles; optimize Snowflake performance and cost as data volumes grow.

Data Modeling & Master Data

Design enterprise and canonical data models and a layered Snowflake architecture (raw, conformed, and curated/medallion layers), including conformed business entities shared across products.
Establish master and reference data management approaches; guide selection of dimensional, Data Vault, or other modeling techniques appropriate to each use case.

Data Governance, Quality & Compliance

Define the enterprise data governance framework including ownership, stewardship, data contracts, quality monitoring, metadata management, and end-to-end data lineage.
Design data protection controls (classification, RBAC, masking, tokenization of PII/PHI) and ensure the architecture supports GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA, GDPR, and SOC 2 requirements.

Analytics, AI & Technical Leadership

Partner with BI, analytics, and AI teams to deliver curated data products for reporting, self-service analytics, and AI/ML use cases including RAG pipelines and Snowflake Cortex AI.
Lead cross-team architecture reviews, mentor engineers, and serve as the primary technical liaison with Snowflake and other data platform vendors.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ATTRIBUTESEssential:

5+ years in data engineering or software engineering, including experience in data architecture and delivering production Snowflake solutions.
Deep experience integrating heterogeneous sources (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, MongoDB, enterprise SaaS); expert SQL and data modeling skills; proficiency in Python and dbt.
Proven AWS experience (S3, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions, IAM); experience with orchestration, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code (Airflow, Terraform, Git).
Experience designing governance, security, and compliance controls for regulated data; ability to produce architecture artifacts and influence stakeholders without direct authority.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent experience.

Preferred:

Experience in pharmaceutical, clinical research, or another regulated industry (GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA, GDPR, GAMP 5); familiarity with CDISC SDTM/ODM or HL7 FHIR.
Advanced Snowflake experience (Snowpark, Dynamic Tables, Iceberg, Cortex AI, Secure Data Sharing); experience with AI/ML enablement, data catalog/observability tools, or data mesh patterns.
SnowPro Advanced certification; AWS data or solutions architecture certifications a plus.

  • We have the courage to do the right thing

Position Summary Verista is looking for an experienced Senior Subject Matter Expert (SME) to act as Lead GxP Auditor on a client engagement with Client. The SME will design, deliver, and support a custom Lunch and Learn training on combination products for Client process owners. The training covers applicable regulatory requirements, quality system expectations, process owner responsibilities, and key compliance considerations. Its goals are to raise awareness, clarify who owns what, and support consistent execution across business processes.

Key Responsibilities

Phase 1 – Presentation Development (approx. 90 hours)

  • Lead a kickoff meeting with Client stakeholders to understand organizational needs and training objectives.
  • Capture the risks identified during assessments and interviews, along with key elements of the proposed future state, to keep the content focused and relevant.
  • Review Client's combination product processes and applicable quality system requirements.
  • Develop a customized Quality & Compliance Lunch and Learn presentation that incorporates key standards and industry best practices.
  • Work with business unit quality and compliance stakeholders to make sure topics, risks, and regulatory requirements are adequately covered, and get Client's approval before delivery.

Phase 2 – Training Delivery (approx. 4 hours)

  • Travel to Client and deliver the approved presentation on-site, with a simultaneous remote option through Microsoft Teams.
  • Support recording of the session for people who cannot attend.
  • Lead a question-and-answer session after the presentation.
  • Provide electronic copies of the final training materials to the client.

Phase 3 – Post-Training Support (approx. 60 hours)

  • Answer follow-up questions from Client process owners and stakeholders.
  • Provide ongoing SME guidance on combination product regulatory requirements and quality system expectations.
  • Clarify process owner roles, responsibilities, and documentation expectations as questions come up during implementation.
  • Refine and update training content based on feedback received.
  • Lead follow-up remote sessions as requested to reinforce key quality and compliance considerations.

Training Content Expertise The SME must be able to speak with authority on the following topics:

  • Combination product regulatory overview, including 21 CFR Part 4
  • Regulatory requirements mapped across FDA, EMA, MHRA, Health Canada, PMDA, MFDS, TGA, and Medsafe
  • Integration of drug (cGMP) and device (QMSR / ISO 13485) quality system requirements

  • Key quality system elements that affect combination products
  • Documentation and data integrity expectations
  • Change control and risk management (e.g., ISO 14971)

Required

  • 10+ years of experience in quality assurance, regulatory compliance, or auditing in the pharmaceutical, medical device, or combination product industries.
  • Proven experience as a lead GxP auditor, including audit program development and execution.
  • Deep working knowledge of combination product regulations and drug and device quality system requirements.
  • Familiarity with global regulatory frameworks (FDA, EMA, MHRA, Health Canada, PMDA, MFDS, TGA, Medsafe).
  • Demonstrated experience developing and delivering training to technical and cross-functional audiences.
  • Strong presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder communication skills.

Preferred

  • Advanced degree in a relevant discipline.
  • Professional certification such as ASQ CQA, CQE, or RAC.

title: Creative Lead
description:
We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. At Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, you’ll collaborate with passionate teams to reimagine our iconic brands and create experiences that spark joy, connection, and community through the magic of play. This is your chance to shape legendary play that lasts a lifetime.

At Wizards of the Coast, we connect people around the world through play and imagination. From our genre-defining games like Magic: The Gathering® and Dungeons & Dragons® to our growing multiverse, we continue to innovate and build new ways to foster friendship and connection. That’s where you come in!

We’re looking for a Creative Lead to join our Digital Ventures team, reporting to the Head of Franchise Development. You’ll guide the creative direction of a slate of video games based on Wizards IP, built with external developers across mobile and PC/console. The role covers a range of creative and management skills: strategy development, project leadership through external partners, incubation and prototyping.

Because this work spans several projects at once, it depends on relationships: earning the trust of partner studios and Wizards teams and leading with integrity on both sides. You’ll bring a clear point of view on the IP and the quality bar and share it in a way partners can build on.

This is a hybrid role requiring three days a week in our Renton, WA office, with occasional travel.

What You’ll Do:

  • Set and maintain the creative vision for each game, grounded in what players love about our brands, from early concept through launch.
  • Lead and manage projects through multidisciplinary partner teams across game design, narrative, UX, art and audio, with clear feedback, reviews, and approvals.
  • Advocate for quality by setting creative intent and world-class standards for each project.
  • Incubate and prototype new play experiences with our IP, and champion them inside Wizards, from early concepts and pitches through development.
  • Translate franchise direction into materials partners can build from, such as aspirational targets, kickoff guides, guardrails and franchise bibles.
  • Help develop strategy for Wizards IP in games, including which opportunities to pursue, which partners to build them with, and the frameworks Wizards uses to evaluate and support them.

What You’ll Bring:

  • 5+ years of director-level creative leadership (creative, design, UX, or a similar role) working with internal and external partners to ship titles on mobile or PC/console.
  • A developer’s understanding of how games are made, from design methodology to craft, and the hands-on design, narrative or art skills to contribute directly when a project needs it.
  • A track record of managing projects through external developers and building strong relationships with them, adapting your direction across studios, cultures, time zones, and matrixed organizations.
  • Sharp judgment on authenticity and quality, and the ability to explain them clearly to partners and leaders.
  • A working knowledge of game industry trends, market analysis, and emerging technology (including AI).
  • Experience turning existing IP into new game concepts and familiarity with Magic: The Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons, or both.
  • Comfort moving between blue-sky concepting, incubation and prototyping, strategy and execution.
  • A self-directed multi-tasker with strong organizational skills and a healthy relationship with feedback.

Nice to have:

  • Experience on the licensor or publisher side of a game partnership.
  • Experience with live-service games.

description:

description:
Pay Range: $19.19 per hour, plus uncapped commissions.

Remote Eligible: Hybrid

We offer a pay-for-performance compensation program including bonuses for all employees and a competitive benefits package. See for a high-level overview of our benefits package and bonus offerings.

General Purpose of the Position

The External Mortgage Loan Officer (MLO) is responsible for generating mortgage production through proactive outside sales while also assisting members and prospective members with their mortgage needs. The primary responsibility is to attract new business through referral relationships and community presence. External MLOs will develop strong partnerships with realtors, builders, and other referral sources to promote Credit Union of Colorado’s portfolio and secondary-market mortgage products. They will guide applicants through the mortgage process from initial consultation to closing, partnering with Mortgage Operations.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develop, strengthen, and maintain referral relationships with external partners such as realtors, builders, financial advisors, and community organizations to grow self-generated mortgage production.
  • Promote CUofCO’s portfolio and secondary-market mortgage products through regular field visits, networking, community engagement, and relationship management.
  • Develop, maintain, and deepen relationships with existing and new borrowers to drive referrals, repeat business, and overall production.
  • Represent CUofCO at community events and industry functions to increase brand visibility and business development opportunities.
  • Achieve minimum production requirements of $500,000 or 3 closed-end mortgage units per month after the first three (3) months of employment.
  • Act promptly and professionally
  • Conduct thorough, consultative interviews with members and potential members to understand financial needs and recommend appropriate mortgage solutions.
  • Evaluate and structure first mortgages to meet member needs and eligibility requirements.
  • Initiate and guide members through a complete and compliant mortgage application within the Loan Origination System (LOS), following established policies and procedures.
  • Obtain and analyze all documentation for completeness, accuracy, eligibility, and alignment with CUofCO’s quality standards.
  • Run initial automated underwriting and follow findings and/or company standards.
  • Ensure all required disclosures and re-disclosures are issued accurately and within regulatory timelines.
  • Maintain detailed knowledge of agency guidelines, investor requirements, and CUofCO loan programs and procedures.
  • Adhere to all applicable regulations including TRID, HMDA, RESPA, Reg Z, Reg B, ECOA, SAFE Act, and CUofCO lending policies.
  • Document all communication with members, partners, and internal teams in the LOS and/or CRM according to policy.
  • Maintain data integrity, member confidentiality, and compliance with all state, federal, and agency requirements.
  • Communicate proactively and consistently with all parties involved in the loan process to maintain transparency and support timely closings.
  • Participate in weekly file review sessions with processing to identify and resolve issues early.
  • Provide support and collaboration to fellow MLOs and operational partners as needed.
  • Complete weekly and monthly production reports and other required documentation as determined by the department.
  • Maintain all required federal and state licenses and complete ongoing education as required by company, state, federal, and investor guidelines.
  • Stay current on mortgage industry trends, product updates, system enhancements, and regulatory changes.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or general education degree (GED). Minimum two years mortgage lending experience required. Existing referral network of realtors, builders, and community partners in the local market preferred.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Proven track record of self-generated production and maintaining strong referral partner relationships.
  • Strong knowledge of mortgage products, agency guidelines (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac), disclosures, TRID, and general regulatory requirements.
  • Experience working in a Loan Origination System (LOS) and CRM-type platform.
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for external sales activities required.
  • Knowledge of portfolio lending, construction and renovation loans, or other specialty products preferred.
  • Bilingual (Spanish/English or other language) helpful but not required.
  • Strong consultative selling skills with the ability to identify member needs and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Comfortable conducting outside sales activities including partner visits, open houses, community events, and presentations.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Ability to interact well with others in a positive manner
  • Proficiency in understanding AUS findings (DU/LPA) and structuring mortgage loans.
  • Ability to review financial statements, tax returns, income documentation, and credit reports.
  • Solid computer skills with the ability to learn new systems, tools, and processes quickly.
  • HP or Financial Calculator
  • Deep understanding of mortgage regulations including TRID, HMDA, RESPA, ECOA, Reg B, Reg Z, and SAFE Act standards.
  • Strong attention to detail with a focus on accuracy, data integrity, and quality documentation.
  • Ability to manage complex files while maintaining compliance and service standards.
  • Detail oriented with strong organizational and time management skills
  • Must maintain high level of confidentiality.
  • Ability to influence timelines, expectations, and proactively negotiate within department
  • Highly self-driven with the ability to work independently in an outside-sales environment.
  • Strong sense of ownership for production goals, lead follow-up, and personal performance.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is typically required to sit for long periods. The employee continually is required to talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, stoop and reach with hands and arms. The employee will occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. Vitu provides innovative, cutting-edge services to the motor vehicle industry. Our namesake solution manages titling and registration transactions in all 50 states and across multiple locations — all on one platform. With the mission of expanding and automating Vehicle-to-Government (V2Gov) transactions, the Vitu platform is reimagining how drivers, businesses and governments interact with vehicles. title: Senior Data Context Engineer
description:

Position Summary

We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Data Context Engineer to design, build, and manage the enterprise data foundation that powers Artificial Intelligence (AI), analytics, and cloud-based business applications. This role is responsible for ensuring enterprise data is accurate, secure, governed, and contextually enriched to support AI solutions, business intelligence, and data-driven decision-making.

The Data Context Engineer Lead will collaborate with business stakeholders, application owners, cloud engineers, data engineers, and AI teams to integrate data from enterprise SaaS applications, AWS services, and on-premises systems into a trusted, scalable, and secure data ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and maintain enterprise data context models that improve AI, analytics, and business reporting.
  • Integrate data from enterprise SaaS applications into AWS data platforms.
  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable data ingestion, transformation, and integration pipelines using AWS services.
  • Manage enterprise data stored in Amazon S3 as the organization's centralized data lake.
  • Develop and optimize datasets for Amazon QuickSight dashboards, analytics, and executive reporting.
  • Support AI initiatives by preparing structured and unstructured data for Amazon Bedrock, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and Large Language Models (LLMs).
  • Design and maintain vector databases and semantic search capabilities to improve AI response accuracy.
  • Build metadata, lineage, business glossaries, taxonomies, and enterprise data catalogs.
  • Implement data quality controls, validation processes, and continuous monitoring to ensure data integrity.
  • Define and maintain data lineage, ownership, and governance policies across enterprise systems.
  • Collaborate with application owners to onboard new SaaS applications into the enterprise data platform.
  • Develop and maintain APIs and integration services for secure data exchange between cloud and on-premises systems.
  • Optimize cloud storage strategies, lifecycle policies, and data organization within Amazon S3.
  • Partner with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Digital Strategy, Security, Infrastructure, and Business Intelligence teams to deliver trusted enterprise data.
  • Support the implementation of enterprise AI solutions using Amazon Bedrock and other AWS AI services.
  • Ensure compliance with enterprise security policies and regulatory frameworks, including ISO 27001, CMMC, GDPR, and applicable data governance standards.
  • Create technical documentation, architecture diagrams, data dictionaries, and operational procedures.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, Cloud Computing, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in data engineering, cloud data platforms, business intelligence, or enterprise data management.
  • Experience working with AWS cloud services.
  • Strong SQL and Python programming skills.
  • Experience integrating enterprise SaaS applications using APIs and cloud-native integration services.
  • Strong understanding of relational databases, data lakes, and ETL/ELT methodologies.
  • Experience with metadata management, data governance, and data quality practices.
  • Knowledge of REST APIs, JSON, and data integration technologies.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred AWS Experience

  • Experience with several of the following is highly desirable:
  • Atlan Data Catalog, Amazon S3, Amazon QuickSight, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Glue, AWS Lambda, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation, AWS IAM, AWS Step Functions, Amazon API Gateway, AWS AppFlow, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon OpenSearch Service, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudWatch, and other related AWS services.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Experience with vector databases and semantic search.
  • Experience with LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar AI frameworks.
  • Experience with enterprise data catalog solutions such as Microsoft Purview, Collibra, or Alation.

  • Understanding of cybersecurity and enterprise compliance requirements.
