title: Field Education Lead, BSW
description:
Cape Breton University (CBU) invites applications for a Full-Time Continuing, Field Education Lead in the Department of Social Work, School of Arts and Social Sciences.

Program Details
CBU’s BSW program is grounded in critical, anti-oppressive, and decolonizing approaches to social work education, with a strong emphasis on:

Advancing awareness and meaningful integration of Indigenous worldviews, Ways of Knowing, and Two-Eyed Seeing in practice.
Advancing Community-based and relational practice
Practice readiness and field education as the signature pedagogy
Advancing Social justice and ethical responsibility
Serving and including rural and underserved communities

The program is situated in Unama’ki (Cape Breton Island), part of Mi’kma’ki, the ancestral and unceded territory of the Mi’kmaq people, and it maintains close relationships with community organizations, service providers, and Indigenous partners.
Position Responsibilities
Reporting to and working with the Program Director, the Field Education Lead creates, facilitates, and assesses field practicum placements for social work students. Responsibilities include:

Lead the management, administration, educational development, and evaluation of BSW field education, ensuring alignment with CASWE standards, Core Learning Objectives, institutional policies, and program outcomes.
Maintain and oversee field education policies, procedures, documentation, learning contracts, evaluation processes, and related materials.
Recruit, assess, approve, develop, support, and retain practicum agencies and qualified field supervisors, and assess placement capacity for Field Practicum I and II.
Coordinate student placement processes, including meeting with students, assessing placement fit, managing placement decisions, and communicating with students, agencies, supervisors, and the Field Practice Educator.
Support placement managers and field supervisors regarding practicum expectations, supervision, student learning, policies, documentation, and evaluation responsibilities.
Ensure required student screening and placement documentation is completed and collaborate with the Field Practice Educator to address concerns related to student performance, conduct, attendance, supervision, safety, learning opportunities, or placement suitability.
Build and maintain community partnerships with social workers and practicum settings and identify opportunities and trends to strengthen field education.
Support professional development, research, collaborative initiatives, and university service related to the BSW program and community partnerships.

Qualifications of this role are:

Master of Social Work Degree (MSW);
A minimum of five years of practice experience in the field of social work;
Understanding of social services, practice and placement requirements and standards, and current issues and trends in social work;
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of social work education and practice, including, but not limited to, social justice, equity, diversity, inclusion, and decolonization;
Understanding of social work education and practice in the context of rural, indigenous, and marginal communities at the micro, mezzo, and macro levels;
Ability to work independently and as a team member, including the ability to develop interpersonal, collegial, and relationship-building skills suited to field education, social work education, university, and professional contexts;
Flexibility with hours of work based on program operation needs (e.g., special events in the evening, early morning preparation for daytime special events, etc.);
Ability to multitask priorities and responsibilities.

Applications for the successful candidate will include:

a cover letter describing the expertise of the applicant
a complete resume (or CV)
A list of least three references.

All required documents must be uploaded to "Additional Documents" with correct titles for each required document. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents.

Applications must be received by 11:00PM on October 27th, 2026.

Care Team Assistant - Pediatrics (Job Overview)

Schedule: 8AM-5PM

As a Pediatrics Care Team Assistant (CTA), you will be a trusted point of contact and an important informational resource for patients, families and caregivers, the call center, the care team, and community resources. Your compassionate support helps patients navigate their care while enabling providers and clinical team members to deliver high-quality, evidence-based care in accordance with Patient Centered Medical Home (PCMH) requirements.

You will bring together clinical coordination, patient communication, and clerical expertise to help care stay connected and accessible. From supporting phone calls and lab results to assisting with medication management, referrals, pre-appointment planning, and forms, your work will make a meaningful difference in the healthcare experience of the community we serve.

Why this role matters

  • Serve as a welcoming and dependable resource for patients, families, caregivers, providers, and community partners.
  • Help identify medically vulnerable patients who may need additional services, monitoring, or referrals.
  • Support quality and compassionate care through effective coordination, timely communication, and accurate documentation.
  • Collaborate closely with providers, nursing teams, referral staff, front-desk colleagues, and community resources.
  • Contribute to a safe, respectful, and patient-centered clinic environment.
  • Build valuable experience across care coordination, clinical workflows, patient support, and the broader healthcare ecosystem.

If you bring empathy, organization, sound judgment, and a passion for helping people access meaningful care, this is an opportunity to join our family and make a difference every day.

Key Responsibilities

  • Patient Communication: Work with onsite nursing or use protocol-based triage parameters to address patient calls forwarded by the call center and/or front desk.
  • Route clinical inquiries requiring provider review to the responsible provider as a phone note document in the electronic health record system (EHRS).
  • Return patient calls as directed by the provider.
  • Place phone calls or create template-based letters, as directed by the provider, regarding results such as lab results, and deliver them to patients in a timely manner.
  • At the provider’s direction, contact medically vulnerable patients after an office visit for an acute medical problem or patients designated as chronically ill/unstable and in need of ongoing monitoring.
  • Pre-Visit Planning: Review the patient schedule daily to promote completion of pre-visit preparations before each patient visit.
  • Confirm that lab and imaging results, consultation reports, care transition details, and information related to major changes in the patient’s health status are available in the patient record.
  • When information is not present in the EHRS, contact patients, consultants, imaging centers, and/or hospitals to gather it.
  • Report barriers to care to the provider.
  • Assist in arranging interpretation services.
  • Assist with and participate in daily huddles.
  • Care Coordination: Assist with transitions of care, including obtaining hospital and newborn discharge records and specialty notes.
  • Manage and maintain the site’s Care Coordination Desktop.
  • Assist patients with entry to and access of ancillary support services as needed, including prescription assistance, patient education, and social work.
  • Medication Management: Assist with medication refills at the direction of and as instructed by provider(s).
  • Assist with medication prior authorizations as needed.
  • Forms: Initiate completion of forms for provider review and final signature, including disability forms, home health orders, durable medical equipment and supply requests, disease status letters, FMLA paperwork, and other paperwork directed by the provider.
  • Communicate with the provider when urgent requests require prompt attention.
  • Referrals: Assist Referral Coordination staff and onsite scanners with completing referrals and including relevant documents in the medical record.
  • Complete and deliver clinical summaries for consultants or other service providers to whom patients are referred, as directed by the provider or dictated by the service line.
  • Demonstrate respect and regard for the dignity of all patients, families, visitors, and fellow employees to ensure a professional, responsible, and courteous environment.
  • Promote effective working relationships and work effectively as part of a team to facilitate the achievement of goals and objectives.
  • Attend all required safety training programs and describe responsibilities related to general safety, department/service safety, and specific job-related hazards.
  • Attend all required safety education programs.
  • Operate assigned equipment and perform all procedures safely as instructed.
  • Maintain the work area and equipment in the condition required by LCHS standards.
  • Demonstrate proper body mechanics in all functions.
  • Check the patient’s environment and equipment to ensure safety.
  • Report safety concerns promptly to appropriate personnel.
  • Follow LCHS exposure control plans for bloodborne and airborne pathogens.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of techniques, procedures, and correct use of protective barrier equipment, including Universal Precautions.
  • Assure a safe environment by instituting appropriate control measures.
  • Attend annual education programs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High-school level education or equivalency
  • Medical Assistant Certification or its equivalent, or at least 2 years clinical experience in an inpatient or outpatient setting
  • Must maintain BLS /CPR

Required Years of Experience

  • At least 2 years of experience in an ambulatory clinical setting preferred
  • Medical Assistant Certification or its equivalent, or at least 2 years clinical experience in an inpatient or outpatient setting

Required Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities

  • Demonstrated competency with an EHRS system
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Excellent customer service skills.
  • Ability to multi task in a fast paced environment.
  • Above average organizational skills.
  • Strong typing and computer skills.
  • This job requires access to confidential and sensitive information, requiring ongoing discretion and secure information management
  • Must be able to manage multiple deadline and decision making responsibilities.

About Legacy Community Health

The largest Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) in Southeast Texas, Legacy Community Health has delivered affordable, high-quality care for nearly 40 years across 50+ clinics in Greater Houston and the Gulf Coast. Our mission — driving healthy change in our communities — guides everything we do, and it starts with our people.

Approachable & Collaborative — Leads with humility, values diverse perspectives, and builds trust through teamwork.

Driven & Committed — Takes initiative and goes the extra mile to improve patient outcomes and drive continuous improvement.

Thoughtful Communicators — Pairs clinical/technical skill with emotional intelligence, navigating complex situations with empathy and professionalism.

title: Tax Specialist I
description:
Who we are

Over 600 employees strong, Asure sees Human Capital Management (HCM) through the lens of entrepreneurs and executives with an owner’s mentality. We help businesses develop their “Human Capital” to get to the next level, stay compliant, and allocate their time, money and technology toward growth. Our HCM platform empowers more than 100,000 clients to build great teams and better manage their people while staying compliant in an ever-changing HR legislative landscape. Asure’s HCM offering includes Payroll & Tax, HR, and Time & Attendance software and HR Services ranging from online compliance tools to a fully outsourced HR department.


How you will contribute

The Tax Specialist I position is responsible for the compliant and accurate resolution of system, agency, and client issues regarding periodic, quarterly, and annual tax notices and requests from clients, internal staff and taxing authorities. Use the Asure tools for documentation and resolution of all tax issues and request. Reponses are required to be accurate and timely. Assists with compliant and timely filing of required quarterly and annual tax returns.

  • Responds to various agency notices inclusive of SUI returns, Missing coupons, missing returns or wage reports, incorrect rate notices, and zero coupon or return submissions.
  • Assists in client set up of new tax types/ agencies, proper and compliant receipt of authorizations and TPA assignments, and ID number updates.
  • Includes annual SUI rate update handling to ensure accurate UI payments for quarter end processing, frequency updates for timely withholding payments, and basic ID number updates/ resolution of ‘applied for’ situations.
  • Assists with notification and collection of quarter end adjustments.
  • Completes special projects and coordinates with Manager on progress.
  • Completes and files amended returns.
  • At year-end, acts as primary support to submit Social Security Number (SSN) updates to the Social Security Administration (SSA) via BSO when new W2s are requested to be provided.
  • Assists with monthly, quarterly, and annual payroll tax reporting within timely established deadlines.
  • Ensures that the appropriate documentation (for clients and agencies) in updated in Asure CRM tool.
  • Resolves tax notice issues and communicate instructions or updates to clients.


    Qualifications

    • Minimum 1 Year of payroll tax payment and/or filing experience.
    • Proficient attention to detail and organization skills.
    • Multi-state and multi-client local taxation experience preferred. Strong communication skills- written and verbal.
    • Strong interpersonal skills.

    • Ability to collaborate and work in a team environment, as well as work independently and make sound decisions.
    • Must be comfortable working in a performance-based and structured environment with demonstrating high ethical standards.
    • Strong computer skills including but not limited to Microsoft Office (Excel, Word), Outlook, Evolution Payroll software (preferred, but not required), or other payroll tax software experience.
    • Advanced excel and payroll software skills.
    • Minimum H.S. diploma/GED equivalent.
    • College degree preferred but not required.

    The base hourly range for this position is $30.00 - $33.00, based on relevant experience, skills, and industry knowledge.

    Our Values

title: Azure Data Engineer
description:
Functieomschrijving
Werk aan innovatieve data oplossingen met Azure, AI en Databricks in een hecht team bij ilionx te Zwolle. Technische diepgang, humor, kennissessies maar ook padel: hier bouw je én heb je plezier!

Jouw rol als Azure Data Engineer

Als Azure Data Engineer bij ilionx te Zwolle werk je aan het ontwerpen en bouwen van schaalbare, robuuste dataoplossingen in de Azure cloud. Je transformeert ruwe data naar waardevolle inzichten met moderne technologieën als Databricks, Microsoft Fabric en Snowflake. Daarbij ontwikkel je data pipelines met tools als PySpark, Python, DBT, SQL en Matillion en werk je aan het realiseren van data lakehouses en dataplatformen. Ook onderzoek je hoe innovatieve technologieën zoals generatieve AI van waarde kunnen zijn binnen onze data engineeringpraktijk.

Je draagt bij aan uiteenlopende projecten: van het migreren van on-premise omgevingen naar Azure tot het ontsluiten van bronsystemen in de zorg of het inrichten van AI-ready dataplatformen. Onze klanten bevinden zich onder andere in sectoren als zorg, overheid, finance, energie en onderwijs. Je werkt zelfstandig of in teamverband, afhankelijk van het project, en hebt veel invloed op de technische keuzes en de richting van je werk.

Naast klantopdrachten krijg je ook de kans om bij te dragen aan onze interne proposities, zoals het ilionx Dataplatform of ZorgControl. Binnen deze trajecten experimenteren we met nieuwe technieken en best practices, gericht op toekomstbestendige dataoplossingen.

Binnen ilionx bepaal je zelf hoe je je ontwikkelt: wil je je verdiepen in de keiharde techniek of doorgroeien richting architectuur? Of geef je liever je kennis door als interne trainer? Ook specialiseren in specifieke richtingen zoals Dataplatforms, Data Science of AI behoort tot de mogelijkheden. Jij kiest het pad, wij faciliteren het.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Een salarisrange tussen de €4.500,- en €6.500,- op 40 uur met bonus!
  • Een uitgebreide leaseregeling voor zowel auto als fiets
  • Een gevarieerd werkveld: extern, intern of een mix
  • Een flexibele werkomgeving en wij omarmen het hybride werken
  • Een flinke focus op de AI transitie, daar zijn wij volop mee bezig

Wat vragen wij van jou?

  • Een afgeronde HBO/WO diploma
  • Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring met BI en/of Data Engineering
  • Je ziet de kansen van AI en denkt vooruit
  • Kennis van en ervaring met: Python en Spark
  • Kennis van: Databricks, Fabric, Snowflake, Synapse
  • Kennis van dimensionaal datamodelleren en logical modelling
  • Kennis van de data architecture concepten Medallion en Mesh
  • Beheersing van de Nederlandse taal vloeiend in woord en geschrift

Deze eisen geven een richting aan het profiel dat wij zoeken voor deze functie. Voldoe jij niet aan alle eisen maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren.

Het team

Het multidisciplinaire team in Zwolle kent een hechte en open sfeer met veel vrijheid! Binnen het team combineren we verschillende expertises zoals data engineering, platform engineering, data analytics en specifiek front-end. Er is een goede balans tussen junior, medior en senior collega's, wat zorgt voor een omgeving waar je kunt leren en jezelf kunt blijven ontwikkelen.

We werken veel samen op kantoor in Zwolle, wat zorgt voor korte lijnen en een sterke teamdynamiek. Onze cultuur is no-nonsense en gericht op samenwerking! Initiatief wordt gewaardeerd, en successen vieren we samen. Tussen het werk door spelen we fanatieke FIFA potjes op de PS5 of zoeken we elkaar op voor een padelwedstrijd. Zo bouwen we niet alleen aan data-oplossingen, maar ook aan een team dat voor elkaar klaarstaat.

Zoek jij een nieuwe plek voor de komende jaren en wil je impact maken binnen een team dat samen wil winnen? Dan kun je als dataspecialist perfect je plek vinden binnen ons Data & AI team te Zwolle!

Met ruim 10+ kantoren zijn wij landelijk vertegenwoordigd en op die manier kunnen wij regionaal vanuit verschillende vestigingen écht het verschil maken. Sluit jij je aan bij één van onze ilionx datateams in jouw regio?

Lees hier praktijkervaringen van jouw toekomstige ilionx data collega's.

Wat krijg je er voor terug Contract voor onbepaalde tijd Goede pensioenregeling Goede arbeidsvoorwaarden Aantrekkelijke bonus Lease auto of mobiliteitsvergoeding Ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen Uitdagende werkomgeving Werk hybride, thuis of op kantoor Thuiswerkvergoeding Agenda vol evenementen en borrels Tijd voor ontspanning Flexibele feestdagen & 25 vakantiedagen Leasefietsregeling

title: Buyer - Industrial Equipment/Engineer-to-Order Manufacturing
description:
Buyer – Purchasing & Supply Chain | Engineer-to-Order ManufacturingKoch Finishing Systems | Caledonia, MI (5041 68th St SE, Caledonia, MI 49316)Full-time | Starting at $60,000/year
Koch Finishing Systems is hiring a Buyer to lead purchasing, procurement, strategic sourcing, and supplier management for our engineer-to-order (ETO) manufacturing operation. This is a strong fit for a purchasing or procurement professional who's comfortable reading engineering drawings, specs, and bills of material (BOMs), and who enjoys solving problems in a fast-paced, project-driven environment.
You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Project Management, Estimating, Manufacturing, Inventory, Quality, Shipping/Receiving, and Accounting to source the materials and components behind our custom-engineered industrial finishing systems — plating barrels, process tanks, structural frames, automated hoists, pumps, chemical dosing systems, filtration systems, rectifiers, heating coils, and custom plastic fabrications.
About Koch Finishing SystemsWe design and build custom industrial finishing equipment — from plating and anodizing systems to chemical processing lines — for manufacturers nationwide, partnering with customers from concept through installation.
What You Get

Starting pay of $60,000/year
Paid holidays, vacation, PTO, and EPTO
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Retirement plans
Tuition and fitness reimbursement
Hands-on exposure to custom industrial equipment projects alongside Engineering, Manufacturing, and Project teams

What You'll Do

Review purchase requisitions, engineering drawings, specs, and BOMs to confirm accuracy before placing orders
Source specialized industrial, plating, and finishing components — including titanium/zirconium heating coils, chemical-resistant pumps and valves, rectifiers, filtration systems, and custom plastic fabrications
Identify and qualify new suppliers and subcontractors; build strong, lasting vendor relationships
Request quotes, negotiate pricing, lead times, payment terms, and delivery requirements; issue accurate purchase orders
Keep materials, equipment, and subcontracted services on track to meet project schedules
Coordinate delivery logistics between job sites, fabrication facilities, and subcontractors, verifying destination, quantity, and timing
Track supplier performance (quality, cost, lead time, on-time delivery) and document results in the ERP system
Partner with Engineering and Estimating to onboard new suppliers, including credit applications and tax-exemption documentation
Manage surplus and obsolete inventory alongside the Inventory Coordinator
Maintain stock levels for standard parts while managing project-specific buyouts
Resolve pricing, fulfillment, and invoice discrepancies with Shipping/Receiving, Engineering, and Accounting
Drive non-conforming material (NCR) resolution, RMAs, and supplier corrective actions with Quality Control
Contribute to cross-functional purchasing and supply chain process improvements

What You Bring

Associate degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain, Purchasing, or related field — or equivalent experience
2+ years of purchasing/procurement experience, including sourcing major equipment or industrial components
Ability to read and interpret technical specs, engineering drawings, and BOMs
Proficiency in Microsoft Office; ERP/MRP/purchasing system experience a plus
Strong negotiation, supplier management, and problem-solving skills
Ability to juggle multiple projects, suppliers, and deadlines without losing accuracy

Nice to Have

Background in metal finishing, electroplating, anodizing, industrial chemical handling, or wastewater treatment equipment
Strategic sourcing or supplier development experience
Familiarity with corrosion-resistant materials (polypropylene, PVC/CPVC, PVDF, titanium, 316 stainless steel, steel, copper)

Occasional travel to other Koch locations may be required (details shared during the interview).

title: Junior Route Setter
description:
Job Summary
As a Routesetter with Movement, you’ll be joining a collaborative, innovative, and passionate team of setters to develop high-quality, safe, and engaging climbs for our community. This opportunity is for a creative and hard-working individual with some setting experience (2 years or less), either through Movement's Routesetting Apprenticeship Program or other setting environment. What you’ll be doing:

Prepare setting area (boundaries, fixed lines, etc.)

Strip wall sections to prepare for new routes/problems

Set high quality skeletons (first draft of a climb) on all types of terrain

Maintain tidy setting area throughout the day, and help clean the area at the end of the day

Adhere to and promote workplace safety expectations (Work at Height standards, etc.)

Forerunning (i.e. climbing)

Be open to feedback and willing to perform as directed

Work collaboratively with the setting team to complete off the wall tasks in the absence of the Head Routesetter

You’re reliably setting high quality skeletons, forerunning, and grading routes/problems effectively

You’re able to operate independently once guidance is provided

You consistently meet production quota for routes and boulders on all terrain types

What you’ll bring with you

You must be 18 years of age or older
Some experience on a route setting team, either through Movement's Routesetting Apprenticeship Program or other setting environment

Strong understanding of Work at Height standards and other workplace safety expectations

Strong desire to further explore the craft of routesetting

Ability to thrive in a team-oriented and collaborative environment

Solid work ethic and the ability to manage your own workflow

Attention to detail

The ability to communicate effectively – communication is your jam and you do well with constructive feedback

The ability to always follow and promote safe practices

Bonus points for:

Lead climbing proficiency

Ability to climb at least 5.11 and/or V5

This role is based in Golden, applicants will be assigned this primary location but may have opportunities to support other locations as agreed upon

This is a Full Time position

Starting pay at $22-24/hour, flexibility available based on experience

Benefits include free membership, in-gym discounts, guest visits, potential 401(k) eligibility, paid time off, health benefits

Internal candidates who apply should be in excellent standing with their current director/management team

New hires will complete a screening process

Scheduled shift times may vary from week to week or month to month

Applications will be accepted until 10/26/26

title: Staff Software Engineer, App Promotion
location: San Francisco, CA, US; Seattle, WA, US; Remote, CA, WA, US
description:

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

We are seeking a Staff Engineer to lead the App Promotion engineering team. In this role, you will own the engineering roadmap to take Pinterest’s App Install Optimization product from beta to GA, hardening the current alpha/beta experience, closing critical measurement gaps, and ensuring readiness across Ads Manager, backend services, and mobile clients. You will lay the groundwork for future optimizations (App Event Optimization, tROAS, and retargeting) by partnering with Ads Quality, ML, and Measurement teams to build scalable models, robust experimentation, and trustworthy reporting. You will manage a team of 5–6 full stack and mobile engineers, foster an inclusive and high-performing team culture, and work closely with cross-functional leaders across Ads, Measurement, and Product to align on strategy, tradeoffs, and execution.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the engineering team responsible for the App Promotion objective and App Install Optimization, owning delivery from beta through GA.
  • Partner with Product, Design, and PMM to define and refine the advertiser experience for App Promotion in Ads Manager, including campaign creation, targeting, optimization, and reporting.
  • Work with Ads Quality, ML, and infra teams to ensure robust serving, modeling, and experimentation for app promotion campaigns.
  • Collaborate with Measurement, Reporting, and Partner teams to close SKAN and MMP attribution gaps and ensure App Promotion reporting is accurate and trusted.
  • Establish and maintain strong engineering practices for App Promotion, including design reviews, experimentation standards, on-call, monitoring, and incident response.
  • Hire, coach, and develop a diverse team of engineers; foster a culture of inclusion, learning, and operational excellence.

What we’re looking for

  • Bachelor's or higher degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Several years of engineering management experience leading full stack and/or mobile teams shipping production systems.
  • Experience in performance, growth, or ads engineering, preferably with app install, app engagement, or lower-funnel objectives.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional projects involving Product, Data, Design, and other engineering teams.
  • Strong technical judgment and ability to dive deep into architecture, data quality, and measurement details when needed.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain strategy, tradeoffs, and technical decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Commitment to building inclusive teams and promoting a sense of belonging.

title: Shipping Clerk
description:
Aerospace Shipping Clerk

Location: Northern Kentucky
Pay: $20+/hour, based on experience
Employment Type: Full-Time
1st shift 40 hours a week with OT when needed

Position Overview

Superior Skilled Trades is partnered with a leading aerospace and advanced manufacturing company seeking an Aerospace Shipping Clerk to support shipping, receiving, inventory, and administrative operations within its warehouse and production facility.

The ideal candidate is organized, dependable, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This position requires basic computer skills, strong communication abilities, and the ability to safely handle and move materials.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare and maintain accurate records of orders and shipments.
  • Receive incoming materials, products, packages, and deliveries.
  • Inspect and process incoming shipments in accordance with company procedures.
  • Store, organize, and issue materials and supplies as needed.
  • Maintain accurate inventory records and assist with inventory control.
  • Keep stock and warehouse areas clean, organized, and orderly.
  • Distribute packages, letters, and materials throughout the facility as needed.
  • Operate warehouse equipment, including forklifts, safely and efficiently.
  • Assist with loading, unloading, securing, and moving materials.
  • Complete administrative and warehouse-related tasks as assigned.
  • Follow all company safety, quality, and operational procedures.

Required Qualifications

  • Basic computer skills and ability to accurately enter and maintain information.
  • Ability to operate warehouse equipment such as forklifts.
  • Ability to lift and move materials weighing 45–60 lbs. individually.
  • Ability to perform buddy lifts of materials weighing up to 120 lbs.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational and administrative abilities.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to multitask.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Dependable, punctual, and committed to maintaining a consistent work schedule.

Preferred Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Previous shipping, receiving, warehouse, inventory, or material-handling experience.
  • Previous manufacturing or aerospace industry experience.
  • Forklift certification or demonstrated experience operating a forklift.

Professional Attributes

  • Customer-focused and service-oriented.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Dependable and trustworthy with a strong work ethic.
  • Detail-oriented and organized.
  • Takes initiative and identifies opportunities for improvement.
  • Communicates effectively with coworkers, supervisors, vendors, and other contacts.
  • Works well as part of a team while also being comfortable working independently.
  • Maintains professionalism and integrity in all aspects of the position.

Physical Requirements

This is a very active position requiring employees to regularly:

  • Stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Bend, kneel, stoop, crouch, crawl, and climb.
  • Lift and move materials weighing 45–60 lbs. individually.
  • Perform buddy lifts of materials weighing up to 120 lbs.
  • Operate warehouse equipment and work around moving machinery.
  • Perform occasional outdoor receiving and loading activities.

Employees must also have the ability to perform tasks requiring close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

  • Manufacturing and fabrication shop environment with exposure to dirt, dust, and noise.
  • Potential exposure to hot and cold temperatures.
  • Exposure to solvents and electrical energy.
  • Work around machinery and moving equipment.
  • Occasional outdoor work receiving shipments or securing loads in various weather conditions.
  • Frequent collaboration with warehouse, production, and management teams.
  • Overtime may be required based on business demand and management discretion.

Benefits

  • Health, Dental & Vision: Comprehensive insurance with approximately 80% of costs covered by the company.
  • Disability & Life Insurance: Short- and long-term disability coverage and company-paid life insurance.
  • Supplemental Coverage: Critical illness and accident insurance options.
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for advancement within the organization and its broader family of companies.
  • Culture of Excellence: Join a team committed to quality, employee development, innovation, and sustainable manufacturing.

title: Associate Dir of Youth Residential Services
description:
The Guild utilizes the collaborative efforts of leading professionals, best-practice approaches, tailored curricula and unmatched care to treat the individuals we serve.

The Associate Director of Youth Residential Services is responsible for the administrative, programmatic, and operational aspects of assigned residential group homes. The Associate Director ensures the completion of activities related to service coordination, staff supervision and evaluation, IEP program development and implementation, reporting and monitoring, oversight of all operational systems within and connected to the assigned cluster of group homes. The Associate Director ensures that all residents are afforded healthy and safe residential environments in which there are ample opportunities to experience community activities, develop relationships, make decisions, learn new skills, and be treated with dignity.

Primary Job Responsibilities:

  • Supervise residential managers within cluster.
  • Collaborate with Human Resources for all residential hiring and promotions within cluster.
  • Ensure the development and implementation of student’s IEP and residential portion of Caring Together treatment plans within cluster residences.
  • Ensure the appropriate staffing, staffing ratios and use of overtime in all youth homes within cluster including developing and maintaining master staffing schedules.

  • Ensure the development and implementation of daily and weekly master activity and programming schedules for all youth residences in cluster.

  • Ensure payroll is completed for each home in cluster.
  • Serve as part of the administrative on-call team.
  • Oversee the preparation of cluster homes for residential inspections in conjunction with facilities and residential manager.
  • Provide orientation and training to new residential managers within cluster.
  • Provide on-call supervision and emergency response to Guild residences.
  • Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree preferred
  • Six years of experience (4 years in a supervisory role) with individuals who have mental health diagnoses and/or developmental disabilities
  • Knowledge of Massachusetts regulatory standards is required with preferred experience in regulatory compliance with standards from Department of Early Education and Care (DEEC), Department of Children and Families (DCF), and Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE)
  • Excellent organization and time management skills
  • Reliable transportation to multiple residential locations in Massachusetts
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Ability to demonstrate supervisor and administrative skills
  • A valid driver's license

title: Kitchen (Edibles) Supervisor
description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Cresco Labs is one of the largest public, vertically integrated, multistate operators in the cannabis industry. Our portfolio of in-house cultivated and manufactured brands features some of the highest quality, most awarded and most popular cannabis products in America. With dozens of locations nationwide, our owned and operated Sunnyside® dispensaries provide a welcoming, positive, judgement-free place to shop for anyone at any point on their cannabis journey.

Founded in 2013, Cresco Labs’ mission is to normalize and professionalize cannabis through our passionate employees. As stewards of the cannabis industry, our teams are constantly focused on supporting the needs of our fellow colleagues, consumers, customers, and communities alike. With a focus on Social Equity and Educational Development, our SEEDTM initiative ensures that our company reflects the communities in which we serve, ensuring equal opportunity for all to have the knowledge and resources to work in and own businesses in cannabis.

At Cresco Labs, we aim to revolutionize and lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on quality and consistency of product, and to bring legitimacy to the industry with the highest level of integrity and professionalism.

If you’re interested in joining our mission, click the below links to join our team today!

MISSION STATEMENT

At Cresco, we aim to lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on regulatory compliance, product consistency, and customer satisfaction. Our operations bring legitimacy to the cannabis industry by acting with the highest level of integrity, strictly adhering to regulations, and promoting the clinical efficacy of cannabis. As Cresco grows, we will operate with the same level of professionalism and precision in each new market we move in to.

JOB SUMMARY

The Edibles Kitchen Supervisor reports to the Kitchen Manager and is responsible for production of Cresco Labs medically infused edible products. Manages a team of kitchen agents and leads to carry out day-to-day tasks including prepping, cleaning, cooking, and operating basic production machinery. Produce edibles in accordance with state regulations and standards set by Cresco Labs.

CORE JOB DUTIES

  • Work with Kitchen Manager to set weekly and monthly production schedules.
  • Lead and motivate the second shift team to meet production goals, maintain efficiency, and ensure product quality.
  • Manage kitchen agents with daily production of cannabis-infused products using commercial machinery.
  • Personnel management to include hiring, discipline, training. etc...
  • Provide end-of-shift reports to the Kitchen Manager/first shift supervisor, including updates on production output, challenges encountered, and equipment performance.
  • Understand and execute batch calculations per Cresco Edibles manufacturing formulas.
  • Maintain production logs, lab test results and sanitation logs.
  • Organize and inventory ingredients and other kitchen production supplies at the facility.
  • Works with Materials Manager/Supervisor to place ingredient orders with approved vendors, log and date each shipment.
  • Packaging finished goods, producing compliance labels, and finalizing Metrc movements.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of state and county health department requirements for Kitchen Production Facilities. Handle preparation for periodic inspections.
  • Maintain a production area in accordance with Cresco GMP, GDP, and Safety/Quality standards.
  • Ensure personal hygiene is acceptable under standards set by Cresco Labs before performing any production activities by washing hands, wearing a hair net, changing clothes, etc.
  • Complete the sanitation of production equipment and tools including workspace, production and packaging equipment, cookware and appliances.
  • Flexibility to adjust schedule based on production demands, including occasional overtime or weekend shifts.
  • Operate with a high degree of autonomy during second shift hours while ensuring seamless handoffs with other teams.
  • All other job duties assigned.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND SKILLS

  • Experience leading, managing, coaching, and developing direct reports and teams.
  • 2+ years’ experience in food or confectionary processing/manufacturing preferred.
  • Experience in a field and/or operation that adheres to strict health and safety policies and procedures, preferably a regulated field producing products for human consumption.
  • Demonstrates a clear understanding of recipes, food production and kitchen sanitation.
  • Demonstrates expert knowledge of SOPs, GFSI, GMP, GDP and other company policies
  • Strong and effective task-management skills and ability to multi-task.
  • ServSafe preferred
  • Attention to detail – ability to monitor basic kitchen production in processes, organize and maintain production logs and ingredient lot numbers.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, changing and challenging environment.
  • Experience with Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, and Metrc/Canix a plus.
  • Requires work around plant material, which could include exposure to plant pollen and/or dust.
  • Requires ability to sit, stand, and/or do repetitive actions with your hands for long periods of time.
  • Requires ability to lift up to 50 lbs to torso level.

Reporting a Scam:

Cresco Labs is aware of fictitious employment offers being circulated from various sources. Many of these schemes consist of an alleged offer of employment with Cresco Labs with the intention of gaining personal information, including payment and/or banking information. Be aware that fraudulent job offers and correspondence may appear legitimate: they may feature a Cresco Labs logo, they may appear to originate from an official-looking email address or web site, or they may be sent by individuals purporting to represent Cresco Labs or an entity which includes the word Cresco Labs in its name.

A Brief OverviewThe Plant Hygienist plays a critical role in ensuring that all hygiene-related processes, systems, equipment, and personnel adhere to the highest standards of efficacy, efficiency, and regulatory compliance. This position is responsible for overseeing cleaning protocols, sanitation procedures, environmental and critical equipment hygiene monitoring programs and employee training to maintain a safe and compliant manufacturing environment.What you will do

Provide training to applicable employees.

Support improvement initiatives through continuous improvement projects focused on optimizing cleaning recipes, 10sanitization recipes, and enhancing environmental responsibility.
Partner with cross-functional teams to investigate and resolve Out of Specification (OOS) microbiological issues, ensuring corrective actions align with quality standards.
Configure, maintain, and optimize Clean-in-Place (CIP) recipes within processing equipment to ensure consistency and effectiveness.
Serve as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for internal and external audits, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards. Provide guidance to hygienic design of equipment for product contact surfaces.
Responsible for site’s monitoring programs for critical utilities and environment. Perform quarterly trend review of purified water distribution system, compressed air and site environmental monitoring program. Prepares and executes the quality report.

1-3 years proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint – required; Microsoft Project – desired). (Preferred)

title: IT Support Engineer
description:

Okta (identity/SSO), Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs), Slack, Jira & Jira Service Management, Confluence, Zoom, Microsoft Entra ID/M365, Chrome, plus MDM for Mac and Windows fleets.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Spektrum supports apex purchasers (NATO, UN, EU, and National Government and Defence) and their Tier 1 supplier ecosystem with a wide range of specialist services. We provide our clients with professional services, specialised aerospace and defence sales, delivery, and operational subject matter expertise. We are looking for personnel to join our team and support key client projects.

Who we are supporting

The NATO Communication and Information Agency (NCIA) is responsible for providing secure and effective communications and information technology (IT) services to NATO's member countries and its partners. The agency was established in 2012 and is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium.

The NCIA provides a wide range of services, including:

  • Cyber Security: The NCIA provides advanced cybersecurity solutions to protect NATO's communication networks and information systems against cyber threats.
  • Command and Control Systems: The NCIA develops and maintains the systems used by NATO's military commanders to plan and execute operations.
  • Satellite Communications: The NCIA provides satellite communications services to enable secure and reliable communications between NATO forces.
  • Electronic Warfare: The NCIA provides electronic warfare services to support NATO's mission to detect, deny, and defeat threats to its communication networks.
  • Information Management: The NCIA manages NATO's information technology infrastructure, including its databases, applications, and servers.

Overall, the NCIA plays a critical role in ensuring the security and effectiveness of NATO's communication and information technology capabilities.

The program

Assistance and Advisory Service (AAS)

The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCI Agency) is NATO’s principal C3 capability deliverer and CIS service provider. It provides, maintains and defends the NATO enterprise-wide information technology infrastructure to enable Allies to consult together under Article IV, and, when required, stand together in the face of attack under Article V.

To provide these critical services, in the modern evolving dynamic environment the NCI Agency needs to build and maintain high performance-engaged workforce. The NCI Agency workforce strategically consists of three major categorise's: NATO International Civilians (NIC)'s, Military (Mil), and Interim Workforce Consultants (IWC)'s. The IWCs are a critical part of the overall NCI Agency workforce and make up approximately 15 percent of the total workforce.

Role ID – C005429

Role Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direction of Service Delivery Manager of Service Oriented Architecture (SOA), the DevOps Engineer will focus on streamlining application delivery and bridging the gap between development and infrastructure:

  • Administer container orchestration platforms using SUSE Rancher Prime and collaborate directly with development teams to seamlessly onboard applications into production environments.
  • Design, build, and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines to fully automate application testing, integration, and delivery.
  • Provision and manage hybrid infrastructure across on-premises environments and the cloud utilizing Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
  • Establish and maintain comprehensive monitoring, logging, and alerting systems to ensure platform reliability and performance.
  • Embed security best practices and compliance controls directly into the deployment pipelines and infrastructure configurations.
  • Troubleshoot complex integration and deployment issues, acting as a technical bridge across agile delivery teams.

Essential Skills, Experience and Certifications

At least 5 years of hands-on experience in DevOps or automated platform management, including:

  • Solid experience deploying and administering container workloads and orchestration platforms, including Kubernetes, Rancher, RKE2 and Docker.
  • Strong proficiency in CI/CD, GitOps, pipeline automation, and version control using enterprise tools like GitLab, ArgoCD or Jenkins.
  • Proven expertise in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles, provisioning hybrid resources with Terraform, and automating system configurations with Ansible.
  • Practical knowledge of managing hybrid infrastructure across enterprise virtualization environments (VMware) and major cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
  • Proficiency in scripting languages like Bash or Python for automating routine operational tasks and tool integrations.
  • Experience deploying and utilizing observability and industrystandard monitoring stacks like Prometheus, Grafana and ELK.
  • Excellent analytical problem-solving capabilities with a strong track record of delivering cross-functional work in fast-moving Agile environments.

Working Location

  • Braine l’Alleud, Belgium

Working Policy

  • On-site

Travel

  • Some travel to other NATO sites may be required

Security Clearance

  • Valid National or NATO Secret personal security clearance

title: CFWS Social Service Specialist 2-3 In Training (SSS3) - Richland
description:
Description


Our vision is to ensure that “All Washington's children and youth grow up safe and healthy, thriving physically, emotionally, and educationally, nurtured by family and community".

Job Title: CFWS Social Service Specialist 2-3 In Training (SSS3)

Location: Richland, WA

Closes: 10/13/26

Salary: $66,072 - $93,288 Annually. This position may receive 10% assignment pay when the incumbent reaches the goal class of Social Service Specialist 3. This is in addition to the regular base salary; the required duties include performing visits in unregulated environments, such as private residences, to conduct investigations for allegations of abuse and/or neglect to assess the safety of vulnerable children.


Are you looking for a rewarding job with a great team? We have the perfect opportunity for you! We're looking for a proactive Child and Family Welfare Services (CFWS) Social Service Specialist (SSS3) to join our amazing Richland team. This full-time position with a flexible schedule is the perfect way to serve our community. A hybrid work environment promotes a great balance between working from home and the office. We have a supportive and dynamic team atmosphere helping you feel included and successful. There are many opportunities for growth and professional development, making this next work opportunity the perfect career move for you!

Click here to learn more about DCYF.

The Opportunity:
 In this role, you will assess complex family situations, interview children and parents, evaluate child safety, develop plans to protect children in their homes, and offer services to children and families. This position will provide Child and Family Welfare services to children and families primarily in north Pacific County.

Some of what you'll do:

  • Conduct investigations into allegations of child abuse, abandonment, or neglect to determine if children are safe with their families and caregivers.
  • Provide advanced-level specialized case management in complex cases involving issues such as substance abuse, mental health, and domestic violence. Implement culturally-relevant, ADA-sensitive, and individualized service plans which are goal-directed, have specific behavioral objectives, and are time-limited.
  • Interview children, family members, caregivers, and collateral sources to gather information necessary to assess child safety and determine service needs.
  • Provide comprehensive assessments of needs for children and families while working with a diverse population, which may include Native American families.
  • Assess the need for out-of-home placement and work with the family to find the most appropriate placement.
  • Provide case management services to facilitate out-of-home placements and review the need for continued out-of-home care.
  • Prepare and document cases for court proceedings.
  • Prepare and present written and oral testimony for court proceedings.
  • Utilize FAMLINK to document case activities and maintain case records.

Salary Ranges:

The goal class of this position is a Social Service Specialist 3. We will also consider candidates at the Social Service Specialist 2 level, with a training plan to advance to the goal class. The Hiring Manager will evaluate the education and experience of each candidate for one of the levels mentioned below.

  • Social Service Specialist 2: Range 57 ($66,072– $88,788)
  • Social Service Specialist 3: Range 59 ($69,348- $93,288)


What we are looking for at each level:
Social Service Specialist 2:

  • Five (5) years of paid social service experience AND 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Service discipline.

OR

  • Bachelor’s degree in social services, human services, behavioral sciences, or any degree which includes 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Service discipline AND one (1) year of paid social service experience.

OR

  • A Master's degree in social services, human services, behavioral sciences, or Master’s degree which includes 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Services discipline AND completed practicum.

OR

  • One (1) year of experience as a Social Service Specialist 1.

Social Service Specialist 3:

  • Six (6) years of paid social service experience* AND 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Service discipline.

OR

  • Bachelor’s degree in social services, human services, behavioral sciences, or any degree that includes 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Service discipline AND Two (2) years of paid social service experience*.

OR

  • Master's degree in social services, human services, behavioral sciences, or any degree which includes 30 semester or 45 quarter credits in a Social Service discipline AND One (1) year of paid social service experience*.

OR

  • One (1) year of experience as a Social Service Specialist 2
AND
  • The ability to take action to learn and grow.
  • The ability to take action to meet the needs of others.

*Paid Social Service experience must include at least one year of assessing risk and safety to children and providing direct family-centered practice services.



Preferred/Desired Qualifications:

  • Prior public child welfare experience.
  • Knowledge of social casework principles and practices, risk assessment and decision-making, interviewing techniques, solution-based casework, principles of child development, applicable Federal and State laws, and community resources.
  • Experience assessing risk and safety concerning child abuse and neglect or developing safety or service plans with families.
  • Familiarity with community resources and the local community.
  • Ability to organize information to meet FAMLINK documentation requirements.

Worker Core Training (WCT):

As a Social Service Specialist, you are required to successfully complete a mandatory 9.5-week Worker Core Training (WCT). This training provides the foundational knowledge and skills needed to perform core job functions, including assessing risk and safety, supporting child well-being, gathering information, and conducting case and permanency planning. During the training, you will have opportunities to practice these skills through classroom activities, simulation exercises, and debriefs. Upon hire, you will be assigned to the nearest available training cohort. The training includes four (4) weeks at our Seattle training site (scheduled for Weeks 2, 4, 6, and 8). For those eligible for travel from their assigned duty location, DCYF covers hotel accommodations and per diem costs.

The WCT curriculum is designed to prepare Social Service Specialists for the responsibilities of the role, including:

  • Understanding the child welfare system
  • Familiarity with the Revised Code of Washington (RCW) related to child welfare
  • Policies, procedures, and best practices
  • Assessing child safety through environmental observation, interviews with children and caregivers, and collateral contacts
  • Collecting records and collaborating with community partners, including medical providers, law enforcement, and chemical dependency services
  • Completing assessments and documenting case notes
  • Writing dependency petitions and court reports
  • Preparing for and testifying in court


How do I apply?
Complete your applicant profile and attach the following:

  • Transcripts (Unofficial transcripts are acceptable for application submission)
  • Cover Letter
  • Current resume detailing experience and education.

title: Metrology Lab Specialist
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

We are looking for a highly skilled Metrology Specialist to program, optimize, and lead complex inspections across a wide variety of products that we design and develop. In this role you will write, debug, and optimize inspection programs across contact and non-contact systems, troubleshoot the most difficult measurement problems, and help shape how the lab does its work. As the Metrology lab grows, you will work across a range of equipment — Portable CMM, CNC/fixed CMM, CT scanner, laser tracker, and optical systems from manufacturers such as Hexagon, Zeiss, Keyence, and LK Metrology — supporting incoming quality inspections, internally manufactured components, quality investigations, and root cause analysis, while mentoring other members of the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Program and operate metrology equipment across contact and non-contact systems to validate that parts meet requirements.
  • Write, debug, and optimize inspection programs to improve accuracy, repeatability, and cycle time.
  • Troubleshoot complex measurement issues — determining why an inspection is failing or producing inconsistent results — and resolve process-level problems.
  • Design, build, and validate holding fixtures used on the CMMs.
  • Work closely with the Quality Engineering team to support problem-solving, root cause analysis, and product design.
  • Define best-practice inspection and reporting strategies with cross-functional teams.
  • Maintain and improve lab equipment and processes (calibration, cleanliness, best practices), reducing downtime and ensuring data reliability.
  • Train and mentor other metrology team members and serve as the go-to resource for difficult measurement problems.
  • Help ensure compliance with industry standards (e.g., AS9100, ISO 17025).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of metrology experience, including programming CMMs.
  • Hands-on experience with at least three different types of metrology equipment (CNC CMM, portable CMM, laser tracker, large-volume or automated 3D scanners, optical comparator, etc.).
  • Proficiency with CMM software; Calypso or Polyworks preferred (PC-DMIS, Verisurf, MCosmos, or equivalent acceptable with the ability to learn PolyWorks and Calypso quickly).
  • Excellent understanding of GD&T (ASME Y14.5).
  • Experience designing and building holding fixtures for CMMs.
  • Proficiency with precision measuring equipment (micrometers, height gauges, and other hand tools).
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and excellent communication skills.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Associate’s degree or technical training.
  • Experience with advanced or specialized inspection methods, including NDT.
  • Experience with CT scanning and automated or large-volume 3D scanning.
  • Experience with PolyWorks|DataLoop or similar metrology data management platforms.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

About the role

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape and build the next generation of our network automation platforms.

Our challenge is one of scale, complexity and criticality. We operate a massive global network supporting PlayStation Network, spanning more than 40 interconnection locations and 20+ data centres worldwide. Operating infrastructure at this scale safely and efficiently requires us to move beyond specialist-driven workflows and individual automation tools toward reliable, declarative software platforms.

You will help make that transition. You will work on software that turns complex network and infrastructure operations into reliable, API-driven and increasingly self-service capabilities. This includes building control-plane services, declarative APIs and intent-based controllers that manage production infrastructure safely and consistently across our global footprint.

This is a Staff-level engineering role with significant technical influence. You will combine hands-on engineering with setting technical direction: defining architectures, solving complex cross-system and distributed-systems problems, writing designs, driving alignment with senior engineers and architects, and mentoring engineers across the team.

Your work will directly influence how one of the world's largest gaming networks is operated and automated, while establishing engineering patterns and platforms that can be reused across multiple network domains and services.

What you'll do

  • Provide technical leadership and architectural direction for network automation and infrastructure control platforms, treating the self-service network API as a product by working with users and partner teams to define outcomes, establish clear expectations for API behavior and reliability, align on team responsibilities, and ensure those commitments are met.
  • Use domain-driven design with network experts, software engineers and API consumers to establish shared language and bounded contexts, then turn those agreements into versioned, testable contracts.
  • Design and build APIs, services, controllers and reconciliation workflows that manage production infrastructure safely at scale.
  • Build on the Kubernetes API, including custom resources and control loops that continuously converge actual state toward declared intent.
  • Own the operational Kubernetes path: CRD rollout, RBAC and admission, controller health, Helm packaging, deployment drift and incident diagnosis.
  • Design distributed workflows that operate correctly under eventual consistency, at-least-once delivery, concurrent writes and partial failure, with idempotency and safe recovery as fundamental properties.
  • Design stable APIs, schemas and data models used across team boundaries, including versioning and backwards compatibility.
  • Develop patterns for multi-tenant infrastructure platforms, including tenant isolation, authorization, policy enforcement and safe automation boundaries.
  • Establish strong approaches to testing, observability and change safety for software that changes live infrastructure.
  • Improve software delivery practices through automated CI gates, versioned artifacts, controlled promotion, and safe deployment and recovery strategies.
  • Lead complex migrations and modernization of existing automation, services and data models, evaluating when components should be evolved, replaced or rewritten, and ensuring safe coexistence, behavioral compatibility and retirement of legacy paths.
  • Drive technical alignment across software engineering, networking, operations and architecture teams; lead decisions within your area of accountability, contribute constructively to decisions owned by others, and make technology choices based on long-term company and product value.
  • Mentor engineers, lead technical and design reviews, and raise software engineering standards across the wider organization.

What we're looking for

Must have

  • Deep expertise in a backend language such as Python, Go, Rust or Java, including asynchronous concurrency, static typing, data modelling and validation, API development, packaging and tooling.
  • Strong experience building Kubernetes controllers or operators, including custom resources and reconciliation/control-loop patterns.
  • Strong experience building event-driven distributed systems, particularly eventual consistency, at-least-once delivery, idempotency, optimistic concurrency and partial-failure handling.
  • Experience designing and building self-service, multi-tenant platforms, including tenant isolation, policy and access control.
  • Strong API and schema design skills, including versioning and schema evolution for interfaces consumed by other teams and systems.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership across team boundaries, including driving architectural designs, building agreement among senior technical stakeholders and mentoring other engineers.
  • A track record of taking ambiguous, technically complex problems from architecture through to reliable production systems that manage large-scale infrastructure, such as networks, compute or cloud resources.

Nice to have

  • Networking fundamentals, particularly BGP, IP fabrics and VXLAN/EVPN/L3VPN.
  • Working knowledge of Go, sufficient to understand and contribute to adjacent services and controllers.
  • Experience designing testing and observability strategies for production infrastructure automation, including systems and backends that cannot be fully reproduced in CI.
  • Experience with graph databases, or with source-of-truth systems that model infrastructure and its relationships.

The impact

You will help establish the architecture and engineering practices behind a new generation of network automation, moving from individual scripts and specialist-driven workflows toward declarative, model-driven and reliable platforms.

At Staff level, your impact is expected to extend beyond the code you personally deliver. You will help shape the APIs and designs other teams build on, develop other engineers, and establish technical patterns that can be reused across multiple network domains and services.
