title: IMP Manufacturing Technician
description:
IMP Manufacturing Technician


Position Type: Full-time, Non-Exempt, Hourly

Reports to: IMP Superintendent/IMP Foreman

Supervisory Responsibility: None

Location: Fort Worth, TX

Company Summary

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.


Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.


Backed by deep engineering expertise and large-scale manufacturing capability, Stellar Energy helps customers deploy critical infrastructure faster and with confidence.

Summary Objective

To have experienced working knowledge of the Insulated Metal Panel installation, Assembly and the various terminologies, blueprint reading, measurements, take outs, job specifications, etc., to build an integrally complete erection system.

Essential Functions

  • Fluent in understanding job specification, blueprint reading, target point measurements, true /plumb /square checking, and any necessary torque requirements, for large industrial structural steel systems.
  • The ability to cut, prep, fit and tack small to large; IMP’s, Flashing, etc., from various material types through true-plumb-square; into weld ready status, using isometric and structural drawings, while adhering to specific fit tolerance requirements.
  • The ability to properly select, measure, hand dress, and cut with grinder, power saws, hand tools, etc., as necessary to prepare IMP process to be completed per job specific requirements.
  • Strong structural aptitude and problem solver who can understand and follow instruction.
  • Accountability for completion of daily work assignments while monitoring quality, safety, and health regulations.
  • Operate overhead cranes and or forklifts, while adhering to industry standard practices of safe rigging systems and techniques.
  • Safely and efficiently direct and monitor two or more helpers.
  • Documentation of all quality reporting methods employed per SEA Quality Standards.
  • Complies with all company policies, procedures, and safety requirements and is physically / medically qualified to wear required PPE per OSHA standards.
  • Responsibilities may require sedentary work, including but not limited to computer operation, video review, classroom or online training, job observations/inspections, and peer work review.
  • Prepares for ISO 9001 and other audits.


Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Competencies

  • Collaboration Skills
  • Reliable Attendance
  • Decision Making
  • Leadership
  • Communication Proficiency; Written and Verbal
  • Ethical Conduct
  • Problem Solving
  • Organizational Skills
  • Thoroughness
  • Time Management

Supervisory Responsibility
This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.

Work Location

This position will work out of our facilities in Jacksonville, FL or Fort Worth, TX. This position is not approved for telecommuting or working remotely.

Work Environment
This position operates out of a fabrication facility. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is sometimes exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. The employee is occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at construction job sites. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud.


Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or listen. The employee is frequently required to stand, walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must frequently lift or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work
This is a full-time position. The first shift days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

Second shift days and hours of work are Monday through Thursday, 3:00 p.m. to 1:30 a.m. Occasional weekend work may be required as job duties demand.

Travel
Travel is primarily not required except for local travel during the business day.

Required Education and Experience.

  • Basic math and language skills are required.
  • Grinding, welding, brazing, rigging, and cutting sheet metal.
  • 1 Year related experience or training

Preferred Education and Experience

  • 2 Years’ experience in Insulated Metal Panels (IMP).
  • Some vocational technical training is desired.

Work Authorization
Must be authorized to work in the USA.

Benefits Summary
We offer a competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance (multiple plan options; preventive care covered at 100% in-network)
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contributions
  • 401(k) with company match (100% match up to 3% + 50% match up to 6%)
  • Company-paid life insurance and AD&D coverage
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage options
  • Supplemental benefits including accident, critical illness, and hospital coverage
  • Wellness programs, including incentives up to $300 annually and a no-cost weight management program
  • Virtual healthcare options, including $0 virtual visits in many cases
  • Additional voluntary benefits including legal services and pet insurance
  • Competitive PTO plan for exempt and non-exempt employees

Stellar Energy Americas Inc. provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Stellar Energy Americas Inc. complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities.

Deliver practical training to leaders, project managers, business development professionals, and other contract and compliance stakeholders.

A degree or diploma in legal studies, paralegal studies, business administration, corporate governance, risk management, compliance, public administration, or a related discipline.
Five or more years of progressive experience in contract management, legal operations, legal administration, compliance, governance, risk management, procurement, or a related corporate function.
Demonstrated experience reviewing commercial agreements and translating contractual requirements into practical business actions.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex requirements in clear business language.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage detailed records, sensitive information, multiple stakeholders, and competing deadlines.

Assets

Professional education or a designation in compliance, governance, risk management, contract management, privacy, records management, or paralegal practice.
Experience with contract lifecycle management platforms, compliance systems, document repositories, or AI-enabled contract review tools.
Experience in a professional services, architecture, engineering, construction, consulting, or project-based organization.

What Success Looks Like

Business leaders receive clear, timely, and practical decision support.
External legal resources are engaged efficiently and supported with well-organized information.

Your Role and Authority

This role is hybrid, requiring you to report on-site to one of the following office locations a minimum of 2 days/week: San Francisco, Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Austin, Nashville, Detroit, Boston, or New York City.

Your Role

As the Technical Director, your role centers around being the on-site manager for major shows and events. You bring expertise in scenic, lighting, rigging, audio, and visual requirements, both in the pre-show and on-site phases. Beyond managing our event execution, you play a crucial role in determining the technical solutions for our shows, with a strong focus on developing and upholding GPJ production standards.

Collaborating closely with an Executive Producer and/or Producer, you take charge of on-site supervision for both union and non-union labor, while managing the technical production budgets and CAD Plans. Much of your time and energy is dedicated to owning and nurturing vendor execution of programs, and the RFQ process.

Your Impact

  • You are CAD Proficient in Vectorworks or AutoCAD
  • Rock star in Google Suites, with Advanced competency in Excel, Word and PowerPoint are also expected
  • You understand on-site methodology and best practices for live events of all kinds
  • Have the ability to read and interpret space plans
  • You can demonstrate you have worked on large-scale events and have a proven track record of managing $3mm+ budgets

Experience & Education

  • Minimum 15+ years direct production management and/or technical production experience.

Travel & Mobility

  • Ability to travel 40%

Your Competencies

Deliver-Produce with excellence, in all your areas you touch directly or indirectly, for the client, the project you are assigned, and the GPJ team.

Confidence-Know that you will succeed, when at times what is being suggested may not have been produced before. Have confidence that you have the team, data, tools and skills necessary to overcome obstacles. Working in close concert with strategy, creative, other production teams, and client teams to communicate all stages of the production process and get everyone to the end goal.

Communication-Technical or Production Team leader adept at identification, hiring and mentoring of skills and resources required to build teams that deliver robust solutions within a controlled project management environment. Strong communication skills with each member of the team (GPJ, Client and Partners) in sharing information, advising but being decisive as required to ensure success. Strong advocate for a safe environment for attendees and staff ensuring each project has all required certifications and documentation.

Curiosity-Desire to discover, explore, learn and expand knowledge of digital, technical, theatrical and media elements to bring brands to life in the most effective way. Live production is one of the most powerful forms of communication in experience marketing and your role is to partner with the strategy, creative and account teams in bringing the best ideas forward and put the strategy into action.

Salary Range: $125k - $140k

Salary is dependent on a variety of factors including (but not limited to) experience, skills, and location.

Who We Are

GPJ is the world leader in experiential marketing. Our 29 global offices are filled with fearless people dreaming up ideas that are transforming industries and bringing the most respected brands to life in powerfully, exciting ways. We are a part of the Project Worldwide family. An independent, employee-owned global network of complementary, wholly owned agencies.

You read that “employee-owned” part, right? You heard us correctly. You work hard, she works hard, we all work hard… we all succeed and reap the rewards. In fact, there is a lot more you would want to know about us, like our FTO policy (no more “accruing” time off), our employer matching 401(k) plan (no vesting period), our “no employee contribution” healthcare option. But we are getting ahead of ourselves here, let’s talk about this exciting opportunity first and we can fill you in on our perks & benefits later.

title: Assistant Prosecutor - Legal Services (Contract Full-Time)
description:
Purpose
The Assistant Prosecutor supports the prosecution department’s operations involving the Provincial Offences Court, pursuant to Grey County’s Agreements with the Ministry of Attorney General, County of Bruce, Grey Sauble Conservation Authority and Saugeen Valley Conservation Authority.
The Assistant Prosecutor provides assistance to the department’s principal prosecutors through organizing prosecution operations in coordination with the Supervisor.
The Assistant Prosecutor also carries out direct prosecution in coordination with the County’s principal prosecutors. In doing so, the Assistant Prosecutor acts as a prosecutor for Grey and Bruce Counties in respect of charges of violations of provincial legislation, Grey County by-laws pursued under the Ontario Provincial Offences Act, Conservation Authorities Act charges pursued by Grey Sauble Conservation Authority and Saugeen Valley Conservation Authority, and for charges of violations of federal legislation under the Contraventions Act.
Responsibilities
Support for Prosecution Services

Receive calls, emails, and in person inquiries; respond to and provide information regarding prosecution and appeal matters where appropriate and refer other inquiries to principal prosecutors or other appropriate contacts; receive and process witness mileage reimbursement requests
Assist principal prosecutors in managing communications with defendants and counsel/agents on Court days
Manage schedules of appointments for all prosecutors with defendants, counsel/agents, law enforcement officers and witnesses
Assist principal prosecutors with preparation, court filing, and service of prosecution and appeal documents (i.e., factums, summons, notices, motions)
Liaise with law enforcement agencies and officers to obtain evidence disclosure submissions for active prosecution matters
Make disclosure packages available to defendants and counsel/agents after review by prosecutors, assist principal prosecutors with review and redaction process, as necessary
Track status of ongoing prosecutions and appeals and maintain statistics on them as required
Track prosecution and appeal matters sent to outside counsel and legal service providers, provide information and assistance to them, as necessary
Maintain internal files and databases on prosecution and appeal matters
Coordinate prosecution operations with Provincial Offences Court administration staff in order to promote efficient court operations
Coordinate with Criminal Court staff in respect of appeal scheduling and operations
Manage prosecution records in accordance with department and county policies

Direct Prosecution Responsibilities

Under the direction of the Supervisor and in coordination with the principal prosecutors:

act as prosecutor under the Provincial Offences Act and the Contraventions Act for offences to be prosecuted by Grey and Bruce Counties unless precluded by law or policy from so acting, and from time to time on behalf of other municipalities and agencies in respect of prosecution of offence charges that Grey County is prosecuting on their behalf.
review charging documents for offences to be prosecuted by the County and screen charges laid.
identify opportunities to resolve charges without trial in accordance with department policy; issue resolution proposal documentation where appropriate; meet/communicate with defendants and with defendants’ counsel/agents to discuss resolution of charges without trial; present proposed resolutions in Court; and
appear in Provincial Offences Court at first appearances, early resolution meetings, plea (resolution) hearings, trials, sentencing hearings, and other court appearances; examine and cross-examine witnesses, make submissions on law and on sentence

Appear in Provincial Offences Court and on appeals as agent for the principal prosecutors when required and permissible
Deliver prosecution services to the public and other participants in the Provincial Offences Court system, including defendants, counsel/representatives, and police and civilian witnesses in accordance with policies, standards, and practices established by the County, the Provincial Offences Court Manager, and the Supervisor with respect to delivery of service to the public
Disclose to the Supervisor any actual or perceived conflict of interest that precludes any Prosecutor from acting in any particular prosecution as soon as a Prosecutor becomes aware of such conflict or the possibility of such conflict

General

Act as a Commissioner for Taking Affidavits in respect of department matters when required
Provide backup coverage for administrative and support functions of the Law Clerk / Real Estate Coordinator when they are unavailable
Carry out other duties as assigned by the Supervisor

Working Conditions
Hours of work are full-time weekly, including time beyond normal working hours if required by the Court.
Some work is conducted in open court before a judge or justice of the peace, opposing parties, their counsel or agent, court staff and members of the public.
Some work involves interactions (both in-person and remote) with members of the public who are charged under the Provincial Offences Act and parties engaged in disputes with the County. Such work may involve intense and emotionally loaded situations.
Travel at various times throughout the year may be required to attend at the Bruce County Provincial Offences Court location in Walkerton. Occasional travel may be required to other locations within and beyond Grey County.
The prosecutors to be supported by the Assistant Prosecutor must complete their work on very specific timelines. Support for prosecution communications, scheduling, and disclosure handling must be handled on specific timelines. Work involving appearances before courts and tribunals must be completed on timelines established by the relevant courts and tribunals, as well as in keeping with any agreement with, or any professional courtesy due to an opposing party, their counsel or agent, and court and tribunal staff.
Work conducted with the County’s Provincial Offences Court administration team must be carried about collaboratively and in a spirit of cooperation.
The position requires a valid Ontario driver’s license and clean police and security checks. The position requires that the incumbent to swear an oath or affirm before a judge or justice that they will act appropriately as a prosecutor, and that they govern themselves accordingly.
The Assistant Prosecutor must promptly disclose to the Supervisor any circumstance where they are charged with an offence under the Criminal Code of Canada or any other federal statute or regulation that is dealt with under the Criminal Code of Canada. They must also promptly disclose to the Supervisor any circumstance where they are charged with an offence under other federal statutes or regulations or under a provincial statute or regulation and where continuing to act in the position of Assistant Prosecutor may erode public confidence in the administration of justice.
Work may be subject to frequent interruption and the Assistant Prosecutor must schedule their work to balance competing priorities.
Contacts
Internal Working Relationships
Reports directly to the Supervisor and works alongside other Legal Services staff. Interacts routinely with Provincial Offences Court staff and manager and occasionally with staff from other departments. Must work collaboratively and cooperatively with all County staff as part of the County team.
External Working Relationships
Interacts with the judiciary, defendants and their counsel/agents in Provincial Offences Act and other court matters. Interacts with law enforcement agencies and their officers as well as municipal enforcement staff.
Knowledge and Skill
● If the incumbent is a Lawyer:

A class L1 license to practice law issued by the Law Society of Ontario
A law degree from an applicable Canadian law school (J.D. or LL.B.) (or acceptable equivalent degree from a school in a foreign jurisdiction together with a Certificate of Qualification issued by the National Committee on Accreditation in respect of that degree)

● If the incumbent is a Paralegal:

A class P1 license to provide legal services issued by the Law Society of Ontario
Satisfaction of the educational requirements of the Law Society of Ontario for the issuance and maintenance of such license
At least two years’ experience in some combination of court-related work in any area (Provincial Offences or criminal law strongly preferred)

Experience in advocacy, both written and oral, before courts and tribunals commensurate to the training/experience requirements noted above
Effective facilitation and interpersonal skills, particularly with respect to interactions with opposed parties
Personable, diligent and a client focused team player
Experience, at a level commensurate to their training and license, with procedures in Ontario Courts and Tribunals and experience with and knowledge of:

the specific legislation the incumbent would be responsible to handle matters arising under (e.g., the Provincial Offences Act, Highway Traffic Act, the Compulsory Automobile Insurance Act)
the use of municipal by-laws as regulatory laws

title: Data Scientist
description:
We're looking for a talented and passionate Data Scientist to join Wildlife's Insights team in São Paulo, Brazil.

Wildlife is one of the largest gaming companies in the world. As a Data Scientist on our Insights team, you will turn petabytes of player data into actionable decisions to make our games better. Working embedded with product teams, you will tackle complex quests, like optimizing matchmaking, scaling game economies, customizing content, and designing smart experiments to help us build games we are truly proud of.

We know that the work we do has a high impact on our company's success and culture. The right person for this position is naturally curious, comfortable in a "take the initiative" environment, loves solving problems, and can thrive in a fast and growing business.

What you'll do

  • Apply experimentation, advanced statistics, and the scientific method to continuously test hypotheses and iterate on the game.
  • Make sense of large and complex player datasets to directly impact product strategy, player retention, and long-term monetization.
  • Partner directly with Product Managers and Engineers to solve open-ended business questions quickly, leveraging existing tools or building new automations.
  • Expand game potential by delivering non-trivial solutions to core product challenges, such as optimizing game economy, matchmaking, and live content customization.
  • Disrupt the status quo by incorporating agentic AI and modern tools into your daily workflow, continuously raising the technical and analytical bar of the team.
  • Support game team decision-making by fostering analytical rigor and building high-quality data products, frameworks, and tools.

What you'll need

  • Applied Statistics & Machine Learning: Solid understanding and practical experience applying statistical techniques to product problems, including experimentation design, A/B testing, and predictive modeling.
  • Product Analytics Mindset: Proven ability to analyze player behavior, formulate hypotheses, and translate data into actionable insights for Product Managers and Engineers.
  • Core Data Skills: Strong proficiency in SQL and Python (or R) to query, clean, and analyze large datasets independently.
  • AI Tooling & Efficiency: Comfort and interest in using AI tools (such as LLMs or coding assistants) to speed up execution, automate routine tasks, and multiply your daily output.
  • Clear Communication: Ability to structure complex findings clearly and communicate effectively with cross-functional partners in written English.

More about you

  • Business-driven and pragmatic: You are motivated by generating real value for games and players, choosing the right tool for the job rather than overengineering solutions.
  • Creative problem solver: You love tackling open-ended business problems and uncovering non-obvious solutions through data.
  • Autonomous with high ownership: You take initiative in leading execution, proactively keeping stakeholders aligned while knowing when to ask for help when blocked.
  • AI enthusiast: You are eager to test new tools, push technical boundaries, and use AI to multiply your personal output.
  • Structured communicator: You communicate complex analytical ideas clearly and logically, both in speaking and writing, including in English.
  • Great teammate: You enjoy learning about adjacent disciplines, working closely with product partners, and raising the bar for those around you.

About Wildlife

Wildlife is one of the world's leading mobile game developers and publishers. We have released more than 60 titles, reaching billions of people around the globe. Here, we create games that will excite, intrigue, and engage our players for years to come!

Equal Opportunity

title: Senior Relay Technician- Utility Services
description:
Position/Job Title: Senior Relay Technician

Job Location (address): Brookhaven, Ms District Office or Conroe Tx Office are the headquarters with job locations predominately in MS, LA, TX, AR.

Job Duration: Permanent - Full Time

Job Schedule: Normally four 10-hour days per week with occasional OT

Start Date: Immediate opening

Website: MMR Group | Home (mmrgrp.com)

Company Culture:

At MMR, our most valuable assets are not our buildings or equipment, it is our family of employees with diverse backgrounds and experiences. Our investment in training programs and resources allows our employees to reach both their personal and professional goals. This is evident with MMR receiving numerous awards including “Best Place to Work” and consistently being recognized as one of the top Engineering News Record’s “Annual Specialty Contractors.”

Organization Description:

MMR has served as the industry leader in instrumentation and electrical construction, maintenance, and technical services for over 30 years. Our diverse list of clients allows us the unique ability to work across industry lines in the oil and gas upstream and midstream as well as chemical and petrochemical downstream, industrial manufacturing, power generation, renewable energy, mission critical, heavy commercial, and energy storage sectors. MMR holds the proud distinction of being the largest privately owned “Open Shop” contractor in the United States with over 30 branch offices including global locations in Canada and Mexico. For more information, please visit our website: .

The responsibilities would include, but not limited to, the following:

We are seeking an experienced Senior/Lead Relay Technician to join our Utility Services team. This position is responsible for the testing, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of protective relaying systems and associated substation equipment in utility and renewable energy facilities.
The successful candidate will serve as a technical leader in the field, performing advanced relay testing and commissioning activities while mentoring junior technicians and ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with customer specifications and industry standards.
This role requires travel and the ability to work independently or lead small work crews on energized electrical substations and complex protection and control projects.
Key Responsibilities
Relay Testing & Commissioning
  • Perform acceptance testing, commissioning, maintenance testing, and troubleshooting of protective relays and control systems.
  • Test and commission transmission, distribution, and generation protection schemes.
  • Verify proper operation of relay settings, logic, communications, and control systems.
  • Perform end-to-end testing, point-to-point verification, functional testing, and system commissioning.
  • Conduct testing on breaker failure, bus differential, transformer differential, line protection, feeder protection, capacitor bank, and generator protection schemes.
  • Analyze relay event reports, oscillography, fault records, and disturbance recordings.
Substation Testing
  • Perform testing and troubleshooting of:
    • Transmission & Distribution Circuit breakers
    • Current transformers (CTs), Potential transformers (PTs), CCVTs, SSVTs
    • Power transformers, Auto transformers
    • Battery systems
    • Control circuits
    • SCADA and RTU systems
    • Line Panels, Breaker Panels
    • Bus and Transformer Differential Panels
    • Various SEL Relays for Transmission & Distribution
    • Metering equipment
    • Capacitor Banks & Protection
    • Reactors and Protection
  • Verify proper operation of protection and control wiring.
  • Support energization and startup activities.
Leadership & Project Execution
  • Lead field crews on relay and commissioning projects.
  • Coordinate testing activities with customers, project managers, construction personnel, and operations groups.
  • Train and mentor Relay Technicians and Apprentices.
  • Review test plans, drawings, settings files, and commissioning procedures.
  • Provide technical guidance and problem resolution during project execution.
Documentation & Reporting
  • Prepare accurate test reports and commissioning documentation.
  • Review relay settings and protection documentation for completeness.
  • Maintain calibration records and testing equipment logs.
  • Ensure deliverables meet customer and company quality standards.
Safety
  • Promote and maintain a strong safety culture.
  • Follow all company, customer, OSHA, and NFPA 70E safety requirements.
  • Participate in job hazard assessments, tailboard meetings, and site safety programs.
Required Qualifications
  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Minimum 8+ years of relay testing and commissioning experience in utility substations.
  • Demonstrated experience with transmission and distribution protection systems.
  • Proficiency in reading:
    • One-line diagrams
    • AC/DC schematics
    • Wiring diagrams
    • Relay settings files
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to travel as required; Mostly Mississippi, Texas, Louisiana, Arkansas.
  • Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to pass applicable background checks, drug screens, and customer qualification requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Associate degree in Electrical Technology or related field.
  • Experience with major relay manufacturers including:
    • GE
    • Siemens
    • ABB
    • Beckwith
    • Basler
    • Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL)
  • Experience with Doble and Omicron testing equipment.
  • Experience with SCADA, RTU, and communications testing.
  • Previous relaying crew lead, relay foreman, or technical supervisory experience.
Technical Skills
The ideal candidate will have experience with:
  • SEL AcSELerator
  • Omicron Test Universe
  • Doble Protection Suite
  • ASPEN OneLiner
  • Relay setting implementation and verification
  • IEC 61850 applications
  • Mirrored Bits communications
  • Fiber optic communication systems
  • Protection scheme testing
  • NERC and utility commissioning requirements
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to work in energized substations and industrial facilities.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to stand, kneel, climb, and work from ladders as required.
  • Ability to travel and work overtime when needed.
Why Join Us
  • Competitive compensation
  • Per diem and travel opportunities
  • Company vehicle
  • Industry-leading testing equipment
  • Career advancement opportunities
  • Challenging utility and renewable energy projects
  • Safety-focused culture
  • Opportunity to work with industry experts on critical power infrastructure

Recommended Career Path for MMR Utility Services
  1. Relay Technician I
  2. Relay Technician II
  3. Relay Technician III
  4. Relay Technician IV
  5. Senior Relay Technician
  6. Lead Relay Technician
  7. Field Commissioning Engineer
  8. Senior Commissioning Engineer
  9. Commissioning Manager

Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification is strongly preferred.
Proven ability to lead and motivate cross-functional teams and influence senior leaders.
Strong command of government contracting, including FAR / DFAR regulations.
Demonstrated experience managing major subcontractors and suppliers on a global scale.
Excellent business power user IT skills (MS Office & Office 365, MS Project)
Previous experience in a machine shop is a plus.
Strong root cause analysis and problem-solving ability.
Strong English language communications skills (verbal, written and presentation); ability to clearly and concisely express and present information (or data) to non-technical associates, peers, and senior management.
Strong financial acumen related to reporting and decision-making.
Highly motivated, self-determined spirit.
Flexibility to adjust and thrive in an environment with changing requirements, schedules and priorities for multiple projects or assignments.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Occasionally lift and move materials up to 10 pounds.
Usual office working conditions with the mix of a production environment.
Expert financial acumen with deep experience managing program budgets, EACs, and P&L.
Proven ability to operate effectively and drive results in an environment with evolving processes and high ambiguity.
Willingness and flexibility to travel up to 20%.

title: R&D Laboratory Technician (Rolling Basis)
description:
Energy Exploration Technologies has a mission to become a worldwide leader in the global transition to sustainable energy. Founded in 2018, the company is fundamentally changing the way humanity is powering our world and storing clean energy with breakthrough lithium-ion technology and energy storage solutions.


The Role

As a Research and Development Lab Technician at EnergyX, you will support our research and development operations as a key contributor in the synthesis, testing, and analysis of innovative organic and inorganic compounds. In this role, you will collaborate closely with senior researchers, gaining invaluable mentorship while executing experimental plans and managing testing schedules. Our ideal candidate will show a keen attention to detail as they convert raw data into comprehensive reports that drive projects forward. Safety is our top priority! Our employees are expected to uphold OSHA regulations while ensuring a secure working environment. As part of our Operations team, you will maintain accurate inventories, facilities procurement processes, and keep our laboratory organized and efficient. This position will be located at our Headquarters in Austin, Texas. All work will be conducted in the office and lab.This position will be available on a rolling basis. All candidates are welcome to apply. No relocation will be offered for this role.


Key Responsibilities

Synthesis, Testing, and Analysis:

  • Assist in synthesizing organic and inorganic compounds according to the specifications provided by EnergyX.
  • Conduct chemical analysis and material testing following proper protocols.
  • Convert raw data and laboratory sample analyses into comprehensive internal and external reports, contributing to the understanding and progress of our projects.

Safety Compliance:

  • Prioritize safety protocols and maintain a secure working environment in accordance with OSHA regulations and permit-specific requirements.
  • Adhere to proper and consistent usage of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) to ensure personal safety and minimize risks.

Experimentation Management:

  • Execute experimental plans under the guidance of senior researchers.
  • Manage and optimize the testing schedule to ensure efficient workflow and timely completion of tasks.
  • Set up the equipment required for experimentation and ensure its proper functioning.
  • Diligently record and analyze experimental data, contributing to the generation of meaningful insights.
  • Assist the science team in daily solution preparation and sampling, demonstrating attention to detail and precision in laboratory procedures.

General Laboratory Duties:

  • Collaborate effectively within the operations team to achieve project objectives.
  • Maintain accurate inventories of materials, ensuring adequate supplies for ongoing research activities.
  • Facilitate procurement processes by ordering equipment, chemicals, and other necessary supplies in a timely manner.
  • Uphold cleanliness and organization in the laboratory environment to promote efficiency and safety.
  • Perform routine maintenance and troubleshooting of equipment to ensure optimal performance and minimize downtime.


Physical Demands:

The physical demands of this job are consistent with working in a wet-laboratory setting. Requires the ability to lift up to 25 lbs.

The physical demands here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.


Minimum Qualifications

  • 2- 4 years of experience in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or similar OR recent Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering, with no experience required.
  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills
  • Proven project execution skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to interpret and communicate information to share within and across teams
  • Time management skills
  • Innovative thinking mindset with great problem-solving skills
  • Go-getter attitude - consistently looking for opportunities to learn and build connections between the work and the science


Benefits:

  • Medical, Dental, Vision with employer contribution + additional voluntary benefits
  • PTO and Sick Leave available
  • Equity Compensation
  • Opportunity to contribute to the accelerated growth of the company


EnergyX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with EnergyX is governed on the basis of merit, competence, and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

title: Automotive Body Shop Technician-Manhattan KS
description:
Position Overview

The Automotive Body Shop Technician is responsible for performing high-quality repairs on damaged vehicles, restoring them to their pre-accident condition. This role involves working with a variety of tools and materials to perform tasks such as dent repair, frame straightening, panel replacement, and refinishing. The Body Shop Technician must have a keen eye for detail, a thorough understanding of automotive repair techniques, and the ability to work efficiently to meet deadlines.

Key Responsibilities

  • Damage Repair:

    • Assess vehicle damage and determine the appropriate repair methods.
    • Perform structural and non-structural repairs, including frame straightening, welding, and panel replacement.
    • Repair or replace damaged body panels, doors, fenders, bumpers, and other components.

  • Surface Preparation:

    • Sand, grind, and prime surfaces in preparation for painting.
    • Apply body fillers and perform necessary sanding to ensure smooth surfaces.
    • Mask and tape vehicles to protect areas not being painted.

  • Quality Control:

    • Conduct thorough inspections of repaired vehicles to ensure all work meets quality standards.
    • Perform final adjustments and touch-ups as necessary.
    • Test drive repaired vehicles to verify proper alignment and functionality.

  • Tool and Equipment Maintenance:

    • Maintain and clean tools, equipment, and work areas.
    • Ensure that all equipment is in good working condition and report any issues to management.
    • Stay updated on new tools, technologies, and repair techniques.

  • Safety and Compliance:

    • Follow all safety protocols and use personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.
    • Comply with local, state, and federal regulations regarding vehicle repairs.
    • Dispose of hazardous materials according to environmental regulations.

  • Collaboration and Communication:

    • Work closely with estimators to understand repair plans and timelines.
    • Communicate with parts associates to ensure timely delivery of needed parts.
    • Collaborate with other technicians and body shop staff to achieve efficient workflow.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent; additional technical training or certification in automotive repair is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of automotive repair techniques and procedures.
  • Proficiency in using a variety of tools and equipment, including welding machines, frame straighteners, and spray guns.
  • Ability to read and interpret repair manuals and technical specifications.
  • Excellent attention to detail and quality craftsmanship.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work efficiently and manage time effectively.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry parts and equipment up to 50 pounds.
  • Frequent standing, walking, bending, and kneeling.
  • Ability to work in a body shop environment, which may involve exposure to loud noises, dust, and fumes.

Work Environment

  • Primarily in a body shop environment.
  • May involve occasional exposure to extreme temperatures, depending on the season and shop conditions.

Performance Metrics

  • Quality and accuracy of vehicle repairs.
  • Efficiency in completing repairs within estimated timeframes.
  • Customer satisfaction and feedback.
  • Adherence to safety protocols and compliance with regulations.

The ideal candidate for the Automotive Body Shop Technician position will be detail-oriented, skilled in various repair techniques, and committed to delivering high-quality workmanship. This role is crucial in ensuring customer vehicles are restored to their original condition, contributing to the body shop's reputation for excellence.

  • Ability to work after hours, weekends, holidays, and during emergency situations as necessary to meet the needs of the client
  • Ability to read and write English in order to understand manuals and procedures, and to write reports

Physical Requirements:

Ability to sit/stand/walk for long periods of time, including walking unfinished construction project sites and on uneven surfaces; manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, phone, and other office equipment; eyesight that allows for reading a computer screen, phone screen, reports, etc.; hearing that allows for hearing/understanding spoken words; lifting and carrying up to 20 lbs.; tolerant of loud noises, airborne dust, chemicals, fumes, and inclement weather.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position is 100% in-office. The role requires working in office during standard business hours. Remote work or telecommuting is not an option for this position.

title: Project Manager, PMO (Leased)
description:
Position Overview

Nscale's North American Data Center Infrastructure (DCI) group is delivering large-scale, high-density data center campuses on demanding timelines. The Project Controls group gives every project a clear, honest view of cost, schedule, and risk.

The Project Controls Manager owns project controls for one or more DCI projects from development through handover. This role leads the project-level controls team (cost, scheduling, and planning), integrates cost and schedule into a single performance picture, and makes sure Project Directors and leadership have the information they need to make good decisions early.

Key Responsibilities

  • Project controls leadership: Lead and mentor the project-level controls team, including Cost Managers, Schedulers, and Planners; assign work, review outputs, and maintain quality standards.
  • Baseline development: Develop and maintain the project control baseline — WBS, cost breakdown structure, budget, and integrated schedule — in line with the DCI project controls framework.
  • Performance measurement: Run earned value analysis and integrate cost and schedule data to report progress, productivity, variances, and forecasts at completion.
  • Reporting: Produce weekly and monthly project reports and dashboards for Project Directors and the Director, Project Controls, highlighting trends, risks, and recommended actions.
  • Change management: Administer the change control process, including trend logs, change requests, and contractor change orders, and assess cost and schedule impacts before approval.
  • Risk management: Facilitate risk workshops, maintain the project risk register, and support quantitative cost and schedule risk analysis and contingency management.
  • Contractor oversight: Review contractor schedules, progress measurement, and payment applications; verify progress claims and hold contractors to contractual reporting requirements.
  • Forecasting and cash flow: Partner with Finance on monthly forecasts, accruals, cash flow projections, and capitalization.
  • Continuous improvement: Capture lessons learned and contribute to the evolution of DCI controls standards, templates, and systems.

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years of project controls experience on large construction or capital projects, including at least 3 years in a lead or management role.
  • Experience on mission-critical or complex facilities, such as data centers, power generation, substations, or advanced manufacturing.
  • Strong working knowledge of CPM scheduling, cost control, earned value management, and change management.
  • Ability to interpret and challenge contractor schedules, cost reports, and progress claims.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication, including presenting to senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Quantity Surveying, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

  • Hyperscale or colocation data center experience, including MEP-heavy and phased delivery.
  • AACE (PSP, CCP, EVP) or PMP certification.
  • Owner-side or owner's representative project controls experience.
  • Experience standing up controls on a new project or in a growing organization.

Character & Conduct

What We Value Most: Character & Conduct

Technical skills can be taught. Character cannot. At Nscale, we're looking for people who show up with integrity, treat others with respect, and take genuine ownership of their work. As a senior leader on the program, this individual also sets the tone for every direct report and site team they oversee. The following traits matter as much to us as any credential or years of experience:
  • Integrity — does the right thing even when no one is watching; never misrepresents status, costs, or progress to protect themselves or their team
  • Ownership mentality — treats the program as their own and holds themselves and their direct reports accountable without being told
  • Respectful under pressure — stays composed and professional with contractors, trades, direct reports, and internal Nscale teams regardless of the circumstances
  • Transparent communicator — surfaces problems early and honestly, never buries bad news, and expects the same from the teams they lead
  • Team-first attitude — ego stays at the gate; the program and the people on it come first
  • Reliable and consistent — shows up prepared, follows through on commitments, and does what they say they will do
We actively seek references that speak to a candidate's character, not just their technical output.

Tools & Software

  • Primavera P6 (required)
  • Cost management platforms (e.g., EcoSys, Procore, or similar)
  • Risk analysis tools (e.g., Safran Risk, Acumen Risk, or Primavera Risk Analysis)
  • Power BI or similar reporting / dashboard tools
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and the Microsoft 365 suite

Work Environment & Schedule

  • Hybrid role based in North America, with regular travel (approximately 25–50%) to active DCI project sites; extended site assignments may be required during key project phases.
  • Fast-paced construction environment with tight milestones; occasional work outside standard hours to support reporting cycles and critical project events.
  • Site visits require adherence to all Nscale and contractor safety programs and use of appropriate PPE.

The range below reflects the base salary for the position. Actual compensation may vary based on job-related factors such as skill set, experience, education, and location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus, equity, and/or commission programs. Nscale may offer a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, flexible paid time off, parental leave, and retirement plan participation.

title: Principal
description:
About the Team

ACCEL Schools is seeking experienced and highly motivated Principal at Barber Preparatory Academy in Highland Park, Michigan dedicated to providing a superior education for all students. We are seeking leaders who are excited to create a rigorous and nurturing environment that prioritizes student engagement and achievement.

The Principal serves as the instructional and administrative leader of the ACCEL Schools campus – responsible for the development, implementation and achievement of the school’s academic vision, student advancement and daily operations. The Principal will ensure successful academic outcomes for all students while employing long-term instructional sustainability measures involving professional development, teacher quality assessment, curriculum and pedagogical advancement.

Be part of the difference at Barber Preparatory Academy!
Barber Preparatory Academy is a public charter school providing PK-8th grade students with a well-rounded education including community service learning and competitive sports. Celebrating over 10 years of service to the Highland Park community, the school is known for its welcoming staff and faculty. Barber Prep is part of ACCEL Schools, an established network of public charter schools serving K-12 students throughout the United States since 2014.

The Principal shall be responsible for:

Instructional Leadership

  • Leading the strategic instructional design and practice, including: implementing an integrated curriculum; directing instructional coaching and evaluation; systematic use of assessment data to guide instruction; and, maximizing impact of the blended learning model (where available).
  • Develop, implement and lead the instructional programs of the school, assessing curriculum, pedagogy, lesson plans and observing classes (teaching and learning) on a frequent and structured basis to encourage the use of a variety of instructional strategies and materials consistent with research on the best practices for student learning and development.
  • Delivering consistently high levels of achievement and learning for all students through rigorous and engaging programs and classroom instruction.
  • Relentlessly work to meet all goals related to student achievement and school culture as well as Adequate Yearly Progress (AYP) goals.
  • Facilitate the implementation of a standards-based curriculum, review lesson plans weekly, and conduct frequent walk-throughs/teacher debriefs.
  • Assume responsibility for student achievement as related to academics and social-emotional wellbeing.
  • Serve as the instructional leader in the building by facilitating a growth-focused professional environment.
  • Develop and/or modify the school’s cultural programming and school-wide PBIS process with an emphasis on appropriate class conduct and behavior.

Organizational Leadership

  • Manage the school’s daily operations, including: facilities management; information/instructional technologies; food services; student data management systems; academic assessment tools; office management; budget and fiscal controls; and, student recruitment and retention.

Cooperate with the back-office service provider where necessary to meet all school administrative activities. Make recommendations for improvement as necessary.
  • Partner with Human Resources to execute a highly effective talent management system of recruiting, selecting, hiring, retaining, recognizing, and supporting all school site staff.
  • Ensure non-discrimination practices in the selection process of faculty and staff by adhering to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) requirements.
  • Collaborate with Home Office/Operations Team on the review and reporting requirements of the State, charter authorizing agency and Federal regulatory agencies, school sponsor, including the charter renewal process.
  • With support from the operations team, oversee maintenance of school census data, attendance data, and other reporting requirements as mandated by the state or school sponsor.
  • With support from the operations team, implement the national school lunch program, transportation, audits, student application distribution, collection, approval, and verifications as applicable.
  • Complete all accountability reports and oversee all student enrollment reports to the state; ensure compliance in all areas.
  • Manage student recruitment and retention and achieve goals of retaining 85% of students annually.
  • Understand and address all compliance items as they relate to the school’s Sponsor Agreement.
  • Maintain a master school calendar to be posted for all stakeholders in all appropriate mediums (i.e. website, social media, student/parent guide, employee handbook). Work with the Home Office staff to ensure all marketing and communications tools are up-to-date and active.

  • Maintain open and ongoing daily and/or weekly meetings with the Regional Vice President
  • Ensure the safety and wellbeing of all students and colleagues.

Community Leadership

  • Cultivate partnerships with external organizations that enrich the culture of the school, as well as strong working relationships with other local districts and charter authorizers.
  • Plan and conduct student and family orientations.

Qualifications

Attributes:

title: Senior Surveyor
description:
Senior Surveyor

Location: Salt Lake City, Utah
Job Type: Full-Time
Pay: DOE

Join Kinkaid Civil Construction

Kinkaid Civil Construction (KCC) is a 100% employee-owned heavy civil contractor specializing in underground wet utilities, earthwork, grading, and roadway infrastructure.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Surveyor to support our growing Utah operations. This position will provide construction surveying, layout, staking, grade control, and field support for heavy civil projects throughout the Salt Lake City area.

The ideal candidate has strong hands-on construction surveying experience and can independently support underground utility, earthwork, grading, and roadway projects while working closely with Superintendents, Foremen, Project Engineers, Project Managers, and field crews.

Position Summary

The Senior Surveyor is responsible for accurate construction layout and surveying throughout all phases of assigned projects. This position establishes and maintains survey control, performs field layout and staking, verifies grades and elevations, completes as-built surveys, and provides survey information needed by field crews.

The Senior Surveyor must be able to read and interpret civil construction plans and translate design information into accurate field layout. This is a hands-on field position requiring strong technical surveying skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently in an active heavy civil construction environment.

This position may also provide guidance and technical support to less-experienced survey personnel.

Perform construction layout and staking for underground utilities, earthwork, grading, roadway, and civil infrastructure projects.

Establish, verify, and maintain horizontal and vertical survey control.

Perform layout for water, sewer, storm drain, pipe alignments, structures, excavation limits, slopes, roadways, curb, and finished grades.

Calculate and verify coordinates, elevations, grades, slopes, offsets, alignments, and construction tolerances.

Read and interpret civil plans, profiles, cross-sections, specifications, and survey information.

Perform grade checks during excavation, utility installation, backfill, grading, and roadway construction.

Perform topographic, existing-condition, and as-built surveys as required.

Maintain accurate field notes, survey records, control points, and project documentation.

Operate GPS/GNSS equipment, robotic total stations, electronic data collectors, levels, and other survey equipment.

Assist with GPS machine-control setup, verification, and troubleshooting when needed.

Identify discrepancies between plans, survey information, and actual field conditions and communicate concerns to project leadership.

Coordinate daily survey needs and priorities with Superintendents, Foremen, Project Engineers, and Project Managers.

Provide field crews with accurate and understandable staking, layout, and grade information.

Assist with field measurements, quantity verification, and construction calculations when needed.

Maintain, calibrate, and protect survey equipment and established project control.

Provide technical guidance to Surveyors, Assistant Surveyors, and other field personnel when appropriate.

Follow KCC safety policies and maintain awareness of excavation, heavy equipment, traffic, underground utilities, and changing site conditions.

Perform additional survey and field-related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

5+ years of construction surveying experience preferred.

Heavy civil construction surveying experience strongly preferred.

Experience with underground wet utilities, earthwork, grading, roadway, or civil infrastructure construction preferred.

Ability to independently perform construction layout, staking, grade checking, and field calculations.

Strong understanding of horizontal and vertical control, elevations, coordinates, slopes, offsets, and alignments.

Ability to read and interpret civil construction plans, profiles, cross-sections, and specifications.

Experience with utility layout, construction staking, topographic surveys, and as-built surveys.

Experience using GPS/GNSS equipment, robotic total stations, and electronic data collectors.

Experience with Trimble equipment and software preferred.

GPS machine-control experience is a plus.

Strong mathematical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.

Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in an active construction environment.

Ability to communicate effectively with field crews and project-management personnel.

Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record required.

title: Senior Technical Instructor, Training & Enablement
description:
At Dragos, the mission is personal. The systems we protect deliver the water you drink, power your home, and keep the hospitals your community depends on running. Those critical infrastructure systems that power our civilization around the world are under attack every day by adversaries. When those systems fail, people are immediately at risk. We are the global leader in xOT cybersecurity, combining technology, threat intelligence, and expert services. The people here chose this work because they understand what is at stake. Here, you will find a remote-first mission-driven team across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and APAC built on authenticity, transparency, and trust. If safeguarding the systems that protect your family, friends, and community is the kind of work that matters to you, you are in the right place.

About the Role:

The Technical Instructor, Learning and Enablement delivers hands-on, technical training to security and operations teams at Dragos customer organizations. The work is primarily classroom and lab-based: you will travel to customer sites and facilitate virtual sessions, teaching the OT/ICS security concepts, platform workflows, and threat analysis skills that practitioners need to do their jobs.

This is not a soft-skills training role. Courses are technical. Students are engineers, OT security analysts, SOC operators, and plant personnel who will challenge you. The right candidate has real experience in OT/ICS environments and can hold a room of practitioners while walking through platform configuration, network traffic analysis, threat detection workflows, and incident response procedures.

You will also contribute to keeping course content current, working closely with Dragos product teams and the threat intelligence team to ensure what you teach reflects the platform as it ships and the threat landscape as it exists today.

This role extends beyond delivery. You will participate in curriculum design — coordinating with your team to develop new courses, updating existing content, and build training programs that respond to emerging customer and partner needs.

Based in APAC, you will be the primary training presence for this region — working with a high degree of autonomy and professional independence. The right candidate is someone who thrives when given broad ownership, sets their own pace, and holds themselves to a high standard without needing external structure to do so.

Responsibilities:

  • Deliver instructor-led and virtual instructor-led training to security teams, OT engineers, and operations personnel at Dragos customer organizations.
  • Facilitate lab-intensive courses covering the Dragos Platform, OT/ICS network visibility, asset identification, threat detection, vulnerability management, and incident response workflows.
  • Teach to technically experienced audiences including engineers, SOC analysts, and plant operators, who expect depth, accuracy, and practical application, and adapt delivery in real time based on audience background, prior OT experience, and comfort level with the Dragos Platform.
  • Manage hands-on lab environments during training sessions, troubleshoot technical issues as they arise, and keep sessions on track.
  • Coordinate with Dragos account and customer success teams prior to on-site engagements to understand the audience profile, deployment stage, and any site-specific constraints.
  • Partner with Dragos product teams to stay current on platform releases, new features, and configuration changes that affect course material.
  • Work with the Dragos threat intelligence team to incorporate current OT/ICS threat activity, threat group behavior, and real-world incident context into technical instruction.
  • Identify gaps or inaccuracies in existing course content and work with the Learning and Enablement team to address them.
  • Participate in curriculum design: work with your team to develop new courses, build new class formats, and create training programs that respond to customer and partner needs.
  • Translate feedback from training engagements into actionable content improvements, working collaboratively with the broader Learning and Enablement team to implement them.
  • Represent Dragos professionally in customer environments: be prepared, be credible, and leave each training engagement having raised the customer's capability.
  • Support post-training questions and follow-up from learners where appropriate, in coordination with the customer success team.

Qualifications:

  • 5 or more years of hands-on experience in OT/ICS security, operational technology engineering, or a related discipline directly supporting OT environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver technical training or instruction to experienced professional audiences, including engineers, security analysts, or operations personnel.
  • Working knowledge of OT/ICS protocols, network architectures, and security monitoring concepts (e.g., Purdue model, DMZ design, passive monitoring, asset identification).
  • Comfort with lab-based technical instruction: setting up environments, troubleshooting issues in real time, and keeping technically complex sessions on track. Strong verbal communication skills. Able to explain complex OT security concepts clearly without oversimplifying to an audience that knows the space.
  • Experience contributing to curriculum design, course development, or instructional content creation — not just delivery.
  • Proven ability to work independently and manage competing priorities without close day-to-day oversight; comfortable taking ownership of decisions in the field.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to customer sites, including industrial facilities, for on-site training engagements (35% travel expected across the region).
  • Experience with virtual lab platforms and remote training delivery tools used in technical instruction.
  • Certifications in OT/ICS security (GICSP, CSSA, ICS-CERT training, or equivalent) or relevant industry credentials, preferred.
  • Direct experience with the Dragos Platform or comparable OT security platforms (network monitoring, asset inventory, threat detection), preferred.
  • Sector background in electric utility, oil and gas, manufacturing, water and wastewater, mining, or other critical infrastructure environments, preferred.
  • Experience building training programs or curriculum frameworks from scratch in response to customer or partner needs, preferred.

Compensation:

  • Salary: AED 420,000
  • Competitive Equity Package
  • Comprehensive Benefits Plan

All new hires must pass a background check as a condition of employment.

title: Senior Technical Product Manager (Remote From Anywhere In CO)
description:
Department Information



Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado

The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.


Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.

Description of Job


TERM LIMITED POSITION: This position is term limited with an anticipated end date of December 31, 2027. This position is eligible for State employee benefits and may be extended as the situation warrants. This video explains the many benefits of working at the State of Colorado on a term limited basis.


IMPORTANT NOTE: Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT’s hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT’s hiring team.

The Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology is in the middle of a transformation worth joining. We're building cross-functional teams that design, deliver, and continuously improve services that work for Coloradans. We're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers in service of the public.

The Resident Services Redesign team is a high-priority initiative within the Governor’s Office of Information Technology, dedicated to reimagining how Colorado delivers services to its residents, starting with public benefits and safety net systems. The team is building shared digital infrastructure that state agencies and Coloradans will depend on. Delivering that kind of complex, cross-agency work requires more than good technology. It requires a team that is well-organized, clear on priorities, and able to move quickly without losing track of what matters.

OIT is seeking an experienced Senior Technical Product Manager who will be a key member of the Resident Services Redesign team. This role will build and integrate the technology that powers a more unified, modern resident experience–moving Colorado from a patchwork of separate systems toward a more modular and coherent set of digital services that residents can navigate seamlessly.

Specific products on the Resident Services Redesign team’s year one roadmap include tools for income verification, a single statewide identity and access management solution, and a secure, portable data “backpack” that would allow residents to consent to save and reuse information across multiple benefits programs and applications. The goal is durable, shared infrastructure: services many agencies and programs can build on, rather than one-off solutions.

The Senior Technical Product Manager role will require strong technical acumen, data infrastructure product management expertise, and comfort driving data-driven decision-making for these critical services. This role will strengthen Colorado's ability to deliver exceptional digital government services by providing technical product leadership for key resident-facing platforms.

As a Senior Technical Product Manager, you will drive product strategy through a combination of user research, data analytics, and technical innovation. Working at the intersection of software development, data science, and public service, you will lead the vision and roadmap for rethinking core services from the resident’s point of view and rebuilding the underlying technology to match. You will implement robust analytics frameworks, conduct A/B testing, and use data to continuously improve how residents discover and access government services.


A key aspect of this role will also be transforming how the State measures and improves digital service delivery. This includes implementing analytics frameworks, establishing experimentation practices, and creating feedback loops that demonstrate impact. This includes managing data integrations, defining meaningful metrics, and translating technical insights into actionable improvements.


In this strategic role, the Senior Technical Product Manager must balance user needs with technical constraints and business requirements while driving consensus across diverse stakeholders. You will collaborate with civic technology partners to learn from and contribute to the broader government technology ecosystem, helping ensure Colorado remains at the forefront of digital government innovation.


In this dynamic environment, the Senior Technical Product Manager must be highly adaptable and comfortable with changing priorities and approaches as we learn what works best for Colorado. This includes being flexible in your methods, willing to pivot strategies based on new information, and able to help others navigate through change while maintaining focus on improving customer outcomes.


This role will own detailed product work for a specific statewide shared service, which will entail technical design, user flows, requirements, metrics, iteration, and delivery coordination. As the portfolio grows and priorities evolve, this role may shift to support or own other services or product areas.



Essential Functions:


  • Own and iterate on detailed product requirements for statewide shared services and components, including benefits access, eligibility and verification flows, and the integrations that connect them to existing state systems

title: Genetics Lab Annotation Specialist
description:

This role will be shared between the cytogenetics and molecular diagnostics labs within the Division of Diagnostic Medical Genetics. It requires familiarity with genomic microarray technologies, cancer diagnostics and novel variant assessment and proficiency in genomic data interpretation.

In this role you will

Assist with molecular and cytogenetic analysis by performing database and literature searches to provide evidence to assist with variant analysis
Establish phenotype-genotype links, review a large spectrum of genetic disorders
Review patient reports for completeness of testing information
Assist with the investigation of new genes and roll out of information when tests go live
Assist with quality improvements strategies and efficiencies related to cytogenetic and molecular data interpretations and assessments
Assist with the assessment and implementation of new databases into the testing process
Participate in quality assurance plans and activities as required
Perform other duties consistent with the job classification as required

Job Requirements:
Mandatory

M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree in a related field from an accredited educational institution with a strong background in genomic database utilization
1 year of experience in an analytical and scientific environment with genetics concepts and/or genetic counselling

Skills and Knowledge

Demonstrated satisfactory performance and attendance history
