title: Senior Project Manager - Professional Services
description:
About the Team

MongoDB Professional Services serves as the delivery owner for complex customer initiatives, translating strategic goals into disciplined execution and measurable business outcomes across modernization, migration, cloud, data, and AI-related programs. The team drives delivery accountability across customers and internal stakeholders through strong governance, proactive risk management, and sustained alignment to customer priorities.

About the Role

MongoDB is looking for a Senior Project Manager to lead complex customer-facing Professional Services engagements and serve as the accountable delivery owner for customer requirements, execution, and business outcomes. The role translates customer objectives into a clear delivery strategy, aligns execution to expected outcomes, and drives alignment across scope, schedule, risk, dependencies, stakeholder actions, governance, and success measures.

The person acts as a consultative partner to the customer’s business. helping shape priorities, tradeoffs, and decisions while keeping delivery focused on value realization. They must bring strong services delivery leadership, executive communication skills, and the ability to operate effectively in technically complex environments with sound judgement.

The role partners closely with Consulting Engineers, Customer Success, Sales, and customer stakeholders to maintain momentum, align resources, and deliver measurable value. It also operates at both the engagement and broader account level, including leading regular quarterly business reviews and helping teams reassess priorities when needed.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Vancouver for our hybrid working model.

What you will do:

  • Lead complex Professional Services engagements from kickoff through closeout, maintaining continuity, accountability, and focus on value realization
  • Own delivery accountability for customer requirements, execution, and business outcomes, keeping work aligned to customer priorities
  • Drive alignment, planning, and execution using industry-standard delivery practices across scope, schedule, milestones, risks, dependencies, governance, and success measures
  • Serve as the primary interface to the customer executive sponsor and own financial accountability for overall engagement health
  • Shape and structure delivery and scope by clarifying objectives, guiding priorities and tradeoffs, and translating business goals into an executable delivery approach
  • Partner closely with customer stakeholders and MongoDB account, services, and technical teams to build alignment, remove blockers, and sustain momentum
  • Balance customer outcomes with business objectives, using sound judgment to manage risk, commercial awareness, resource efficiency, and overall engagement health
  • Lead governance cadences, including executive reviews and quarterly business reviews, to reassess priorities and keep resources focused on the highest-value work

What you bring

  • 8+ years in a project manager or delivery leader role, with a proven track record of leading projects for enterprise-scale clients in a SaaS product company
  • Strong executive communication and leadership skills, with credibility across senior customer stakeholders and internal cross-functional teams
  • Strong command of delivery fundamentals, including scope management, milestone planning, dependency management, risk management, executive reporting, and escalations
  • Comfort operating in technical environments, paired with strong Professional Services business acumen across delivery economics, resource planning, commercial awareness, and engagement health
  • Demonstrated problem-solving ability, strong judgment, and comfort navigating ambiguity, tradeoffs, and complex delivery decisions
  • Proven leadership delivering outcomes across cross-functional teams and customer stakeholders, with the ability to influence, align, and drive accountability without direct authority

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience leading database, cloud, modernization, or software delivery initiatives
  • Familiarity with MongoDB products, services, and common customer transformation journeys
  • Familiarity with AI and Agentic application architectures, ecosystem services, and emerging customer use cases
  • Practical experience leading the delivery of AI-integrated projects

Why this role matters

Senior Project Manager role is defined by delivery leadership and deep accountability for customer success. Rather than focusing on process, you act as the architect of the delivery experience—shaping priorities, navigating complex trade-offs, and ensuring that every milestone is directly tied to the realization of the customer's desired business outcomes..

This role links strong delivery leadership to the health of the Professional Services business by balancing customer value, delivery quality, resource efficiency, and engagement discipline. Strong Senior Project Managers improve delivery predictability, customer confidence, account health, expansion and renewal potential, and MongoDB’s reputation as a trusted partner in complex transformations. As AI becomes a larger customer priority, the role also helps identify where AI consultation can improve outcomes or delivery efficiency and ensures the right experts are engaged.

About MongoDB

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It’s what makes us MongoDB.

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we’re committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees’ wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it’s like to work at MongoDB, and help us make an impact on the world!

MongoDB is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request an accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.

MongoDB is an equal opportunities employer.

title: Diligence Program Lead
description:
About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart’s Partner Implementation & Enablement team is responsible for bringing new bank and credit union partners onto our platform and keeping existing partners equipped to run their lending programs. We own the operational core of the partner relationship: the diligence materials partners use to evaluate us, the change management process that tells them when our policies and models change, and the systems that deliver both. How quickly a partner can launch, and how much confidence they have in us once they have launched, is decided by this team’s work.

As the Diligence Program Lead at Upstart, you will own the diligence and change management programs our lending partners depend on. You will answer the due diligence questionnaires that partners and their examiners require, maintain the document library and access controls behind them, and run the recurring process that notifies partners when our policies, procedures, and models change. You will work across Compliance, Lending Partnerships, Account Management, and Product to turn a set of manual, individually held processes into programs that hold up as the partner base grows.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Own the lending partner change management program end to end: assemble each release, notify partners of policy, procedure, and model updates, and keep the supporting document libraries current.
  • Respond to lending partner due diligence questionnaires and information requests, working with Compliance, Legal, and Model Risk Management to source and verify every answer.
  • Maintain the partner-facing document repository and its access controls, including which materials each partner can reach based on their product mix and stage in the relationship.
  • Run the recurring corrective action reporting cycle: validate the source data, distribute partner-specific reports, and confirm delivery with the teams that publish them.
  • Work with Product to move manual diligence and change management workflows onto supported tooling, and document each process so more than one person can run it.
  • Identify gaps in policy ownership and documentation approval status, and raise them with Compliance and Lending Partnerships before they reach a partner.

Minimum Qualificationsu

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience
  • 5 years of experience in financial services compliance, risk, audit, or third-party due diligence
  • 2 years of experience responding to due diligence questionnaires, regulatory examinations, or audit requests from banks, credit unions, or other regulated institutions
  • Experience owning a recurring operational or reporting process end to end, including its documentation
  • Experience administering a document management system, virtual data room, or other controlled-access content repository

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of consumer lending products and the policies that govern them, including personal loans, auto, and home equity
  • Knowledge of model risk management practices and how model documentation is shared with third parties
  • Knowledge of third-party risk management expectations at banks and credit unions
  • Skilled in using generative AI tools to draft, verify, and maintain large volumes of written documentation
  • Ability to build process automation in spreadsheet or workflow tools and hand it off to others to run
  • Ability to influence across compliance, legal, product, and commercial teams without direct authority

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

#LI-Associate

title: Environmental Professional
description:
The Environmental Professional is responsible for supporting and administering Superior Tire & Rubber Corp.’s environmental compliance programs and environmental improvement initiatives. This position assists in ensuring company operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, permits, and internal requirements.

The Environmental Professional works closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Purchasing, and other departments to manage environmental requirements associated with air emissions, waste, wastewater, stormwater, chemicals, spills, and operational changes. The position serves as a technical environmental resource while helping integrate environmental compliance into day-to-day manufacturing operations and continuous improvement activities.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Support and administer environmental compliance programs in accordance with applicable regulatory, permit, and company requirements.
  • Conduct routine environmental inspections, audits, and compliance reviews; document findings and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Maintain environmental records, inspection documentation, manifests, analytical results, permits, plans, reports, and other required compliance documentation.
  • Manage hazardous, residual, universal, and other regulated waste streams, including waste characterization, labeling, accumulation requirements, storage, inspections, manifests, and vendor coordination.
  • Support air-quality compliance activities, including emissions tracking, permit requirements, equipment inspections, material usage records, and regulatory reporting.
  • Support wastewater, stormwater, and other water-related compliance programs, including inspections, sampling, analytical review, documentation, and evaluation of discharge requirements.
  • Coordinate environmental sampling and testing activities with laboratories, consultants, waste-management vendors, and other external service providers.
  • Review environmental analytical results and assist in determining appropriate actions based on regulatory and operational requirements.
  • Investigate environmental incidents, spills, releases, permit deviations, and other environmental concerns.
  • Develop, coordinate, and track corrective and preventive actions through completion and verify effectiveness.
  • Assist with preparation and submission of environmental regulatory reports, permit applications, modifications, renewals, and other required documentation.
  • Review new chemicals and materials for environmental requirements and potential impacts prior to use.
  • Participate in reviews of new equipment, processes, facility modifications, and operational changes to identify environmental requirements before implementation.
  • Develop, maintain, and update environmental procedures, work instructions, plans, inspection forms, and other compliance tools.
  • Develop and provide environmental training and technical guidance to employees and supervisors.
  • Support regulatory agency inspections and assist with responses to regulatory inquiries, findings, and other compliance matters.
  • Monitor environmental regulatory requirements and communicate changes that may impact company operations.
  • Analyze environmental data to identify trends, risks, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce waste generation, emissions, water usage, environmental risk, and the environmental impact of company operations.
  • Support environmental projects associated with facility improvements, equipment installations, process changes, and other capital projects.
  • Provide environmental technical support to Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Purchasing, and company leadership.
  • Promote environmental awareness, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

· Perform other related duties as assigned.

Other Duties:

  • Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Health, Chemistry, Biology, Occupational Safety and Health, or a related field preferred.
  • Relevant environmental, EHS, manufacturing, laboratory, regulatory, or technical experience may be considered in combination with education.

Preferred Education and Experience:

  • Previous environmental compliance experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment preferred.
  • Experience working with environmental permits, regulatory reporting, waste management, environmental sampling, or compliance inspections preferred.

Competencies/Skills:

  • Knowledge of or ability to develop working knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
  • Knowledge of environmental compliance principles related to air emissions, waste management, wastewater, stormwater, chemical management, and spill prevention.
  • Ability to interpret regulations, permits, technical documents, laboratory reports, and environmental data.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate documentation and recordkeeping.
  • Strong analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to identify compliance concerns and develop practical corrective actions.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, deadlines, and regulatory requirements.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prepare professional technical and regulatory documentation.
  • Ability to communicate environmental requirements effectively to employees, supervisors, managers, and other stakeholders.

title: Business Process Consultant (Temp)
description:
Join Aya Healthcare, winner of multiple Top Workplace awards!

Aya Healthcare is building the Aya Performance System, a practical approach to improving how work gets done across the company. APS brings together business process improvement, operational measurement, technology enablement, and change management to help teams solve meaningful business problems and sustain better outcomes.

We are seeking an APS Consultant to work closely with the APS Director and business leaders across Aya. The initial focus will be improving the processes that support Fulfillment, Sales, Recruiting, and client service—including how work moves between teams, how decisions are made, and how technology and operational workflows support business outcomes.

This person will help identify and define operational problems, facilitate discovery with frontline teams, map current- and future-state processes, evaluate solution options, and support implementation and measurement. The ideal candidate is comfortable operating in ambiguity, engaging directly with frontline employees and business leaders, translating complex problems into clear recommendations, and moving work from insight to action. Experience improving sales, recruiting, staffing, fulfillment, or client-support processes is especially valuable.

This is an initial temporary assignment with the potential to convert to a regular full-time position based on business needs, performance, and mutual fit. The initial assignment is expected to last approximately 9 months.

Who We Are:

We’re an $8+ billion, rapidly growing workforce solutions provider in the healthcare industry. We deliver tech-enabled services that help healthcare organizations meet and manage their contingent labor needs. We build and manage tech-enabled marketplaces for national and local healthcare talent and deliver contingent labor management solutions through our proprietary software platform.

At Aya, we’re obsessed with creating exceptional experiences for our clients, clinicians, and employees. In fact, we put employee satisfaction above all else. Our team members are responsible for incomparable customer experience and we know that happy employees are critical to maintaining happy clients. We foster an entrepreneurial, high-energy, low-bureaucracy culture and value innovative thinking and creative problem solving. We embrace diversity in thought and backgrounds unified by a commitment to high achievement. When you join Aya, you’ll be surrounded by teammates who care about you as an individual and leaders who will help you grow both personally and professionally.

Preferred Qualifications:

title: Transportation Coordinator (On-Call/Per Diem; Day Shift)
description:
Nestled in San Francisco's Excelsior neighborhood on a nine-acre campus, the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL) is the leading senior services organization in Northern California. Our continuum of care includes: the Frank Residences assisted living and memory care; the Jewish Home and Rehabilitation Center, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, an acute geriatric psychiatric unit for adults over the age of 65; and our Foundation.

Founded in 1871 and formerly known as the Jewish Home, our legacy grounds us as our vision propels us forward. Today, we've evolved to support more than 2,500 older adults each year through innovative, comprehensive programs rooted in the Jewish values of compassion, community, and excellence. We are equally proud of our inclusive culture, where 950 team members of diverse faiths and backgrounds work together in shared purpose.

WHY WORK WITH US

  • Mission-driven nonprofit organization
  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits
  • Meaningful work that positively impacts the lives of older adults every day
  • Inclusive community, welcoming to all (you do not need to be Jewish to live or work here)
  • Supportive, team-oriented environment
  • Opportunities for professional growth and development
  • Collaborative leadership focused on enhancing the employee experience

POSITION SUMMARY

The Transportation Coordinator is responsible for providing safe, timely, and courteous rides for residents to and from various activities while providing quality service. The Coordinator is also responsible for maintaining paperwork and records and keeping the community’s vehicles in good working condition. The Coordinator helps arrange residents' transportation needs, including medical appointments, outings, and other activities. The Coordinator is responsible for ensuring effective communication with residents, families, and caregivers and for notifying the manager and Health and Wellness Department of any changes in a resident’s condition or behavior.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Transport residents (as well as a care provider if needed) to scheduled destinations in a safe, courteous, and timely manner.
  • Place passenger safety above all other concerns; always maintain accountability of passengers at all times.
  • Assist residents with any special needs during transportation, such as but not limited to, carrying packages, opening doors, and assisting residents in and out of the vehicle and to the point of destination. This may also include pushing a wheelchair.
  • Operating a Wheelchair lift and properly securing the resident’s wheelchair to securement devices to stabilize wheelchairs during the trip.
  • Arrange residents’ transportation schedules per residents’ requests based on the resident transportation guidelines.
  • Maintaining records of all transportation requested and following the guidelines.
  • Communicating with residents, family members and/or care providers in order to properly schedule drop off and pick up.
  • Responsible for reviewing the daily transportation schedule and communicating with fellow Coordinators.
  • Transporting residents to/from planned outings booked by other departments.
  • Provide miscellaneous pickup and delivery services as needed.
  • Check vehicle prior to use for readiness, i.e., fuel, oil, tires, etc. Records routine maintenance and service check on vehicle. Maintaining the vehicle in a high state of cleanliness. Notifies supervisor of necessary repairs and vehicle malfunctions.
  • Assisting with scheduling and taking the vehicle to/from service appointments.
  • Operate vehicle in accordance with traffic laws and regulations.
  • Submit to the Department of Transportation drug testing program and any other mandated safe driving program as requested.
  • Notify supervisor of resident concerns, problems or incidents immediately.
  • Assisting the Front Desk with operational needs.
  • Logging and delivery of packages to residents and departments.
  • Attend department staff and in-service meetings, as assigned.
  • Follow safety, loss prevention, and infection control procedures.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

JOB DETAILS
• Pay Rate: $26.85/hr
• Hours: On-Call
• Shift Schedule: Day Shift; 8 AM - 4:30 PM; 9 AM - 5:30 PM
• Days Off: Varies
• Working Days: Varies

Please note that this is an On-Call position and, as such, is not eligible for benefits.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3 years as a licensed driver.
  • Valid California Class C license, with good driving record and no suspensions or revocations in the prior 3 years.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Process computer skills related to scheduler programming.
  • Experience with senior population; ability to transport residents in wheelchairs.
  • Must be able to interpret and follow map directions.
  • Ability to operate various sizes of vehicles (4 passengers, vans and buses) comfortably.
  • Ability to read, write, and effectively communicate in English.
  • Must maintain a courteous, friendly and helpful attitude with the residents and guests at all times.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Must be able to sit in a vehicle for up to 6 hours per day.
  • Must be able to stoop, bend, stretch, and squat to load and unload cargo areas.

  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds for handling luggage, medical equipment, and resident groceries. May be exposed to the elements (rain, snow, cold, heat) for short periods of time.
  • Must have good driving skills in handling vehicles on wet and/or slippery roads.

OUR INVESTMENT IN YOU

Comprehensive benefits, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage; a 403(b) Retirement Plan; Paid Time Off (PTO); Tuition Reimbursement; Commuter Benefits; and Weekday Shuttle Service to and from Glen Park BART Station.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
What We Do

Insurance is a $10T industry still running on PDFs, email threads, and manual reconciliation. Ascend is changing that. We built the first and only complete financial operations platform purpose-built for insurance — combining accounting automation, payments, and premium financing in a single vertically integrated solution. In five years, we've become the market leader: over 4,000 businesses, including more than half of the 50 largest brokers in the country, trust Ascend to bring clarity to complex accounting operations from collection to close.

How We Do It

Ascend automates the financial operations that insurers, MGAs, and agencies run every day and embeds directly into the transactions where money actually moves. Point solutions are easy to build and even easier to copy. The companies that win won't just sell tools — they'll capture value where the money actually moves. Ascend is built for exactly that moment. Our customers don't just adopt software, they unlock measurable efficiency with a proven 5-7x return on investment.

Our team is onsite in San Francisco. We bring deep expertise in insurance, fintech, and financial infrastructure to build what the industry has never had.

Why We Do It

The insurance industry intermediates trillions of dollars — and almost none of that infrastructure was built for the modern era. Legacy systems aren't just inefficient; they're a ceiling on what the industry can become.

Ascend's mission is to become the leading financial automation platform for insurance by 2030 — powering the financial operations of the entire industry and transforming the way trillions of dollars move. We're not building another point solution, we're building the financial backbone of insurance.

Your Role

Ascend is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer to join our team on-site in San Francisco to build custom integrations and own the technical delivery of customer implementations.

You will work directly with customers, Sales, Customer Success, and Engineering to understand customer workflows and turn ambiguous, high-stakes problems into practical solutions. You will write production code, build API integrations and custom features, and resolve technical blockers to launch and adoption. Your work will help unblock deals, reduce time to go-live, and embed Ascend in customers’ day-to-day operations.

Responsibilities Will Include

  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to build demos, integrations, or features that remove blockers to a deal or renewal

Objective #3: In your first 90 days and beyond:

  • Independently own account setup, configuration, and complex integrations for new customers from technical scoping through go-live
  • Lead technical conversations with customers and drive technical delivery in partnership with Customer Success
  • Build integrations, custom features, and internal tools that embed Ascend in enterprise customer workflows
  • Help drive adoption by working with customers to put solutions into daily use and remove barriers to sustained usage
  • Resolve most technical issues independently, bringing in Engineering when a broader product fix is needed
  • Turn recurring customer needs and one-off builds into product features, reusable integrations, and implementation playbooks

Must Have

  • Experience with relational databases and strong SQL
  • Hands-on experience with APIs, webhooks, and data integrations

Nice to Have

Tech Stack & Processes

  • Ruby on Rails API hosted on Heroku
  • Next.js with TypeScript hosted on Vercel

title: Director of Finance
description:
Wisconsin Center District Job Description – Director of Finance


Position Overview: Reporting directly to the Vice President of Finance and CFO, the Director of Finance assists in the development and implementation of company goals and priorities relating to financial management, budget, accounting, purchasing, and/or payroll in compliance with State and Federal law and Wisconsin Center District policies and procedures.

The Director of Finance manages the day-to-day operation of the finance department and assists the VP of Finance & CFO in providing financial leadership to the business. Primary responsibilities include management and performance of WCD event specific finance activities including finalizing event profit & loss statements, show settlements with promoters or artists, labor variance analysis, financial analysis and financial reporting, budgeting/forecasting, audit and control, asset and liability reconciliation, working capital and cash control, and management and supervision of finance staff. Assists with capital expenditure plans and WCD reporting.

The Director of Finance will provide timely, accurate and actionable business intelligence to allow the WCD to make decisions that will improve financial results, and supports management in the achievement of strategic goals through complex statistical analysis of financial results and forecasting future results using data-driven models.

Responsibilities:

Team Management & Supervision

  • Directly manage, supervise, and mentor department staff, including the Accounting Manager and Payroll Specialist.
  • Plan, direct, coordinate, and review the work plan for assigned staff; assign work activities, projects, and programs; review and evaluate work products, methods, and procedures; meet with staff to identify and resolve problems.
  • Oversight of the payroll process and payroll staff to ensure the timely and accurate processing of payroll, compliance, and reporting.

Event Finance & Settlement

  • Review and finalize event profit and loss statements in Acumatica
  • Prepare all event settlements, review with senior management, and finalize with the promoter or artist.
  • Collaborate and consult with the Booking Department on key deal points and relationship history.
  • Work closely with the Event Services Department on expense management and external communications to clients.
  • Analyze monthly show statements, perform variance analysis on events, and reconcile statements to the general ledger.
  • Consult with other applicable departments and/or contracts for clarification regarding event logistics and billing as needed.

Financial Reporting & General Accounting

  • Oversee the month-end close process, including journal entry reviews and making adjusting journal entries as necessary.
  • Prepare monthly financial reporting, cash flow statements, and client reporting.
  • Audit daily sales and deposit information; perform detailed analysis of accounts.
  • Provide highly responsible, complex professional accounting services; interpret and apply accounting standards and determine applicability to department operations; prepare and/or review highly complex financial schedules and statements.

Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Analysis

  • Participate in and provide management of the annual budget process; collaborate with departments to meet deadlines, make recommendations, and prepare variance analyses for management review.
  • Track budgets and forecasts throughout the fiscal year.
  • Track and monitor labor variances, collaborate with operations team on labor analyses
  • Analyze monthly financial statements and other data to identify trends, recognize problems, and recommend improvements.
  • Use data-driven models and complex statistical analysis to forecast future results and provide actionable business intelligence to senior leadership.

Internal Controls, Compliance & Auditing

  • Implement, document, maintain, and ensure compliance with accounting controls and procedures, including cash controls, loss prevention policies, and control environment requirements.
  • Supervise compliance with all accounting and financial requirements in accordance with GAAP, governmental accounting standards, and federal, state, and local rules and regulations.
  • Ensure WCD’s and partners’ compliance with contracts and/or other written agreements.
  • Work closely with internal and external auditors; ensure processes and financial record-keeping comply with accounting standards; provide information and answer questions regarding financial processes and decisions.

Systems, Strategy & Relationship Management

  • Advise and participate in the design and implementation of automated financial information systems and updates; continuously evaluate potential system improvements, ensure regulatory changes are addressed, and train users on system changes.
  • Develop internal relationships and use analytics to advise senior management; consult with applicable staff to resolve billing, ticket sales, and cash receipt posting issues.
  • Develop and manage external relationships with tenants, promoters, vendors, partners, and other entities to further advance the goals and interests of the WCD.
  • Lead strategic planning, process improvement initiatives, and other required ad hoc projects.
  • Perform other responsibilities and duties as assigned by management to ensure the effective utilization of company resources.

Skills & Qualifications:

  • Leadership & People Management: Strong supervisory and leadership skills, with a proven track record of managing professional finance teams, fostering a collaborative environment, and utilizing high emotional intelligence (EQ).
  • Financial & Data Acumen: Comprehensive understanding of revenue management principles and advanced quantitative skills. Extensive proficiency with financial ERP systems (e.g., Acumatica), payroll software (e.g., ADP), and advanced Excel functions for complex financial modeling.
  • Relationship & Stakeholder Management: Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills. Proven ability to navigate organizations, build cross-functional relationships, and confidently advise senior leadership, promoters, and external partners.
  • Project & Event Management: Outstanding organizational and project management skills, with a strict attention to detail and a demonstrated ability to prioritize and execute multiple event settlements and deadlines on time and within budget.
  • Strategic Problem Solving: A critical thinker and decisive problem solver who uses quantitative logic to evaluate alternative solutions, assess cost-benefit analyses, and deliver optimal business recommendations.
  • Adaptability & Resilience: Self-motivated and comfortable operating under pressure. Proven ability to manage concurrent demands, pivot smoothly in a fast-paced environment, and maintain a calm, structured approach under tight deadlines.
  • Discretion & Compliance: Absolute integrity with a strict commitment to maintaining highly confidential financial, personnel, and organizational data.
  • Scheduling Flexibility: Ability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as dictated by the event calendar, promoter settlements, or critical fiscal deadlines.
  • Exemplify the organization’s core values: Bold, Proud, Experience Obsessed


Education & Experience:

  • Required
    • Bachelor’s degree with a major in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related field or equivalent number of years of experience
    • Five (7) or more years of experience in accounting
    • Five (5) or more years of experience in a management capacity
    • Advanced proficiency in the use of the Microsoft Office Suite of Products: Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook
  • Preferred
    • Licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
    • Previous experience with Acumatica, ADP Workforce Now and ABI
    • Previous experience with a quasi-government entity, convention center, hotel, and/or sports team

Physical Demands:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand and walk.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision and peripheral vision. Specific hearing abilities required by this job include the ability to hear to be able to listen to employees, clients, guests in the course of work. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. The employee is required to use their fingers and hands in the course of general work tasks.

title: Digital Experience Product Leader
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Gap International is creating a new digital experience designed to extend the impact of our work. The vision is established. Now we are looking for an exceptional Product Lead to help make it real.

This is a rare opportunity to build something from the ground up. You will work closely with Gap’s senior leadership to translate an ambitious vision into a compelling digital product, bringing together experience design, technology, content, customer insight, and external partners.

Leadership holds the vision. You will lead the work of turning that vision into an experience people can see, use, and return to.

ABOUT GAP INTERNATIONAL

Gap International is a global performance consulting company that works with executives and their organizations to produce extraordinary business results in an ever-changing marketplace. For nearly 50 years, we’ve helped leaders articulate and fulfill the boldest possible future for their business — creating breakthrough outcomes and aligning the organization’s actions to be consistent with that future.

Our work spans 65 countries and has reached more than 50,000 executives across 1,500 organizations, from Fortune 1000 companies to entrepreneurs.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Turn vision into product. Translate the vision into a clear product strategy, experience, roadmap, and priorities.
  • Lead from 0 to 1. Move rapidly from ideas to prototypes, testing, learning, MVP, and launch.
  • Shape the experience and continued engagement.
  • Transform content into experience.
  • Bring the right people together. Lead across creative, technology, content, customer engagement, and external partners to create one coherent experience.
  • Drive choices and momentum. Establish priorities, make trade-offs, clear obstacles, and keep the work moving toward tangible outcomes.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of experience in digital product leadership, product management, digital experience, innovation, or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree required; graduate degree in business, technology, design, or a related field a plus.
  • Proven experience building and launching digital products or experiences from 0 to 1—including prototyping, user testing, MVP development, and launch, and leading across design, technology, content, customer engagement, and business.
  • Experience in digital transformation, customer experience, innovation, or technology-enabled products and services, with understanding of personalization, digital engagement, and emerging AI-enabled experiences.

WHY THIS ROLE

This is not an established product waiting to be managed. It is an opportunity waiting to be built. For the right product leader, this is a chance to take a distinctive body of thinking, an ambitious vision, and decades of experience helping people and organizations produce extraordinary results and create an entirely new way for people to experience it.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a builder who thrives at the intersection of vision and execution.

You bring:

  • Exceptional product judgment and an instinct for turning ambitious ideas into simple, powerful experiences
  • Comfort working closely with senior executives and visionaries
  • The ability to create clarity and momentum in situations where not all the answers are known

Most importantly, you know how to bring structure without bureaucracy, challenge thinking without needing to own the vision, and turn possibility into something real.

LOCATION

Gap International associates are based out of our corporate office in the Philadelphia metropolitan area.

In order to be considered for this role, applicants should be legally authorized to work in the US.

Gap International is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need, and all qualified candidates will receive consideration.

title: RAD TECH III
description:
RAD TECH III Monday-Friday *Safety Sensitive Job


Radiologic Technologists, also known as Rad Tech's or RT's, assist the Radiologist physician with the process of imaging and diagnosing illness. Radiologic Technologist job descriptions include tasks such as capturing the image, obtaining the best quality image, and ensuring the patients are comfort and safe. The Rad Tech must be able to effectively explain the procedure to the patient and be sure that they are comfortable and at ease during the procedure; however, it is very important that they do what is necessary to obtain a high-quality image that will be sufficient for thorough examination by the physician and allow for correct diagnosis.

  • Patient communication and preparation including removal of garments or jewelry that may interfere with procedure and explaining how the process works.
  • Positioning patients properly to obtain x-rays, CT scans, MR scans, or mammograms (see radiology categories below)
  • Setting the equipment to obtain the best density, detail, and contrast of the area being imaged.
  • Taking preventative steps to avoid unnecessary exposure to radiation.
  • Applying their knowledge of anatomy and physiology to the process in order to help the physician diagnose problems.
  • Must be able to closely follow physician instructions, prepare radiography equipment, position patients, and obtain optimal images for diagnosis.
  • Must be able to communicate calmly, compassionately, and professionally with all different types of patients including the elderly, ailing, and handicapped.

title: DSP Software Engineer
description:
Altamira Technologies has a long and successful history providing innovative solutions throughout the U.S. National Security community. Altamira serves the defense, intelligence and homeland security communities worldwide by focusing on creating innovative solutions leveraging common standards in architecture, data and security. Altamira believes that our people and the culture of our company differentiate us from other companies.

Position: DSP Software Engineer

Location: Warrenton, VA

Position Description:

We are seeking a Software Engineer who thrives on developing high-throughput data, low-latency code, and complex algorithm implementation. The available position moves beyond high-level application code, focusing on the intersection of systems programming, digital signals processing, and real-time data orchestration. As a Software Engineer at Altamira, you will design and build the software engines that power our sensing and communication platforms. You will be responsible for the full software lifecycle - architecting data pipelines, implementing algorithms in code, and developing robust APIs. You must be comfortable working in a Linux-centric environment where performance optimization and memory management are critical.

Key Responsibilities:

· High-Performance Development: Architect and maintain mission-critical applications using C++ for performance-intensive processing and Python for prototyping algorithms, systems logic, data manipulation, and rapid feature deployment.

· Data Orchestration: Develop software to handle high-rate data streams over UDP/TCP, ensuring packet integrity and low-latency transfer between hardware and software.

· Automation & Tooling: Create Python-based tools for automated testing, signal simulation, and benchmarking performance of the software stack. Support GitLab CI integration for automated build and deployments.

· Software-Defined DSP: Translate complex mathematical algorithms (FFTs, FIR filters, DDC, spectral estimation) into efficient, scalable Digital Signal Processing (DSP) software implementations.

· Agile Collaboration: Lead and participate in code reviews, utilize Git and Jira development productivity tools, support complex software releases in a collaborative environment.

Must-Have Qualifications and Experience:

· Software Engineering: Professional software development experience with an emphasis on C/C++ and Python.

· Linux Systems: Proficiency with multi-threading, Inter-Process Communication (IPC), and network socket programming.

· Frameworks: Experience with DSP signal processing frameworks (X-Midas, GNU Radio, REDHAWK).

· Mathematical Computing: Experience implementing mathematical / scientific algorithms in code.

· Software Best Practices: Strong rasp of Object-Oriented Design (OOD), design patterns, and modern DevOps/CI/CD.

Nice-To-Have Qualifications and Experience:

· CUDA or OpenCL: Experience using GPU-accelerated signal processing.

· Experience with hardware/software integration and networking.

· Docker or Podman: Knowledge of containerization and orchestration for deploying processing nodes.

· Signals: Familiarity with signal characteristics (pulsed/CW radar, modulations) and algorithms (FFTs, FIR filters, DDC).

· Digital Signal Processing (DSP): Understanding of concepts and software implementation (NumPy, SciPy, or FFTW).

· Applications: Background in Electronic Warfare (EW) or SIGINT (COMINT, ELINT) application areas.

Clearance Requirements:

Must be a U.S. citizen and be able to obtain up to a TS/SCI clearance.

The anticipated salary range for this position is $100,000 to $150,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, the scope of the position, relevant experience, education, certifications, internal equity, customer contractual requirements, security clearance requirements, and other legitimate business considerations.

title: Assembly & Packaging Associate
description:
About VersaDesk

VersaDesk is a Los Angeles-based, American-made ergonomic workstation brand with 25+ years of manufacturing history. We design and build standing desks, converters, drafting tables, cubicles, and workspace accessories for corporate, education, healthcare, and government customers. Our belief is simple: workspaces should adapt to people. We're looking for a Director of Lifecycle & Retention Marketing to own the customer lifecycle from first purchase through repeat business, expansion, and referral — across both our DTC storefront and our B2B/institutional sales motion.

The Role

An Assembly & Packaging Associate is responsible for preparing, inspecting, and securely packaging large items—such as desks, chairs, cubicle panels, etc—for safe warehouse storage and transit. They ensure all customer orders are complete, damage-free, and labeled correctly according to shipping specifications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Wrap and cushion items: Protect wood, laminate, glass, and metal surfaces using foam wrap, bubble wrap, corner pads, and shrink wrap.
  • Assemble custom cartons: Construct structural cardboard boxes and wooden pallets to size for complex furniture components.
  • Conduct quality checks: Inspect finished pieces for surface scratches, missing hardware, or structural defects prior to sealing.
  • Verify pick slips: Cross-reference physical product counts, hardware kits, and serial numbers against the order documentation.
  • Affix shipping labels: Place barcodes, handling stamps (like "Fragile" or "This Side Up"), and invoices prominently on the exterior container.
  • Load and secure inventory: Move wrapped items using heavy warehouse equipment and stack them safely onto delivery trucks to prevent shifting.
  • Keep an orderly workspace: Clear out cardboard debris, organize packing materials, and maintain a hazard-free staging floor.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Education: High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Tool proficiency: Experience using manual and pneumatic tools like industrial tape guns, staple machines, box cutters, and shrink-wrap dispensers.
  • Equipment operation: Basic knowledge or certification in operating material handling tools such as pallet jacks or dollies.
  • High attention to detail: Precision to match complicated part numbers and ensure hardware kits are entirely complete.
  • Adaptable schedule: Flexibility to work changing warehouse shifts, including early mornings, overtime, or occasional weekends.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures and noise levels.
  • Ability to stand and walk for up to 8 hours daily and lift up to 50 lbs consistently without assistance.
  • Ability to stand for long shifts, bend, twist, and repetitively lift heavy office furniture weighing up to 50 lbs.

description:
Job Title: Estimator III

Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department: Loenbro Industrial Construction
Location: As Assigned

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary
The Estimator III leads complex pursuits and major scopes with minimal supervision while providing advanced technical judgment, quality control, and development support to the estimating team. This role integrates work packages, leads risk and constructability analysis, directs quotation strategy, and coordinates estimate decisions with key stakeholders. A typical project-value guide is up to approximately $50 million, but complexity, risk, delivery method, scope integration, and required independence govern assignment.

Essential Job Responsibilities

  • Lead planning and execution of complex plan-and-specification, design-assist, design-build, and conceptual pursuits.
  • Integrate multiple work packages and validate quantities, productivity, pricing, indirect costs, schedule assumptions, and execution strategy.
  • Lead risk, constructability, contingency, and value-engineering analysis for assigned pursuits.
  • Direct quotation strategy, bid leveling, scope reconciliation, and resolution of subcontractor and vendor gaps.
  • Lead estimate reviews for assigned work and perform peer QA/QC on estimates of limited to moderate risk.
  • Coordinate with clients, designers, Operations, Procurement, and Business Development on scope, pricing, and pursuit strategy.
  • Mentor and direct junior estimators on pursuit assignments without assuming department personnel authority.
  • Contribute to cost history, benchmarks, production data, tools, templates, and process improvement.
  • Support estimate turnover and lessons-learned activities to improve future estimate quality.

Minimum Qualifications

Required:

· Minimum of 5 years of relevant construction estimating or equivalent directly applicable experience, with a strong focus on mechanical, structural, and industrial construction.

· Advanced estimating capability with demonstrated experience independently developing complex self-perform estimates from conceptual through final bid stages.

· Proven experience estimating self-perform scopes including light civil, concrete/structural, structural steel installation, process engineering, and process piping.

· Ability to lead estimate planning, scope development, quantity takeoffs, cost analysis, risk identification, estimate reviews, and cross-functional coordination with minimal supervision.

· Strong command of labor productivity, crew composition, production rates, material and equipment pricing, subcontractor/vendor analysis, indirect costs, general conditions, and proposal development.

· Advanced ability to interpret and quantify mechanical, structural, process piping, process engineering, civil, architectural, and related construction drawings and specifications.

· Experience developing detailed self-perform estimates for concrete structures, structural steel installation, process piping systems, mechanical systems, equipment installation, and light civil/site work.

· Effective written, verbal, presentation, collaboration, and mentoring skills, with the ability to communicate estimate assumptions, risks, and recommendations to project leadership.

· Proficiency with applicable estimating and takeoff software, Microsoft Office, reporting, CRM, and document-management systems.

· Ability to travel periodically to offices, client locations, and project sites.

· Valid driver’s license and insurability when driving is required.

· Advanced proficiency in mechanical/structural estimating and self-perform construction, with demonstrated ability to evaluate quantities, labor requirements, productivity, material costs, equipment needs, and overall execution strategy.

Preferred:

  • Enforce DD254 provisions and own the issuance of subcontractor DD254s
  • Coordinate SCI indoctrinations/debriefings
  • Partner with Mission Management and government representatives to ensure program deliverables are met
  • Create and update all annual refresher, indoctrination, and exit briefings as needed in accordance with policy and government customer requirements
  • Partner with Mission Management and Engineering teams to enhance their understanding of the program classification and other protection requirements
  • Possess a strong understanding of SCG development and the ability to influence customer determinations
  • Maintain accountability of associated program materials
  • Prepare for and successfully execute compliance inspections, including self-inspections
  • Conduct security-related inquiries and incident reporting
  • Keep abreast of the latest security trends and policy updates, implementing innovative solutions and processes
  • Attend and support various customer meetings and working groups

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree; OR 7+ years of security experience performing NISPOM-related security responsibilities in lieu of a degree
  • 5+ years of security experience performing responsibilities specifically within a SCI environment
  • Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility. Note that an active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions. If so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug, and alcohol testing

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree
  • Strong knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs), and other related security policies and procedures
  • Familiarity with DISS, NBIS, TALON, and Scattered Castles
  • Familiarity with SIMS

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to favorably complete a U.S. Government CI scope polygraph
  • Ability to travel in support of mission requirements
  • Willingness to work extended hours or weekends as needed in support of mission-critical deadlines and milestones

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $130,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

title: Security Associate - 1st Shift
description:
Schedule (Open Availability Highly Preferred):

Tues-Sat 8AM-4:30PM

Pay Range: $17 hourly

About Carvana

At Carvana, we believe buying a car the old-fashioned way sucks — so we're rewriting the playbook. Yes, we're the vending machine people. Yes, we built that on purpose. And yes, we're just getting started.

We're looking for people who want to thrive in an environment of impactful change. Team spirit shows up in everything we do — every day, our passion and creativity drive the kind of innovation that moves an industry. We take big swings, set ambitious goals, and challenge each other to make data- and process-driven decisions in everything we do. Here are a few of our stories. We've been changing the game since 2013, and we're not letting up. Want the full story? Check it out here.

About the team and position

Our Safe & Secure team is the heartbeat of every Carvana location. You're the people we trust to protect our associates, our customers, and the thousands of vehicles that flow through our gates every day. Rain, shine, ice, or 110° heat — the mission doesn't change, and neither does the standard.

This is a boots-on-the-ground role. We bring the strategy; you bring the hustle. From clearing snow during a winter storm to running heat-safety protocols in July, you'll be the reason our site stays open, safe, and moving. Some days you'll be at the gate — the literal face of Carvana to every associate, vendor, and visitor walking through it. Other days, you'll be out on the lot scanning vehicles, knocking out safety audits, or restocking the supplies that keep this place humming.

You won't just monitor a perimeter — you'll own it. That means spotting hazards before they become incidents, building real relationships with the folks on site, and stepping up when something needs your attention. You'll be trained and trusted to act in emergencies, partner with our Inspection Center and Logistics teams, and feed sharp, accurate intel back to your Safe & Secure leadership. Hourly position, reporting to your Safe & Secure Functional Lead or Manager.

What you’ll be doing

  • Lead with a service-first mindset in every interaction.
  • Live the Carvana values — and make sure they're felt by everyone you work with.
  • Be the face of Carvana at the gate for associates, vendors, and visitors.
  • Communicate like a pro — clear, calm, active listener, no missed signals.
  • Use our Unified Security Platform to monitor live cameras, review footage, and investigate intrusion alerts so nothing on site catches us off guard.
  • When things get hot, keep it cool. De-escalate, win with partners, and remember — we're all in this together.
  • Run point at the gate using the Safe & Secure App (SAS App) and RFID tech, enforcing ingress/egress procedures every single time.
  • Manage and document vehicle movement through the Inspection Center entrance and exit gates.
  • Show up when the team needs you. You'll be trained and certified in first aid, CPR, and AED — and we expect you to use it when the moment calls for it.
  • Know our emergency protocols cold so you can act decisively when seconds count.
  • Keep the site operational in any weather — snow removal in winter, heat-safety protocols in summer, no excuses, no shortcuts.
  • Drive a safety-first culture by spotting environmental hazards, running safety audits, and reinforcing best practices with the people around you.
  • Scan thousands of vehicles a day to keep operational flow tight — between mobile rover tech and manual handheld scans, every car gets accounted for.
  • Cover ground. This role involves serious walking to reach restricted or hard-to-access areas of the lot.
  • Run vehicle location research and deliver clean, detailed reports to leadership when operational questions come up.

Key Metrics:

  • Unit Loss Rate versus Plan
  • Safe & Secure App Execution
  • Inventory Control/Accuracy and Tracking
  • Safety Incident Performance

What you should know/have

  • 1–2 years in a customer service environment
  • Strong verbal and written communication
  • A track record of solid decision-making in a complex, fast-moving environment
  • Ability to build strong working relationships and connect with people quickly
  • Ability to organize, plan, and execute multiple tasks at once in a fast-paced setting
  • Ability to handle conflict in a positive, productive way

We’d love it if you also have

  • Familiarity with CCTV, RFID, Card Access, or other Safe & Secure technology
  • Previous experience supporting an OSHA / Safety Team program
  • Experience with crisis prevention and/or response plans

What we’ll offer in return

  • Full-time hourly position with a competitive wage
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits
  • 401(k) with company match
  • A stack of perks — student loan support, vehicle discounts, pet benefits, and a lot more
  • A wellness program built to keep you healthy, physically and mentally
  • Real opportunities to grow your skills and share what you know across the org
  • A promote-from-within culture with a startup feel — career paths can move fast around here
  • A seat at one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

Other requirements

To do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you:

  • Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English
  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • This position is designated as a safety-sensitive position
  • Must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently; the majority of lifting from knee to shoulder heights; other lifting required from various levels
  • Must be able to carry and transport up to 60 pounds up to 20 feet
  • Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet, and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance
  • Requires excellent visual acuity and manual dexterity
  • Requires use of safety equipment that may include, but is not limited to, face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment
  • Requires frequent driving and computer data entry
  • Must adhere to regular and predictable attendance
  • The facility is a 24/7 operation, and gates must be manned at all times

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any protected category.

title: Project Manager - Geotechnical
description:
Project Manager – Geotechnical

Wall Township, NJ, US

French & Parrello Associates (FPA) is seeking an experienced Project Manager to join our growing Geotechnical Department at our headquarters in Wall Township, NJ. This is an exciting opportunity for an accomplished geotechnical engineering professional to lead complex projects, strengthen client relationships, mentor technical teams, and build a long-term career with one of the Northeast’s fastest-growing engineering consulting firms.

Recognized year after year as one of NJBIZ’s Best Places to Work in New Jersey, FPA is committed to creating a culture where talented professionals are empowered to grow, collaborate, and succeed. In 2026, FPA was ranked #49 on Zweig’s Hot Firm List, recognizing the firm among the 100 fastest-growing AEC firms in the United States and Canada. Our continued growth is driven by our investment in our people, technical excellence, and commitment to delivering innovative solutions for the communities we serve.

The successful candidate will have extensive experience managing geotechnical projects and providing technical leadership in geotechnical investigation, analysis, and design. Working closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams, this individual will oversee all aspects of project delivery.

This role offers the opportunity to develop practical solutions to complex geotechnical challenges and help guide the continued growth of FPA’s geotechnical practice. The Project Manager will cultivate client relationships, mentor junior engineers and technical staff, and contribute to proposals and new business opportunities.

Geotechnical Engineering Expertise & Project Experience

FPA’s Geotechnical Department provides investigation, analysis, design, and construction-phase services for diverse infrastructure and development projects. Our professionals evaluate subsurface conditions and develop practical recommendations that support safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible project delivery.

The Project Manager – Geotechnical will oversee projects from initial investigation and feasibility evaluation through design and construction support. This role requires strong technical expertise, project management experience, and the ability to coordinate with clients, regulatory agencies, contractors, and multidisciplinary teams while managing multiple assignments.

Responsibilities

• Lead and manage geotechnical engineering projects from inception through completion, ensuring they are delivered on time, within budget, and meet client expectations.

• Establish and maintain strong relationships with clients, stakeholders, and regulatory agencies, providing technical advice and strategic direction as needed.

• Oversee the design and analysis of geotechnical aspects of projects including foundation design, slope stability, soil mechanics, earth retaining structures, and groundwater management.

• Supervise and mentor junior engineers, geologists, and technicians, ensuring their professional development and adherence to company standards.

• Prepare and review geotechnical investigation reports, feasibility studies, and technical specifications for clients and contractors.

• Ensure high standards of quality control, review project deliverables, and provide constructive feedback to team members.

• Develop project budgets, track project costs, and monitor schedules, proactively addressing any issues that could impact project delivery.

• Assist in identifying new business opportunities, preparing proposals, and supporting marketing initiatives to grow the geotechnical division.

• Ensure all projects comply with local, state, and federal regulations and maintain the highest standards of safety and environmental responsibility.


Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, or a related field required.

• Master's degree in Geotechnical Engineering or related discipline preferred.

• Professional Engineer (PE) license in the State of New Jersey required.

• Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in geotechnical engineering, with a focus on project management and leadership.

• Experience with geotechnical site investigations, foundation design, soil-structure interaction, and remedial solutions.

• Prior experience managing multiple projects simultaneously and interacting with clients.

• Strong technical expertise in geotechnical engineering, including software tools for analysis

• Proficient in project management software.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities.

title: Mission Lead Systems Engineer Senior III
description:
As a Mission Lead Systems Engineer, you will lead the charge on space vehicle missions, driving technical execution and championing the disruption that comes with our programs. You’ll have the autonomy to shape entire missions, the support to grow your expertise, and the opportunity to make a real difference in the future of space operations.
This role will be fully on-site in the Denver area at our Greenwood Village, CO office.

Responsibilities

Lead and Drive: Direct systems engineering activities across the full spacecraft lifecycle, from concept development and system architecture through integration, verification, and mission execution to ensure rapid deployment and mission success.
Champion Disruption: Challenge legacy approaches by applying innovative systems‑engineering methods, accelerating technical progress through efficient requirements decomposition, interface management, and system‑level decision making.
Amplify Impact: Operate within small, highly agile engineering teams where your system‑level leadership influences spacecraft design, subsystem integration, and mission outcomes.
Own Outcomes: Develop, derive, allocate, trace, and verify mission and system‑level requirements. Maintain technical baselines, V&V plans, and configuration control for assigned missions.
Forge Partnerships: Serve as a primary technical interface with customers, payload partners, subsystem owners, ground segment teams, and external mission stakeholders to ensure alignment across the system architecture.
Inspire Teams: Motivate interdisciplinary engineering groups to deliver system‑level solutions, resolve blockers, and maintain mission cadence through proactive technical leadership.
Solve Problems: Lead technical investigations, perform trade studies, manage risks, and make rapid system‑level decisions that ensure spacecraft performance and mission reliability.
Be Adaptable: Perform other duties as assigned to support programs and the Company.

Required Qualifications

Education: BS in Systems Engineering or related technical field.
Experience: 8–12 years as a systems engineer or in a broad technical leadership role (chief systems engineer, product lead, team lead).
Mindset: Self-starter, autonomous executor, and willing to stretch beyond current knowledge areas.
Technical Mastery: Deep understanding of the SE ‘V’, program execution, and space vehicle design/test.
Communication: Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills; adept at customer interfacing.
Collaboration: Proven ability to engage and motivate multidisciplinary teams, while working at least 4 days in office.
Clearance: Active Secret (or higher) clearance required

Preferred Qualifications

Active TS/SCI clearance

title: Clinical Trial Assistant
description:
SystImmune is a leading and well-funded clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company located in Redmond, WA and Princeton, NJ. It specializes in developing innovative cancer treatments using its established drug development platforms, focusing on bi-specific, multi-specific antibodies, and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). SystImmune has multiple assets in various stages of clinical trials for solid tumor and hematologic indications. Alongside ongoing clinical trials.   • Participate in regular team meeting / teleconferences; CRO, Vendor and Investigator Site meetings as necessary; and Investigator Meetings, as necessary.

  • Support the Clinical Project Management team in the tracking of subject recruitment at all study sites; monitoring visits and approval; infringements, breaches, and misconduct, fraud, and negative trends and protocol deviations. Notify CRO and sites of updates on global study information.
  • Assist Clinical Project Management team in the collection, review and filing of site Essential Documents, and maintenance of the TMF.
  • Assist in the tracking of clinical supplies at site in coordination with established systems such as IWRS, EDC and CTMS as needed.
  • Support the Clinical Project Management team in formal risk assessment activities; review and corrective action plans across study, participates in the planning of quality assurance activities, internal and external audits/inspections, and coordinates communication of audit/inspection findings.
  • Communication and support Clinical Project Management team with cross-functional study team interaction.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in health science or related field.
  • 2 years in research experience preferred.

  • Located in NJ or can commute to Princeton, NJ
  • Ability to travel as required.


Compensation and Benefits:
The expected base salary range for this position is $60,000 - $90,000 annually. Actual compensation will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to a candidate’s qualifications, experience, and skills.
While most offers typically fall within the low to mid-point of the range, we may extend an offer toward the higher end for exceptional candidates whose background and expertise exceeds the requirements of the role.

SystImmune is a leading and well-funded biotech company with a bright future. We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company’s success. At Re:Build Optimation, we specialize in delivering custom-engineered process equipment and automated systems to clients across the globe. With nearly 40 years of experience in complex chemical process systems, we have built a reputation for precision, reliability, and innovation. Our multidisciplinary team of 70+ engineers, designers, and programmers, combined with 150,000 square feet of fabrication space and over 70 skilled tradespeople, allows us to provide full turnkey solutions—from initial concept through fabrication, installation, and commissioning.

Our deep industry expertise and end-to-end capabilities make us the ideal partner for companies seeking cutting-edge automation, process control, and engineered systems.

We are looking for an experienced materials and planning professional who can connect manufacturing needs with the systems and data that keep production moving. You bring hands-on experience in materials management, production planning, scheduling, and ERP/MRP systems, with the ability to anticipate supply risks and turn data into action.

You are analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable balancing urgent material needs with longer-term planning and systems improvements. You take ownership, solve problems, and collaborate effectively across Procurement, Production, IT, Finance, and suppliers.

What You Get To Do

  • Manage material availability and inventory levels to support production schedules and resolve shortages or discrepancies.
  • Partner with Procurement and suppliers to track orders, address delays, and minimize production disruptions.
  • Develop and maintain the master production schedule, balancing demand, capacity, inventory, and material availability.

  • Drive improvements to materials, planning, scheduling, and ERP-supported processes.
