title: Fiber Engineer
description:
About Lightpath

Lightpath is building the fiber infrastructure the digital economy depends on - owning, operating, and expanding dense, high-performance networks for enterprises, public institutions, carriers, and cloud innovators. Our all-fiber network supports mission-critical environments, from financial markets and healthcare systems to AI platforms and next-generation cloud architectures. As we expand across the Northeast and into high-growth markets nationwide, we invest ahead of demand - building infrastructure with precision, resilience, and accountability.

To support that growth, we’re building a team of people who take ownership, think long-term, and take pride in tackling complex work with care and integrity. At Lightpath, every role contributes to infrastructure that powers critical systems and real-world outcomes. We look for individuals who value precision, accountability, and collaboration and who want to help build networks, processes, and partnerships that are engineered to last.

Basic Function:

The Fiber Engineering Organization is responsible for the usage, maintenance, and documentation of Lightpath’s robust fiber network. Daily efforts of a Fiber Engineer will include work supporting pre-sales engineering, new customer service installation, maintenance of existing services, asset record management within our GIS database, fiber trace analysis, outside vendor management, customer requests, and other departmental needs. Will support and report to the Manager of Fiber Engineering.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Own and manage the usage of Lightpath’s Fiber Network.
  • Make decisions regarding usage of the fiber network and how it is to be leveraged to enable our customers’ success. Will include engineering fiber routes for various telecom services such as Dark Fiber, Ethernet, SD-WAN, WDM, DIA, Small Cell, and FTT services.
  • Produce creative solutions using Lightpath assets to deliver unique services for our customers’ needs supporting design criteria such as distance limitations, diversity needs, or specific routing requirements.
  • Research existing databases, files, and records for purposes of network design, fiber optimization, customer communications, and/or relocation of fiber facilities.
  • Create and provide output specifying selected fiber path and required splicing work to be performed for new fiber-based service installations, relocation of existing fiber facilities, and/or restoration of existing traffic.
  • Ensure company records are accurate by inputting and maintaining data of physical assets in our GIS database.
  • Ensure inventory of fiber usage & customer service records are accurate by inputting and maintaining circuit data in our GIS database.
  • Establish and maintain effective communications and a professional working relationship with customers both internal and external, including Lightpath service delivery, project management, circuit design, OSP construction, sales engineering, vendors, and customers.
  • Organize workday efficiently to maximize productivity by utilizing proper time management techniques.
  • Assist in the accomplishment of company objectives or needs by performing other related duties as assigned by manager.

Qualifications:

  • 4-Year Degree in Engineering or equivalent telecom fiber network experience.
  • Ability to function independently and self-motivate.
  • Strong interpersonal skills for supporting and communicating with a variety of cross functional teams.
  • Proficiency in the MS Office suite of tools including MS Visio.
  • Proficiency in usage of Google Earth & creating/managing KMZ files.
  • Experience using Salesforce.com platform is a plus.
  • Experience using GIS-based data management system is a plus.
  • Experience using AutoCad is a plus.
  • Proficient analytical, organizational, and time management skills, including the ability to effectively prioritize assignments.
  • Knowledge & experience of fiber network engineering or fiber construction practices are preferred.
  • Work experience within Telecom industry preferred.

Lightpath is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to recruiting, hiring and promoting qualified people of all backgrounds regardless of gender, race, color, creed, national origin, religion, age, marital status, pregnancy, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law.

Lightpath collects personal information about its applicants for employment that may include personal identifiers, professional or employment related information, photos, education information and/or protected classifications under federal and state law. This information is collected for employment purposes, including identification, work authorization, FCRA-compliant background screening, human resource administration and compliance with federal, state and local law.

This position is identified as being performed in/or reporting to company operations in New Jersey. The pay range at the time of posting in the specified locations is $60,000 - $85,000/year and will be eligible for overtime pay in accordance with applicable law and company policy. Pay ranges are supplied in compliance with New Jersey law. Pay is competitive and based on a number of job-related factors, including skills and experience. Some of our featured benefits include medical, dental, vision insurance, yearly bonus program and company matched 401k.

title: Senior Product Manager, Forward Deployed
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Mission Command team is part of the Connected Warfare Division. We build the command and control (C2) tools that help warfighters understand what is happening around them, make faster decisions, and direct their forces. We spend a lot of our time with the people who actually use these tools: in the field, during exercises, wherever they are.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is not a product manager who happens to spend some time forward. The forward work is the product work. As a Forward Deployed Product Manager, you own the path from a warfighter problem to a fielded solution. That covers applications, data models, user experiences, integrations, and infrastructure.

Most of all, you work as a translation layer between the warfighter and the engineering teams. You embed with units, build real expertise in how they fight, and earn enough trust that influence runs both ways. You are there to solve their problems, not to sell them something, and you build an open, trusting relationship by doing exactly that. Sometimes an introduction is made for you. You have to be comfortable with walking into a unit that has never heard of Lattice, and earn your footing from the bottom up.

The profile we are hiring for: a product manager who can walk into a formation, understand the fight, earn the trust of the people in it, map the workflow and the data underneath it, and then pull the right parts of Anduril together to solve it. You walk in with a strong sense of ownership and responsibility, but you back it up with real curiosity and humility.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own warfighter outcomes, not features. Embed with units, learn the mission, find the problems that matter most, and own them through development, fielding, and the work that comes after.
  • Build real relationships with the people in the fight. Earn the trust of warfighters, commanders, staff, and subject matter experts. Become a partner who understands how the unit actually fights, not just what shows up in a requirements document.
  • Do the research in the field. Learn by watching, asking questions, and taking part in real workflows. Turn what you learn into clear priorities.
  • Connect the fight to the product. Map the users, decisions, workflows, systems, data, and dependencies behind an outcome, and use that to drive what gets built and integrated.
  • Design across the whole stack. Do not default to a new app or a new screen. Work out whether an outcome needs an application change, a new or richer data model, an integration, a workflow that spans applications, or a change in how data moves across the Mesh.
  • Use the data model as a product tool. Get to know what data exists, how it is represented, where it comes from, who uses it, and what has to change to make a workflow possible.
  • Design for the tactical edge. Understand how the network and the hardware affect what the user sees and does. Account for degraded conditions, bandwidth, latency, and compute when you define a solution.
  • Pull the right people together. Get warfighters, engineering, design, and the other teams around the same problem, and drive them toward one coherent answer.
  • Make ambiguous problems workable. Be just as comfortable writing a strategy, sketching a workflow, working through a data flow with an engineer, or standing at a whiteboard with the people who will use the product.
  • Run the room. Lead workshops, working groups, and design sessions. Get useful information out of a room, settle competing views, and leave with decisions and next steps.
  • Brief well and tell the story. Communicate clearly to a few operators, to a large room, and to senior leadership. Adjust the level of detail for the audience without losing the substance.
  • Prototype before you spend engineering time. Test ideas quickly with users so you get to the right answer faster.
  • Stay with it through fielding. Watch whether the solution actually helps the mission, find where it breaks under real conditions, and feed that straight back into the product.
  • Look past the single request. Spot the patterns that can become reusable across units and programs, instead of building a one-off every time.

WHO YOU ARE

Anduril moves fast and is scaling fast. We value ambition, hard work, a high bar, and a willingness to disrupt how things are normally done. The people who do well here tend to show these traits:

  • Bias for Action. You ask for forgiveness, not permission, and you hate waiting around to be told what to do.
  • Outcome-Oriented. You figure out what the business needs and work backward from there.
  • Customer Focused. You have real empathy for users and build things they actually want to use.
  • Dive Deep. You sweat the details and get into the weeds to find the root cause of a problem.
  • Ownership. You care about your products and about everything the business depends on them for. You hold yourself accountable for what your systems do and for what they fail to do.
  • Agility. You change direction without drama when the priorities change.
  • First Principles Thinking. You solve problems based on what is actually best here, not because a vendor recommended it or because it is how your last company did it.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance.
  • 4 to 8 years in product management, product scope definition, or service design, or an equivalent record of turning hard user problems into fielded solutions.
  • A track record of translating technical and domain-specific information into narratives, CONOPS, mission threads, and feature definitions.
  • Experience doing research and synthesis with users and SMEs, and building a roadmap from what you learn.
  • A history of earning trust with non-technical, operational users and partnering with them, not just collecting their requirements.
  • The ability to balance needs across engineering, data, and business stakeholders.
  • Comfort working with people across a wide range of technical backgrounds, and the willingness to learn technical systems well enough to use them in your product decisions.
  • Strong facilitation and whiteboarding skills, including leading interactive planning and decomposition sessions.
  • The ability to do your own design work in common tools such as Figma.
  • Strong organizational skills and reliability.
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% of the time, including to field and training environments.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Military experience, or direct experience working alongside operational military units, with a feel for how a unit fights and for Army staff processes, TTPs, and doctrine.
  • A range of product experience across internal tools, customer-facing applications, and tools for technical users.
  • Working knowledge of data models, system integrations, networking, or distributed and edge systems, enough to reason about data flows and network constraints.
  • A self-starter who does well with ambiguity and loose organizational structure.
  • Experience fielding capabilities and improving them based on real operational feedback.
US Salary Range
$166,000—$220,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit .

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

title: AI Scientist
location: Seattle, WA or Palo Alto, CA
description:
About Our Company

We are an innovative biomedical data company dedicated to helping healthcare institutions realize the full value of their biobanks. Through trusted, long-term partnerships, we are building a secure, de-identified repository of clinical and molecular data designed to accelerate precision medicine research. Our platform integrates streamlined biobanking with advanced data analytics, enabling faster diagnostics and the development of breakthrough therapies. Founded in 2022, we are supported by leading investors including S32, Breyer Capital, Founders Fund, and JSL Health Capital.

Role Overview

We are in search of an AI Scientist to join our computational team, where our core work spans three domains: Artificial Intelligence, Bioinformatics and Software Engineering. If you’re looking to join a core group of highly motivated, versatile professionals with demonstrated expertise in applications of artificial intelligence for biomedical discovery, please read on.

The Domains We Navigate

1. Machine Learning:

  • Design, optimize, and validate deep-learning models for high-dimensional biological data including histopathological slides, spatial transcriptomics, and structured clinical datasets.
  • Translate biological insights into modeling strategies.
  • Support model interpretability, robustness, and validation in regulated or translational research contexts.

2. Agentic AI:

  • Architect and build agentic AI systems that reason over multiple steps, plan autonomously, and orchestrate external tools.
  • Develop LLM-driven agents that retrieve, prioritize, and synthesize evidence with memory and feedback loops that let them revise hypotheses and adapt as new data emerges.
  • Engineer production-grade infrastructure that unifies structured and unstructured biomedical data at scale, and rigorously assess the robustness, reliability, and interpretability of autonomous systems operating in high-stakes clinical contexts.

3. Software Engineering:

  • Apply software engineering best practices to ensure reproducible and efficient scientific discovery.
  • Develop tools and services that support experiment tracking, reproducibility and quality control.
  • Perform software validation and documentation in research or regulated diagnostic contexts.

How We Work

We believe a small team can operate with speed, precision and efficiency by leveraging modern productivity tools. We expect you to:

  • Broaden Knowledge Base: Harness new biological concepts and technical skills outside your primary expertise rapidly.
  • Accelerate with Logic: Leverage AI coding agents for implementation and testing. You focus on architectural rigor and system logic.
  • Think Critically: Act as the ultimate auditor to identify subtle AI-generated hallucinations in code or scientific reasoning before they reach our systems.

Who You Are

  • First-author contribution to state of the art AI model publications in competitive journals or conferences.
  • Proven ability to drive end-to-end development on major projects.
  • Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, or a related field. Open to recent Ph.D. graduates, postdocs, and early-career candidates with up to 5 years of post-Ph.D. experience.

More About Us

At Network Bio, you’ll thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced startup environment where innovation and impact happen daily. Our hybrid work model blends the flexibility of remote work with the energy of in-person collaboration. We foster an inclusive, team-driven culture where every voice matters, ideas are valued, and opportunities for growth and advancement are built into our DNA.

Join us and be rewarded with a competitive compensation package that includes salary and equity, giving you a stake in our shared success. Beyond the numbers, you’ll have the rare opportunity to make a direct, visible impact in a mission-driven organization at the forefront of life sciences innovation, where your work contributes to breakthroughs that can transform patient care and advance the future of precision medicine.

The salary range for this position is $145,000 - $175,000 for the Scientist level and $180,000 - $215,000 for Senior Scientist. This represents a good-faith estimate of what we reasonably expect to pay for this role; actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. This range does not include bonus, equity, or benefits. This role is eligible for company benefits, including medical, vision, dental, and 401(k).

title: L&I Industrial Relations Agent 2 (Spanish Bilingual)
description:

Keep Washington safe and working as an Industrial Relations Agent 2. title: Product Manager, Ecosystem
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow revenue, and create new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet.

About the team

Stripe’s ecosystem enables third-party developers and technology partners to extend products such as Payments, Billing, Tax, Checkout, and Workflows. The Ecosystem team builds the Stripe Apps Marketplace and the distribution, platform, and incentive systems that connect businesses with valuable third-party solutions.

Our goal is to create a compounding ecosystem: better distribution generates merchant demand and stronger partner returns; those returns attract more high-quality apps; and those apps broaden Stripe’s product fit and value to users.

What you’ll do

We’re looking for an Ecosystem Product Lead to own the strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for Stripe’s third-party app ecosystem, including the Stripe Apps Marketplace.

You will lead both sides of the ecosystem: helping businesses discover and adopt trusted solutions, while enabling developers and partners to build successful products on Stripe. You will determine where Stripe should expand ecosystem coverage, improve the merchant journey from discovery through ongoing usage, and establish the product and operating foundations for a high-quality marketplace.

Responsibilities

  • Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and success metrics for Stripe’s third-party app ecosystem and Marketplace.
  • Define the highest-value merchant needs and ecosystem gaps by product, segment, industry, and geography; determine when Stripe should build, partner, or enable third parties to address them.
  • Improve the merchant funnel from discovery and evaluation through installation, activation, usage, and retention.

Owning your domain end-to-end, taking direct accountability for architecture decisions, technical quality, code reviews, and production incidents.

Building and maintaining production-grade REST APIs using .NET and C#; work across the stack including micro frontend components where needed

Driving resolution of technical debt while balancing short-term delivery with long-term maintainability

Championing testing standards and helping define the team's test culture — unit and integration tests are expected, not optional

Owning incidents and production issues end-to-end; useing DataDog and observability tooling as standard practice

Serving as the reference point for architectural patterns like CQRS, DDD, and event-driven architecture — expected to evaluate and introduce tooling where there's clear benefit

So are YOU our next Senior Software Engineer? You are if you…

Have 5+ years of senior-level experience building backend REST APIs in .NET and C# in production.

Have strong expertise in software design principles and patterns, including Domain-Driven Design (DDD), Event Sourcing, and CQRS.

Have experience architecting and delivering distributed, microservices-based systems with cloud infrastructure (ideally GCP) and NoSQL/MongoDB databases.

Are proficient in both asynchronous (Pub/Sub messaging) and synchronous (HTTP/REST) integration patterns.

Have frontend development experience with Angular or TypeScript (exposure to micro frontend architecture is a plus).

Are committed to quality with a strong track record of writing unit, integration, and automated tests as part of regular delivery.

Have hands-on production support and observability experience, including CI/CD workflows (GitLab) and monitoring tools (DataDog).

Have a product and business mindset: curiosity about business context in a complex, regulated domain (financial services / mortgage servicing) and the ability to clearly articulate technical and architecture decisions.

Are familiar with AI-assisted dev tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude, etc.) — the team actively uses these

Tech stack at a glance

Backend: .NET

Frontend: Angular

Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

Architecture: Distributed microservices, Domain-Driven Design, Event Sourcing, CQRS

Communication: Async (Pub/Sub), Sync (HTTP)

Testing: Automated tests across the stack; Playwright / Cypress an asset

Additional kudos if you…

Have experience with Playwright and/or Cypress for end-to-end testing.

Have experience in financial services, fintech, lending, or mortgage/secured-lending domains.

Have experience in Micro frontend / module federation.

Compensation Information:

Base salary range: $100,000 - $130,000

The final compensation package will be commensurate with the successful candidate's experience, skills, and geographic location (Canada). It includes a comprehensive benefits plan and a competitive incentive (bonus) program for Full-Time Permanent roles.

title: Product Engineer Intern
description:
INTRODUCTION:

At Ouster, we build sensors and tools for engineers, roboticists, and researchers so they can make the world safer and more efficient. We've transformed LIDAR from an analog device with thousands of components into an elegant digital device powered by one chip-scale laser array and one CMOS sensor. The result is a full range of high-resolution LIDAR sensors that deliver superior imaging at a dramatically lower price. We are taking this one step further by building industry focussed end-to-end Lidar-based Detection Technology solutions so our customers time-to-value is faster. Ouster Solutions caters to solving big problems in Smart Cities, Warehouse automation, Physical Security, and Mining to name a few. If you're passionate about solving complex problems in these fields, we need your help.

We are looking for a Software Product Engineering Intern to own and drive the system engineering, product documentation, third-party product integrations, and verification and validation functions, to bring to market innovative end-to-end Lidar Detection Technology software solutions, thereby accelerating the global automation revolution for a safe and efficient future. This position will be reporting directly to the VP of Product.

➔ Design and build proof-of-concept (POC) solutions and custom demos that showcase the power and flexibility of our product. You'll be the expert in integrating our product into a customer's existing technology stack

➔ Build value-add integrations between Lidar detection platform and Video management systems such as Genetec and Milestone

➔ Empower the sales team by developing and maintaining technical sales assets. These include demo environments, presentation decks, data sheets, unique data sets for ML algorithm improvements, and best practice guides

➔ Triage customer-reported bugs, diagnose issues in the existing product, and identify the root cause of problems

EXPERIENCE:

➔ Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. or a recent graduate, in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science

➔ Previous internship or project experience related to manufacturing, robotics, or electro-mechanical systems

➔ Experience with a scripting language like Python for test automation or data analysis ➔ Be able to roll-up sleeves and do mechanical fit up and installs

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.


Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.

title: Principal, TradFi Settlement & Digital Assets
description:
Who We Are:

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on .

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are:

The TradFi/Settlement Principal Lead is the specialist voice on how traditional financial infrastructure actually works, and what it takes to rebuild it for digital assets. This is a deep-domain role, not a generalist PM function: you need hands-on experience on both sides — settlement, custody, and post-trade flows inside a TradFi institution, and the equivalent flows inside a digital asset or blockchain environment (tokenization, on-chain settlement, digital custody). You understand the full institutional trade lifecycle end to end, and how it maps — and doesn't map — onto digital asset rails.

You will partner directly with DIS leads on the vision and strategy for our custom build engagements, co-own product direction for those builds, and translate complex institutional requirements into specs that engineering can execute against without guesswork. You are comfortable challenging assumptions — client-side and internal — and pushing back when a requirement doesn't hold up against how the lifecycle actually operates, on either side of the TradFi/digital asset divide.

This is a client-facing role. You will run discovery directly with Tier-1 institutional stakeholders, from operations and engineering teams to senior executives, and you will be the person in the room who can tell the difference between a real settlement constraint and an assumed one — in both the TradFi world and the digital asset world.

What You’ll Do:

  • Partner with DIS leads on the product vision and strategy for custom build engagements, owning prioritization and direction as the work moves from concept to delivery
  • Serve as the team's specialist on settlement, clearing, and post-trade flows across both TradFi and digital assets — bring deep, current knowledge of the institutional trade lifecycle (custody, settlement cycles, corporate actions, reconciliation) and how it translates on-chain, into every requirement
  • Translate institutional and regulatory requirements into clear, buildable specs and acceptance criteria that engineering can execute against with minimal rework
  • Run discovery and requirements sessions directly with client stakeholders, from engineers to senior operations and technology leaders, and define success in their terms
  • Challenge ideas and assumptions — both the client's and the team's — pressure-testing every requirement against how TradFi infrastructure actually behaves today and where it needs to change for digital assets
  • Partner closely with the Architect and engineering leads to make sure product decisions hold up technically, and stay in the details when it matters
  • Serve as the voice of the client internally and the voice of the roadmap externally, keeping delivery and client expectations aligned as requirements evolve
  • Embrace and champion the thoughtful adoption of AI tools to improve team performance, decision-making, and output quality

What We’re Looking For:

  • Deep, hands-on TradFi experience with settlement systems, post-trade flows, and the full institutional trade lifecycle — custody, clearing, settlement, reconciliation
  • Equally deep, hands-on experience with digital asset or blockchain infrastructure — tokenization, on-chain settlement, digital custody. This role requires genuine fluency in both worlds; a TradFi background alone, or a digital-assets background alone, is not sufficient
  • Proven experience as a Product Owner or Product Lead who has shipped complex, regulated financial infrastructure, not just consumer or generic B2B products
  • Comfort operating as a specialist rather than a generalist — real depth in one domain matters more here than breadth across many
  • Client-facing experience with Tier-1 financial institutions; credible in working sessions with engineers and in briefings with senior stakeholders
  • A strong point of view and the willingness to challenge requirements, assumptions, and even senior stakeholders when the details don't hold up
  • Ability to translate ambiguous, cross-functional institutional requirements into structured specs engineering can build against
  • Experience partnering closely with technical leadership on vision and strategy, not just backlog execution

Bonus Points:

  • Background at a custodian, clearinghouse, prime broker, or other post-trade infrastructure provider on the TradFi side, or a digital asset custodian/exchange on the crypto side
  • Formal product management experience inside a regulated fintech or capital markets environment
  • Fluency in payments rails and trading systems alongside settlement
  • Experience having personally led a build that bridged a TradFi institution onto digital asset rails (e.g., a tokenization pilot, on-chain settlement project

What We Offer:

  • Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
  • Hybrid/Flexible Working Arrangements
  • Flexible Time Off (paid)
  • 3% 401(k) company contribution
  • Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
  • Generous paid Parental Leave
  • Competitive family planning benefits for US employees
  • Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
  • Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
  • Free daily snacks and weekly breakfasts/lunches
  • Employee Resource Groups
  • Free coaching and counseling sessions through Headspace

Apply now and join us as we grow the economy that runs on code.

title: Clinical Liaison - Detroit, Michigan (Part Time)
description:
Kandu, Inc. is pioneering an integrated approach to stroke recovery by combining FDA-cleared brain-computer interface technology with personalized telehealth services. title: Automotive Inventory Specialist
description:
Automotive Inventory Specialist​

Full-Time | Monday–Friday | 8:00 AM–4:30 PM

Schedule: End time may vary depending on completion of assigned dealership work

Service Area: Fremont, San Jose, Milpitas, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Newark, Union City, and surrounding areas

Hourly earnings are made up of base pay plus per-vehicle photo compensation.

Work With Vehicles. Visit Different Locations. Keep Inventory Moving.

Pro-MotionPix supports automotive dealerships by helping them maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date online vehicle listings.

We're looking for someone dependable who enjoys being active, working outside, and visiting different dealership locations throughout the week.

In this role, you'll help dealerships get vehicles ready for their online listings. You'll locate vehicles, track down keys, move cars when necessary, and create the images, 360° views, and videos used to market inventory online.

You'll be provided with an iPhone and our mobile application, and we'll train you on exactly how the process works.

You don't need professional photography experience. What matters most is that you're dependable, organized, comfortable working on your own, and able to follow a consistent process.

What You'll Handle

Once you arrive at a dealership, you'll work through the assigned inventory for that location. Responsibilities can include:

  • Reviewing your scheduled vehicle assignments
  • Finding vehicles throughout dealership lots
  • Locating keys and confirming vehicle availability
  • Moving vehicles to the appropriate staging area
  • Capturing standardized vehicle images
  • Creating 360° vehicle views and videos
  • Using a company iPhone and mobile application to document completed work
  • Communicating with dealership employees about vehicle status and availability
  • Reporting vehicles that cannot be located or are not ready
  • Making sure each assignment meets Pro-MotionPix quality standards
  • Traveling between dealerships according to your assigned schedule
  • Keeping your work organized so scheduled assignments are completed on time

The job requires a combination of vehicle handling, customer interaction, technology, and attention to detail.

What Makes Someone Successful Here?

You don't have to come from the automotive industry.

This position can be a strong match for people who have worked in environments where they needed to stay active, manage responsibilities independently, and interact with customers or coworkers throughout the day.

Your previous experience could include:

  • Automotive dealerships or service departments
  • Vehicle detailing or lot operations
  • Warehouse or inventory positions
  • Delivery or route-based work
  • Construction or installation
  • Landscaping or outdoor work
  • Maintenance or facilities
  • Moving or other physically active jobs
  • Merchandising or field-service positions

We care more about your work habits and reliability than having a specific job title on your résumé.

We're Looking for Someone Who:

  • Shows up consistently and takes their responsibilities seriously
  • Can organize their own workload throughout the day
  • Is comfortable spending several hours on their feet
  • Doesn't mind walking large dealership lots
  • Can work outside in different weather conditions
  • Communicates professionally with customers and dealership employees
  • Pays attention to small details
  • Can troubleshoot when a vehicle, key, or assignment isn't where expected
  • Is comfortable learning new technology
  • Can work without someone providing constant direction
  • Takes pride in completing accurate work


Requirements

What You'll Need

  • Valid driver's license
  • Reliable personal vehicle for traveling between dealership locations
  • Ability to work a Monday–Friday full-time schedule
  • Ability to walk, stand, bend, and perform physical tasks throughout the day
  • Comfort working outdoors in changing weather
  • Basic smartphone and mobile-app skills
  • Strong communication and problem-solving abilities
  • Manual transmission experience is helpful, but not required
  • Previous hands-on, automotive, warehouse, delivery, construction, or similar experience is preferred
  • Ability to successfully complete a pre-employment background check and drug screening


Benefits

What We Provide

  • $25.00++ per hour
  • Base pay plus per-vehicle photo compensation
  • Paid training
  • Company-provided iPhone and required equipment
  • Mileage reimbursement between dealership locations
  • Company uniform shirt
  • Monday–Friday schedule
  • No regular weekend schedule
  • Independent work environment
  • Health, dental, and vision benefits available to eligible employees
  • 401(k) available to eligible employees

No Photography Background? That's Okay.

Our training covers the equipment, mobile application, vehicle workflow, and standards you'll need to perform the job.

The work isn't about artistic photography or creating a perfect studio shot. You're following a repeatable system to make sure dealership vehicles have the correct media for their online listings.

Ready to Get Started?

If you're looking for a full-time job that keeps you moving, gives you variety throughout the week, and puts you in the middle of the automotive industry, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today to become part of the Pro-MotionPix team.

title: Automation & Controls Designer
description:
Automation & Controls Designer


Position Type: Full-time, Exempt, Salary

Reports to: Automation and Controls Director

Supervisory Responsibility: None

Location: Jacksonville, FL (Headquarters) or Fort Worth, TX (Manufacturing Plant)


Company Summary

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.


Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.


Backed by deep engineering expertise and large-scale manufacturing capability, Stellar Energy helps customers deploy critical infrastructure faster and with confidence.

Summary Objective

As a member of the technical staff, the Automation & Controls Designer is responsible for preparing technical drawings of controls systems for the design of modular TIAC (Turbine Inlet Air Cooling) Plant, CHP, Mission Critical and District Cooling Plant up to full production. During the design process, the Designer will work closely with the Engineer to compile technical data for the control systems, including product features, dimensional information, owner specifications, contract requirements, and electrical characteristics of the distribution system. This Automation & Controls Designer will also be responsible for technical coordination of all products currently in production.

Essential Functions

  • Collaborates with controls engineers to receive instructions and direction for the project design.
  • Co-ordinates with other disciplined designers to integrate design and avoid interferences.
  • Compiles standard project drawings depicting the systems to be manufactured by Stellar Energy. These drawings will include legend sheets, installation details, schematic sheets, I/O diagrams, loop sheets, and 3D models of installed electrical conduit and equipment.
  • Involved with specification review for system requirements, assist with generation of design calculations, verify design dimensions in the field, and generate bills of materials.
  • Accomplish tasks in accordance with the company procedures, specifications, standards and any project specific addenda.
  • Participates in project teams and all activities related to the development of the modular plant.
  • Provides technical support to sales and marketing for bids and proposals, such as schematics and layouts.
  • Prepares design drawing packages to enable procurement, supply, fabrication, installation, and construction to take place.
  • Maintains good interface with designers, drafters, and production personnel from an array of design disciplines, including structural and mechanical.
  • Ensures that design deliverable dates and met.
  • Assist inhouse preliminary and factory acceptance test.
  • Interact with manufacturing production team, control systems installer, and site commissioning personnel.


Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Most work is performed in an office environment. Regular trips to the Stellar Energy fabrication facility for observation and support may be necessary which may require the use of personal protective equipment such as safety glasses, steel toed shoes and mandatory head protection.


Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit. The employee frequently is required to walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand. The employee must frequently lift or move objects up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift or move objects up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work
This is a full-time position. Days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional overtime effort may be requested to meet project specific deadlines.

Travel
Anticipated 20% travel for this position with some overnight stays. Some occasional local day travel may also be necessary.

Required Education and Experience.

Preferred Education and Experience

None.

Must be authorized to work in the USA.

title: YES Member at Steamtown National Historic Site
description:
Position Title: Youth Empowerment Steward (YES) AmeriCorps Member at Steamtown National Historical Site

Conservation Legacy Program: Stewards Individual Placements

Site Location: Steamtown National Historical Site
150 S. Washington Ave.
Scranton, PA 18503

Terms of Service: 52 weeks

  • Start Date: 12/07/2026
  • End Date: 12/03/2027
  • Application Deadline: 11/01/2026
  • Number of Positions Available: 1
  • AmeriCorps Slot Classification: 1700 Hours

Stewards Individual Placements & Youth Empowerment Steward (YES) Initiative:
Stewards Individual Placements provides individuals with AmeriCorps service and career opportunities to strengthen communities and preserve our natural and cultural resources. The Youth Empowerment Steward (YES) initiative aims to increase access to the outdoors for all Americans.

Are you passionate about expanding access to public lands and creating welcoming outdoor experiences for all visitors? Do you believe everyone should have the opportunity to explore and enjoy our National Parks? Our health, our planet, and our collective future rely on variety – in thought, ability, experience, and ideas. Join the Youth Empowerment Stewards (YES) program and contribute to strengthening park operations and enhancing the visitor experience by helping to remove barriers to outdoor access—ensuring that our national parks remain open, attainable, and welcoming to all Americans.

Steamtown National Historic Site
Steamtown National Historic Site (NHS) was established in 1986 to preserve, interpret, and protect the history of steam railroading in America. Steamtown encompasses a historic railroad yard, steam locomotives, rolling stock, and an operational railyard, where visitors can experience the sights, sounds, and mechanics of 19th and early 20th-century railroading. Steamtown’s mission is to educate visitors about the role of railroads in American industrialization, transportation, and cultural development. The site highlights technological innovations, labor history, and economic impacts of the railroad industry, while offering hands-on experiences such as train rides, museum exhibits, and live restoration demonstrations.

Role of YES Member at Steamtown National Historic Site

The Youth Empowerment Steward (YES) AmeriCorps Member at Steamtown National Historic Site will play a key role in expanding access, improving visitor trip planning, and increasing access to historically constrained spaces; advancing the park’s access and welcome efforts.

The YES Member will use National Park Service-provided audio/visual equipment and Adobe Creative Cloud applications to document historic railcars, stations, platforms, and visitor spaces with known access constraints. Through professional video, photography, and digital storytelling, the YES Member will create Section 508-compliant virtual visitor experiences and multimedia resources that improve trip planning, expand access to historically constrained environments, and support adaptive interpretation. These products will support public-facing access information, digital engagement, and internal planning for future projects to increase access.

This service project builds on prior YES access assessments and advances the implementation of the Explore Act by expanding equitable access to park resources, while also providing this YES Member with hands-on experience in access standards, digital media production, and public service.

Description of Duties:
To achieve the goals of this YES position, the Youth Empowerment Steward (YES) AmeriCorps Member at Steamtown National Historic Site will:

  • Capture high-quality video, photography, and supporting media of historic buildings, railcars, locomotives, and visitor spaces using NPS-provided audio/visual equipment
  • Develop Section 508-compliant virtual visitor experiences and digital resources using Adobe Creative Cloud applications, including Premiere Pro, and related software
  • Incorporate captions, audio description, graphics, and other Universal Design principles into multimedia products to ensure attainability for diverse audiences
  • Create visitor-friendly digital resources that improve trip planning and provide meaningful alternatives for spaces that are temporarily closed or physically inaccessible
  • Document access features and barriers to inform future planning, interpretation, and infrastructure improvements
  • Collaborate with park staff and NPS access specialists to ensure digital products align with Section 508 requirements and NPS best practices
  • Support access planning for interpretive programs, volunteer initiatives, and special events by developing digital resources that expand visitor access and engagement

Expected Deliverables
By the conclusion of the service term, the YES Member will produce:

  • A library of professionally produced Section 508-compliant virtual visitor experiences for priority visitor facilities, historic railroad equipment, and other significant park resources
  • High-quality digital photographs documenting access features, visitor circulation, and areas of interest
  • Section 508-compliant multimedia resources, incorporating captions, audio descriptions, alternative text, and other features
  • Visitor-facing digital content that improves trip planning and provides greater transparency regarding access conditions throughout Steamtown NHS
  • Internal documentation and recommendations that support future access improvements, interpretive planning, and digital engagement initiatives

Qualifications:

  • United States citizen, United States national, or a lawful permanent resident alien
  • Be between the ages of 18-30 (or up to age 35 with Veteran status)
  • Has received a high school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • Agrees to provide information to establish eligibility and to complete a National Service Criminal History Check.
  • Able to commit to 52 weeks of service
  • Have a connection to the disability community

Preferred Qualifications and Skills

  • · Self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively
  • Interest in using photography, video, and digital storytelling to improve access to visitor experiences and historic resources
  • Interest in learning and using new technology, software, and audio/visual equipment
  • Interest in learning about Section 508 requirements, Universal Design principles, and accessible digital content
  • Prior experience with photography, videography, graphic design, social media, or Adobe Creative Cloud applications is helpful but not required

Our Commitment:
Conservation Legacy is committed to the full consideration of all qualified individuals and will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to perform essential job functions. Physical requirements may include periodic overnight travel, non-traditional work hours, ability to move across varied terrain, use program-specific tools and a range of technology on an infrequent or frequent basis. Exerting up to 25 pounds of force occasionally to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects. The ability to safely drive an organizational vehicle may also be required for some positions. If you need assistance and/or reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please send a request to the hiring manager.

Time Requirements:

  • Typically, this position is expected to serve Monday through Friday, from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but exact service schedules may vary. A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service
  • Member may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term
  • YES Members are part of a cohort and meet virtually online on a bi-weekly basis; the YES cohort space is established for YES Members to collaborate and support one another on various access projects, while also discussing various personal and professional development topics

Orientation and Training:

  • Member will receive an orientation that includes training on AmeriCorps prohibited and unallowable activities
  • Accessibility and Section 508: Training and mentorship in Section 508 requirements, Universal Design, and accessible multimedia, including captioning, audio description, alternative text, and accessible graphics
  • Digital Media: Hands-on training in photography, videography, audio/visual equipment, digital storytelling, and Adobe Creative Cloud applications
  • NPS Digital Communications: NPS Beginner Digital course, NPS.gov CMS 101, intermediate digital training, and Social Media Training modules
  • NPS Accessibility Professionals: Opportunities to learn from and collaborate with NPS accessibility specialists, including the Park Accessibility for Visitors and Employees (PAVE) Program, as available
  • FRA 101: Participation in Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) 101, as available, to provide an introduction to railroad operations, terminology, safety, and the regulatory environment relevant to Steamtown

Benefits:

  • Segal AmeriCorps Education Award
  • Living Allowance of $660 per week
  • AmeriCorps Health Insurance coverage
  • · Access to all Member and alumni benefits of Conservation Legacy
  • · Opportunity to make a HUGE impact on your community
  • · Service opportunities can help propel your career forward with intentional experience and professional connections
  • · YES Members have opportunities to connect and collaborate with other YES Members in the bi-weekly virtual YES Cohort space

Evaluation and Reporting:

As an AmeriCorps member, performance will be evaluated on whether the member has completed the required number of hours, the member has satisfactorily completed assignments, and if the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service.

Reporting requirements include, but are not limited to, bi-weekly timesheets and accomplishment tracking.

title: Mechanical Engineering Co-op
description:
Mechanical Engineering Co-op
Position Summary
PADNOS, a fourth-generation, family-owned recycling and recycled-materials company headquartered in Holland, MI (padnos.com), is seeking a Mechanical Engineering Co-op to join its Engineering team. This is a three-semester cooperative education position completed through the Grand Valley State University Padnos College of Engineering (PCE) co-op program.
This co-op is centered on mechanical design and research and development for scrap and recycling processing equipment. Working alongside degreed engineers, our in-house machine shop and millwright crews, and plant operations, the student will use CAD to design new machinery and components, build and test prototypes, reverse engineer existing equipment, and develop improvements that raise the throughput, reliability, and material recovery of our processing systems, including shredders, balers, shears, separation and sorting systems, and conveyors.
Key Responsibilities
CAD and New Machinery Design

Create 3D part models, assemblies, and fully dimensioned 2D fabrication and machining drawings in SolidWorks (or similar)
Design new machinery, components, and subassemblies for scrap processing operations, from concept sketches and calculations through released drawings
Perform engineering calculations (loads, stresses, weldments, fasteners, drives, and power transmission) to validate designs, using FEA where appropriate
Maintain organized CAD files, revision control, and bills of materials

Prototyping and Research & Development

Support R&D projects from concept and feasibility through prototype, testing, and full implementation
Build, install, and test prototypes with the machine shop and millwright crews; collect test data and iterate on the design
Research new processing technologies, materials, and equipment; benchmark alternatives and present findings and recommendations to engineering leadership
Help prepare project scopes, equipment specifications, vendor quotes, and cost and feasibility estimates for R&D and capital projects

Reverse Engineering

Field-measure and reverse engineer existing equipment, components, and wear parts to produce accurate CAD models and drawings
Develop in-house drawings for obsolete, undocumented, or high-cost OEM parts to support fabrication, alternate sourcing, and design upgrades

Processing Equipment Improvement

Analyze production, downtime, and wear data to identify design-driven improvement opportunities on processing equipment
Redesign components and systems to improve throughput, metal recovery, wear life, safety, and maintainability
Perform root-cause analysis on recurring equipment failures and develop engineered corrective actions
Support installation, commissioning, and post-implementation review of new and modified equipment
Collaborate daily with maintenance, operations, and EHS (environmental, health & safety) teams, and document designs, procedures, and lessons learned

Typical Co-op Progression

Co-op I: Build CAD and shop-floor fundamentals by reverse engineering existing equipment and wear parts, creating and updating drawings, and supporting active design and improvement projects
Co-op II: Take on component and subsystem redesigns, perform supporting calculations, and build and test prototypes with the shop and millwright teams
Co-op III: Lead a defined design or R&D project from concept through prototype, testing, and implementation, and present results to engineering and operations leadership

Qualifications & Requirements

Enrolled in the GVSU Padnos College of Engineering (PCE) Mechanical Engineering program, in good academic standing
Completed (or completing) the Engineering Professionalism course and approved by PCE to accept a co-op offer
Available for three alternating semesters at 40 hours/week (Standard schedule), or the Flex option (six consecutive semesters at 20 hours/week) by special approval
Working knowledge of 3D CAD software (SolidWorks or similar), including part modeling, assemblies, and detailed drawings
Coursework or strong interest in machine design, statics and mechanics of materials, and manufacturing processes
Hands-on build experience preferred, such as FIRST Robotics, Formula SAE or Baja SAE, fabrication, machining, welding, or personal design projects
Strong mechanical aptitude, curiosity about how machines work, and hands-on problem-solving skills
Comfortable working in an industrial/manufacturing plant environment, including time on the production floor and in the machine shop
Strong communication, teamwork, and documentation skills

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

Split between an engineering office setting for CAD design and analysis and an industrial recycling plant and machine shop environment, with exposure to noise, dust, and variable temperatures
Required to wear PPE at all times on the plant floor and in the shop (safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe boots, and other area-specific PPE)
Able to walk and stand for extended periods, climb stairs/ladders, and occasionally lift up to 25-50 lbs
Must follow all PADNOS safety protocols, including lockout/tagout procedures, when working near or on equipment

Co-op Program Structure
This position follows GVSU PCE co-op requirements (gvsu.edu/pce):

Three alternating work semesters (Co-op I, II, III), completing one full year of engineering work experience before graduation
PADNOS and the student agree on all three rotations upfront; students may not change employers between semesters without approval
Supervision by a degreed engineer, with progressively responsible engineering work each semester (not solely technician-level tasks)
A supervisor site visit (virtual or in-person) with a GVSU faculty member each work semester
An electronic final evaluation completed via Handshake each semester, with responsibilities and schedule confirmed via Handshake at the start of each rotation

How to Apply
Interested GVSU PCE Mechanical Engineering students can apply through Handshake. Questions about the co-op program or approval process can be directed to Ethan Tanis, Industry Partnerships & Work-Based Learning Manager, Padnos College of Engineering, (616) 331-6021.

title: Systems Engineer-IT
description:
HPC Linux Software Engineer

US Citizenship is required.
An active TS/SCI is required.

DPG Solutions is seeking an experienced HPC Linux Software Engineer to support a High Performance Computing (HPC) research and development customer in Colorado Springs. You will be an active member of the Technical User Support (TUS) team, working on-site with the TUS lead, program Chief Scientist, customer representatives, researchers, users, and site staff.



This role combines software engineering with direct support for people using HPC systems. You will help users work through modeling and simulation problems, troubleshoot Linux environments, and develop, debug, and maintain software across heterogeneous platforms. The right candidate is comfortable working independently in a lab while collaborating closely with scientists and engineers.



Responsibilities

  • Support HPC users with modeling and simulation workflows, applications, and graphical user interfaces.
  • Diagnose and resolve Linux system, software, and end-user issues in an on-site lab environment.
  • Develop, use, debug, and maintain modeling and simulation software across heterogeneous, multi-platform environments.
  • Write and maintain software in Fortran, C, and/or C++, along with Bash and Korn shell scripts.
  • Analyze existing code, resolve defects, and maintain the integrity of established applications.
  • Support the full software development lifecycle, including requirements, use cases, design, coding, documentation, and testing of scalable, distributed Linux applications.
  • Apply coding standards, unit testing, and configuration management practices.
  • Mentor junior engineers and scientists, provide technical guidance, and participate in code reviews.
  • Develop and deliver workshops, tutorials, or onboarding materials for HPC users and internal staff.
  • Coordinate technical work with the TUS team, program Chief Scientist, customer, users, and site staff.



Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline and at least 10 years of professional experience.
  • Approximately five years of experience developing and using modeling and simulation software in heterogeneous, multi-platform environments.
  • Knowledge of HPC environments, related technologies, and user workflows for modeling and simulation.
  • Proficiency in Fortran, C, and/or C++.
  • Proficiency in Bash and Korn shell scripting.
  • Strong Linux skills and the ability to resolve end-user system problems independently in a lab environment.
  • Experience with coding standards, unit testing, and configuration management.
  • Experience analyzing, debugging, and maintaining an existing code base.
  • Experience developing scalable, distributed applications in Linux through requirements, design, implementation, documentation, and testing.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or scientists, conducting code reviews, and providing technical guidance.
  • Experience creating and delivering training or onboarding materials for technical users.
  • Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities.
  • US Citizenship, an active TS/SCI, and an adjudicated CI Polygraph prior to start.



What We Are Looking For

We are looking for an engineer who enjoys working directly with users as much as solving difficult software problems. You should be able to move between a researcher’s workflow, the underlying code, and the Linux environment to find the cause of an issue and help the user move forward. This role is a strong fit for someone who takes ownership of technical problems, communicates clearly, and enjoys helping others become more effective with HPC tools.



About DPG Solutions

DPG Solutions provides mission-focused engineering, software development, DevSecOps, systems administration, and cleared technical support to national security customers. We hire engineers who can integrate with a team, solve real problems, and deliver value in complex mission environments.

About the Role

We are looking for an Instructional Design Manager to own how our learning products come to life through facilitation. This is a client-facing role that may be 100% remote and may require up to 40% travel on-site to international clients or other locations for business needs.

Reporting to the Director of Learning Design and Development, this role sits at the intersection of learning design, product, client experience, and delivery and is responsible for translating our learning experiences into clear, consistent, scalable facilitation practices.

You will define our facilitation methodology and standards, build facilitator enablement and certification systems, establish quality and coaching frameworks, and ensure facilitators and SMEs are fully prepared to deliver learning experiences as they were designed.You will also partner directly with clients and internal client-facing teams to understand delivery needs, support key engagements, and represent the learning experience perspective in conversations about program design, facilitation, and delivery quality.

This role solves the critical challenge of bridging the gap between product development and scalable delivery. You will build the systems that help facilitators deeply understand a product’s instructional intent, confidently adapt in the moment, and maintain a cohesive learner experience across programs, clients, regions, and delivery modalities.

This is not primarily a curriculum development role and does not include direct people management. While you will bring strong learning design expertise and work closely with our Learning Design team, your primary focus will be facilitation excellence, product enablement, client experience, and delivery quality.

  • Remote – US

In this role you can expect to

Facilitation Standards & Methodology

  • Establish and maintain a consistent, scalable facilitation methodology across program types and delivery modalities.
  • Define facilitation presentation standards, quality criteria, and best practices that clarify what excellent delivery looks like.
  • Partner with Learning Design to translate instructional intent into high-quality facilitator guides, run-of-show materials, and supporting resources.
  • Establish documentation standards for facilitator-facing assets, including structure, usability, consistency, and level of instructional guidance.
  • Define inclusive and accessible facilitation practices that support diverse learner needs, learning environments, and global audiences.
  • Model strong facilitation practices through demonstrations, train-the-trainer sessions, and facilitator enablement experiences as needed.

Facilitator Enablement & Readiness

  • Design and maintain scalable onboarding and enablement pathways for new facilitators, experienced facilitators, and subject-matter experts.
  • Define readiness criteria, certification protocols, and product-specific enablement requirements before independent delivery.
  • Develop systems that help facilitators efficiently build familiarity with new products, instructional approaches, and delivery expectations.
  • Ensure facilitators remain current as products, content, tools, and delivery approaches evolve.
  • Maintain clear visibility into facilitator certification, readiness, and demonstrated areas of expertise so Operations and Delivery teams can make informed staffing decisions.
  • Identify gaps in facilitator readiness and recommend targeted enablement or remediation approaches.

Product Delivery Readiness

  • Ensure facilitation readiness is embedded into the product development and launch process from the outset.
  • Define the facilitator enablement requirements that must be complete before a new product or major product update moves into live delivery.
  • Partner with Product and Learning Design teams to ensure facilitator guides, enablement resources, readiness criteria, and delivery guidance are complete and usable before launch.
  • Identify delivery risks or gaps that could prevent facilitators from executing the learning experience as intended.
  • Support product pilots and early deliveries to validate facilitator readiness and surface opportunities for improvement before broader rollout.

Quality, Coaching, and Continuous Improvement

  • Define and maintain the quality framework, observation practices, and evaluation standards used to assess facilitation across our learning experiences.
  • Establish consistent observation and calibration practices so facilitators receive clear, actionable, and equitable feedback.
  • Use observations and delivery data to identify coaching opportunities and recurring quality themes across facilitators, products, and programs.
  • Synthesize feedback from facilitators, learners, clients, and delivery teams to understand what is working and where experiences need to improve.
  • Distinguish between individual facilitation needs and systemic product or delivery issues, ensuring each is addressed through the appropriate mechanism.
  • Translate recurring insights into improvements to facilitation methodology, curriculum, facilitator resources, onboarding, and enablement.
  • Track quality indicators and surface trends, risks, and opportunities to Learning and Product leadership.

All About You

Core Experience & Education

  • 5+ years of experience in Instructional Design, Learning Experience Design, facilitator enablement, training, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience delivering live, interactive learning across virtual, hybrid, and in-person environments.
  • Demonstrated experience building facilitator onboarding, enablement, certification, or train-the-trainer programs.
  • Experience evaluating facilitation performance and driving improvement through structured observation, coaching, performance rubrics, and feedback loops.
  • Strong understanding of adult learning principles and how instructional design translates into effective live facilitation.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Instructional Design, Human Resources, or a related field preferred. Professional certifications such as CPTD or equivalent instructional, facilitation, or coaching certifications are highly desirable.

Facilitation Systems & Quality Expertise

  • Demonstrated success designing scalable onboarding and enablement pathways that accelerate facilitator readiness while maintaining delivery quality.
  • Ability to build practical quality frameworks, evaluation rubrics, certification standards, and feedback systems across diverse product offerings.
  • Experience creating facilitator guides, delivery playbooks, run-of-show materials, and other facilitator-facing resources.
  • Strong coaching and feedback skills, with the ability to identify both individual performance needs and systemic quality issues.
  • Ability to use quantitative and qualitative feedback to identify trends and inform continuous improvement.
  • Strong judgment in balancing instructional design integrity with the realities of adaptive live delivery.

Collaboration & Adaptability

  • Experience working cross-functionally across Learning Design, Product, Operations, and Delivery teams.
  • Ability to influence standards and drive adoption without direct people-management authority.
  • Proven agility operating in fast-paced environments where products, client needs, and delivery approaches evolve quickly.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to translate complex instructional concepts into clear, practical guidance for facilitators and stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting learning experiences across multiple regions, cultures, or delivery contexts is highly desirable.
  • Comfort working across virtual, hybrid, and in-person modalities and traveling internationally when required.
  • Demonstrated experience working directly with clients or external stakeholders in a consultative, advisory, training, or learning-delivery capacity.
  • Strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to build credibility, understand client needs, and confidently represent learning design and facilitation recommendations.
  • Ability to translate client goals and constraints into practical learning and delivery solutions while maintaining instructional quality.

What Success Looks Like

  • Facilitation quality: Live learning experiences consistently meet established facilitation and instructional quality standards across products, facilitators, and delivery modalities.
  • Facilitator readiness: Facilitators and SMEs complete clear onboarding and readiness pathways and demonstrate product and facilitation proficiency before delivering independently.
  • Efficient onboarding: New facilitators and SMEs move from onboarding to delivery readiness efficiently, with clear expectations, resources, and support throughout the process.
  • Ongoing performance and coaching: Active facilitators receive regular observation, actionable feedback, and coaching that drives continued development and stronger delivery.
  • Product launch readiness: New learning products launch with complete facilitator guides, enablement resources, readiness criteria, and delivery guidance in place.
  • Learner and client experience: Facilitation contributes to strong learner engagement, satisfaction, and client confidence in the quality and consistency of our learning experiences.
  • Client partnership: Clients view this role as a credible learning and facilitation partner who provides clear guidance on learner experience, facilitation, and program execution.
  • Continuous improvement: Insights from facilitators, learners, clients, and delivery teams are systematically translated into improvements to curriculum, facilitator resources, and facilitation methodology.

What we offer

  • Growth opportunities within a human resources global leader
  • We prioritize learning to stay agile in an increasingly competitive business environment.
  • We foster an open-minded environment where people spark new ideas and explore alternatives.
  • Compensation: $70,000 - $100,000 per year plus annual bonus opportunity

Placement within this range is determined based on geographic location, experience, and other compensatory factors.

  • Benefits: Employees who opt into benefits as part of full-time employment, benefits include medical, dental, vision, term life and AD&D insurance, short-term and long-term disability, additional voluntary benefits, commuter benefits, wellness plans, and a 401k plan or a non-qualified deferred compensation plan. Available paid leave includes Personal Time Off (PTO) on an accrual basis per year, Paid Holidays, and up to 6 weeks of Paid Parental Leave. PTO and holiday hours are prorated based on hire date within the calendar year.

As one of the world’s largest employers, we believe in talent, not labels, and focus on the diverse and unique skills our people bring. We have zero tolerance for unlawful discrimination or harassment against any employee, associate, or candidate, at any stage of their journey with us. We seek to create an environment where everyone can thrive and feel engaged. Our commitment to equal opportunity is part of our broader commitment to respecting fundamental human rights across our value chain.
