title: Product and Privacy Counsel
description:
Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

Why Kikoff:

This is a consumer fintech startup, and you will be working with serial entrepreneurs who have built strong consumer brands and innovative products. We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

The Role

We are looking for a talented, curious lawyer to serve as a legal partner to our product, engineering, and business teams. You will work across Kikoff's growing product ecosystem — including credit-building products, earned wage access (EWA), and new product lines in development — to help us move fast while staying on the right side of a complex and evolving regulatory landscape.

This role is a fit for someone who is early enough in their career to still be building depth, but far enough along to own problems end to end. You will have real ownership over your matters from day one and a direct line of sight into how legal decisions shape the product. You should be comfortable operating in areas of legal ambiguity, eager to learn both bank-partnered and direct-to-consumer product structures, and excited by the intersection of consumer financial services and technology.

What You'll Do

  • Act as a day-to-day legal advisor to product and engineering teams throughout the product development lifecycle, from concept through launch and iteration, escalating novel or bet-the-company questions as appropriate.
  • Advise on the design, structuring, and regulatory implications of consumer financial products, including credit-building tradelines, earned wage access, lending, and new product concepts.
  • Research and apply federal and state consumer financial regulations.
  • Advise on data privacy and consumer data protection requirements.
  • Provide guidance on marketing and communications.
  • Track regulatory developments and translate them into practical, actionable product guidance.
  • Support state licensing applications, renewals, and compliance filings.
  • Draft, review, and negotiate consumer-facing terms and disclosures, a variety of different marketing materials, and commercial agreements.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with compliance, risk, marketing, and operations to embed legal guardrails without slowing the pace of innovation.
  • Use AI to make the Legal function more effective and efficient.

What We're Looking For

  • J.D. from an accredited law school.
  • Be an active member of the California state bar or registered in-house counsel in California.
  • 5-8 years of legal experience, including meaningful time in litigation, product counseling, or regulatory practice. A mix of law firm and in-house experience is a plus, but we are open to candidates coming directly from a firm.
  • Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, and a track record of turning legal research into clear, practical guidance rather than a memo full of caveats.
  • Good judgment, intellectual honesty about what you do and do not know, and a bias toward enabling the business rather than only identifying risk.
  • Eagerness and curiosity in learning new substantive areas of the law.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex legal concepts for non-legal audiences.
  • Experience and interest in the use of AI to support legal functions.
  • Enthusiasm for Kikoff's mission and the opportunity to expand access to financial services for underserved consumers.

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge of federal consumer finance statutes (TILA, ECOA, FCRA, EFTA) and a willingness to build depth quickly in state lending and money transmission frameworks.
  • Familiarity with consumer data privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA, GLBA), or the appetite to get up to speed on advising product teams on data collection, use, and sharing practices.
  • Exposure to at least one of: credit-building or credit reporting products, earned wage access, consumer lending through bank partnership models, or payments.
  • Exposure to multi-state licensing or regulatory examination processes.

Why This Role

This is a high-ownership seat on a small legal team at a company shipping real consumer financial products. You will not be a cog reviewing a queue of contracts. You will sit with product managers and engineers while decisions are being made, own your own regulatory questions, and grow into a subject-matter owner across one or more of our product lines.

🏥 Medical, dental, vision — Kikoff covers the full cost for employees, 50% for dependents

📈 RSU's

🛃 Visa sponsorship available

title: AHAH Project-Based and Capital Partnership Program Manager (COM 3)
description:
Description

AHAH Project-Based and Capital Partnership Program Manager (COM 3)
The Department of Commerce is the one agency in state government that touches every aspect of community and economic development: planning, infrastructure, energy, public facilities, housing, public safety and crime victims, international trade, business services and more. We work with local governments, tribes, businesses and civic leaders throughout the state to strengthen communities so all residents may thrive and prosper.

The Housing Division (HD) partners with local governments, Tribes, housing authorities, nonprofits, and other organizations to develop and preserve affordable housing, promote individual and family self-sufficiency, and reduce adult and youth homelessness.


This position works within the Housing Division (HD), in the Office of Apple Health and Homes/Permanent Supportive Housing (AHAH/PSH) Unit. The AHAH/PSH unit is responsible for increasing the capacity of permanent supportive housing opportunities for persons with persistent disabling conditions.


This position reports to the Subsidy Team Supervisor of AHAH/PSH and is committed to expanding the capacity and quality of permanent supportive housing (PSH) options. Evidence-based Practice PSH is a specialized service area that is gaining significant attention and investment from the Governor and Legislature and this position will be focused on providing training and technical assistance to community partners and managing subsidy program grant agreements with these goals in mind.


This position supports the Office of AHAH/PSH’s work by developing and maintaining cooperative relationships with government, businesses, property managers, service organizations, community organizations and/or government officials to increase the capacity and quality of PSH. Primary areas of responsibility include: Providing technical assistance to housing providers and property managers in PSH. Assisting with draft legislation to identify gaps in the implementation of AHAH, presenting at statewide, regional, local or national conferences. Developing, coordinating and conducting workshops or seminars focusing on evidence-based practices of PSH to local, state and national audiences. Developing and maintaining program policies, procedures, guidelines, objectives, and funding applications in support of grants; analyzing program, grantee, and fiscal performance; developing and maintaining relationships with grantees; conducting risk assessments and monitoring; and providing technical assistance to grantees to meet the program requirements and ensuring accountability for funding. This position will manage capacity grant funds allocated by the Legislature by contracting with ‘By and For’ organizations, organizations interested in partnering with or providing FCS services.

Duties

Program Management
Tasks include:
• Utilize racially equitable and culturally appropriate practices to develop and maintain program goals, guidelines, policies, procedures, fund applications, and work plans in support of grants to fund providers of supportive housing.
• Utilize racially equitable and culturally appropriate practices to develop and conduct competitive funding and procurement rounds.
• Develop, negotiate, and monitor technical aspects of contracts with grantees and the public to meet program requirements, performance outcomes, and ensure accountability for funding.
• Work closely with Commerce’s fiscal team, the AHAH-PSH Management team to develop and adjust program budgets, prepare and review monthly and quarterly reports and expenditures, determine where budgets are over and/or underspent, and reconcile expenditures with general ledger.
• Work closely with the AHAH-PSH Compliance Team to perform risk assessment and monitoring, and to implement corrective action plans, if necessary.
• Work closely with the PSH Fidelity team to evaluate program fidelity and make program-level corrections, as needed.
• Work with Performance Manager to implement performance metrics, review housing data systems, analyze program performance and communicate performance results to internal and external stakeholders.
• Assist with drafting legislation and representation at the agency level at professional, local, state, regional, or national meetings.
• Respond to agency, legislative, and audit requests for information.
• Make professional level decisions, recommendations, and provide program oversight.
• Identify and promote best business practices and efficient program designs.

PSH Training and Technical Assistance
Tasks include:
• Provide training and technical assistance on the evidence-based practice of PSH to developers, housing providers, and property managers throughout WA State.
• Contribute to the development of capital procurement applications or addendums, review and score capital PSH applications for the AHAH program in conjunction with other Housing Division units.
• Support projects that plan to apply for funds in the AHAH account to acquire or construct PSH projects and provide connection and linkage to additional pre-development technical assistance resources.
• Provide information and respond to technical assistance and data inquiries to internal and external agency partners.
• Represent and present information on PSH, the office of AHAH, Commerce services and resources at local, state, regional or national conferences.
• Support the development of legislative tracking and reporting by compiling data on training and technical assistance activities including the number, attendees, type, barriers/challenges and training topics.

Risk Assessment and Grantee Monitoring
Tasks include:
• Develop risk assessment and monitoring tools.
• Evaluate program activities and monitor grant compliance by reviewing program fiscal and service delivery to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
• Provide advanced technical level assistance and training to meet local agencies and program need and to ensure accountability for state funds.

Qualifications

Required Position Qualifications:
Seven (7) years of combined professional level experience and/or education that involves community, trade or economic development with a focus in implementing or providing PSH using the Substance Abuse Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) or equivalent model and:
o One (1) or more years (full-time equivalency) of professional-level experience must include developing and/or delivering training or presentations.

Lived experience with housing instability and/or experience navigating and receiving services from public systems such as homeless and housing services systems, foster care, the criminal legal system, or behavioral health system may substitute for one (1) year of education beyond high school equivalency and/or professional-level experience.
• What is lived experience? Lived experience is relevant expertise derived from the accumulated personal life and professional experiences of an individual. Experience can be gained through life events, volunteer role/capacity, any experience gained outside of professional paid and unpaid experience, academic or a combination of experiences.

Examples of how to qualify:
• 7 years of experience
• 6 years of experience and one year of lived experience
• 6 years of experience and one year of education
• 5 years of experience, one year of education, and one year of lived experience
• 5 years of experience and two years of education
• 4 years of experience and three years of education
• 3 years of experience and four years of education

Required Position Competencies:
• Ability to work well under stress and meet tight deadlines.
• Proficient verbal and written communication skills to clearly and succinctly document and describe processes, procedures, performance measures, and results.
• Ability to track, organize, and maintain individual workload timely and efficiently.
• Proven ability to collaborate and seek out and utilize diverse perspectives in program and policy development.
• Committed to continuous quality improvement on homeless housing program access and outcomes for people most impacted by homelessness.

Preferred/Desired Qualifications:
• Experience working in a policy, administrative, or direct service role to serve vulnerable individuals or individuals with disabling conditions experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
• Demonstrated high level of interpersonal communication skills — two way communication, information sharing, gathering, and using stakeholder feedback.
• Understanding of the intersection of race and gender as it relates to efforts to address homelessness.
• Understanding of the drivers of homelessness/chronic homelessness and the role of trauma and its impact on individuals experiencing housing instability.
• Experience in grants management, including monitoring budgets, developing grantee risk assessments, and/or performing compliance monitoring of contracts.
• High level experience using computer and web applications, such as Excel, Word, Internet Explorer, and other applications and databases.
• Strong ability to meet budget, grant, and reporting deadlines with high degree of accuracy.
• Strong understanding of interpreting, writing, and applying detailed policies and procedures.
• Experience analyzing data from homeless systems, ability to research, evaluate and draw conclusions from data and support recommendations with facts and analysis in alignment with rules, laws, policies and procedures.
• Research and Analytical Skills/Abilities: Ability to research, evaluate and draw conclusions from data from the Homeless Management Information System (or similar client-level databases); support recommendations with facts and analysis; interpret and apply rules, laws, policies and procedures
• Familiarity and/or experience with state contracting procedures and systems.
• Familiarity and/or experience working with or for Human Service oriented non-profit agencies.
• Knowledge of specific housing and fiscal data systems, such as the Department of Commerce’s Contracts Management System (CMS).

To be considered for this position the following are needed:

  • A complete and detailed online application.
  • A cover letter (enter online).
  • At least three professional references (enter online).
For questions about this recruitment, please contact our recruitment team via email: comrecruitment@commerce.wa.gov - please reference the job number in your message.

Supplemental Information

Work from Anywhere in Washington State
This position may be located anywhere within Washington State though occasional travel to a Commerce office building or in-state travel to attend events or meetings will be required. If selected, you will need to travel to pick up equipment and receive instruction. Many Commerce employees work remotely or have a hybrid schedule.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies over the next 60 days.

Technical support is provided by NEOGOV, 855-524-5627 (can't log in, password or email issues, error messages). DES job seeker support may answer general questions regarding the recruiting system at careershelp@des.wa.gov.

Our Commitment to Equal Opportunity
The Washington State Department of Commerce is an equal opportunity employer. We strive to create a working environment that includes and respects cultural, racial, ethnic, sexual orientation and gender identity diversity. Women, racial and ethnic minorities, persons of disability, persons over 40 years of age, veterans or people with military status, and people of all sexual orientations and gender identities are encouraged to apply. Persons needing accommodation in the application, testing, or interview process or this job announcement in an alternative format may email Human Resources at Human.Resources@commerce.wa.gov. Applicants who are deaf or hard of hearing may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 7-1-1 or 1-800-833-6388.

Department of Commerce also offers a competitive benefits package including: medical and dental insurance benefits, retirement and deferred compensation plans, 11 paid holidays each year, 14-25 vacation days per year (depending on length of employment), 8 hours of sick leave per month (if full time employed), bereavement leave, an employee assistance program, as well as other benefits. Please see the Benefits Tab for more details.

title: Quality Assurance Technician
description:

The Quality Assurance Department ensures all products and services meet internal standards, legal compliance, and customer expectations. The Quality Assurance Technician plays a critical role in this mission by performing receiving, in-process, first-article, and final inspections/audits using advanced measurement instruments and techniques. This role is also responsible for developing inspection methods, ensuring strict adherence to quality procedures, and assisting with collaborative problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives.

Essential Job Duties
  • Inspection & Auditing: Perform comprehensive receiving, first-article, in-process, and final inspections/audits to ensure compliance with The Specialty Manufacturing Company’s Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Measurement & Testing: Utilize manual measuring tools (micrometers, calipers) alongside advanced equipment (Keyence, Vertex, CMM) to gather precise data.
  • Defect Management: Identify, segregate, and formally report defective or out-of-specification materials to prevent them from advancing through production.
  • Documentation: Maintain precise, highly accurate written and electronic quality records.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engineering and Operations to identify root causes of defects and support Lean or continuous improvement projects.
  • Time Management: Prioritize tasks effectively to meet production deadlines in a timely, efficient manner.
  • General Support: Perform other quality-related duties as assigned by leadership.

Education & Experience
  • Required: High School diploma or GED.
  • Preferred: Associate degree in a technical field or a specialized Quality Technician certification.

Skills and Qualifications
  • Blueprint Reading: Ability to read and accurately interpret technical blueprints.
  • Technical Skills: Basic computer literacy and proficient math skills.
  • Autonomy: Proven self-starter capable of working productively with minimal supervision.
  • Soft Skills: Exceptional verbal/written communication, strong organizational habits, and meticulous attention to detail.
  • Attendance: Ability to maintain highly regular and predictable attendance on-site.
  • Preferred: Direct experience with CMM or Vision programming systems.
  • Preferred: Working knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).

Work Environment & Physical Requirements
  • Environment: Must be comfortable working full-time in a manufacturing setting with regular exposure to shop noise.
  • Pacing: Ability to stand continuously for up to four hours at a time.
  • Lifting: Ability to safely lift and move up to 50 lbs. regularly throughout the workday.
  • Schedule: All work must be performed on-site during normal The Specialty Manufacturing Company’s operational business hours.

Compensation and Benefits
Expected Compensation Range: Hourly, non-exempt- $22-$30
Specialty Manufacturing is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.
Specialty Mfg. provides a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings, focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. Specialty Mfg. operates an onsite work environment where employees are expected to work in the office 5 days per week.

title: Senior Software Engineer II, Managed Databases
description:

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer II to join our Managed Databases (DBaaS) engineering organization. Managed Databases delivers fully managed Postgres, MySQL, and related database services so customers can run production data workloads—and increasingly AI inference and data-intensive applications—without operating clusters themselves.

In this high-impact IC4 role, you will apply advanced subject-matter expertise across distributed control planes, database platform infrastructure, and production reliability. You will bridge product and system requirements with concrete architecture, lead complex technical projects across DBaaS and adjacent platform boundaries (e.g., Networking, Droplets, Storage, engine teams), and mentor engineers to elevate standards on the team. You should be comfortable independently moving from ambiguous problems to design, implementation, launch, and long-term operation.

What You’ll Do

  • Architect and implement DBaaS platform systems: Design and build scalable control-plane and infrastructure components that improve throughput, multi-region operability, and reliability for managed database workloads.
  • Turn ambiguous requirements into deliverable architecture: Deconstruct customer and system needs into clear technical designs and workstreams that drive predictable delivery with product and engineering partners.
  • Own performance and resiliency outcomes on your services: Improve resource utilization, fault tolerance, and availability—using profiling and targeted changes against I/O, CPU, and network bottlenecks under real production load.
  • Strengthen lifecycle capabilities: Ship improvements to automated failover, continuous backups, point-in-time recovery (PITR), and maintenance workflows so clusters handle higher data volumes and tighter SLAs.
  • Scale for data-heavy and AI-adjacent demand: Expand and harden control-plane and infrastructure pieces that support compute-heavy and high-concurrency customer workloads.
  • Raise the team engineering bar: Guide technical decisions for engineers on the squad through design and code reviews; contribute clear design docs for the initiatives you lead.
  • Mentor team members: Coach engineers through technical guidance, architectural reviews, and code-quality standards to accelerate growth and execution velocity.
  • Operate what you build: Establish observability, failover, and recovery practices; participate in on-call; turn incident learnings into durable platform improvements.

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience: 8+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems or data-plane/control-plane infrastructure (SaaS/PaaS or equivalent).
  • Production depth: Proven track record diagnosing and solving complex, high-concurrency engineering problems in production cloud environments.
  • Database platform fluency: Working knowledge of relational database engine internals—specifically PostgreSQL and/or MySQL—including query performance, replication, and scale (preferred).
  • Distributed systems mastery: Strong understanding of concurrency, failure modes, multi-region concerns, and performance optimization in production Linux/cloud environments.
  • Scale for data & AI workloads: Experience scaling services for compute, memory, and networking demands of data-intensive or AI inference-adjacent workloads (preferred).
  • Collaboration & mentorship: Track record of driving complex cross-team technical projects, mentoring engineers, and communicating tradeoffs clearly with partners and leadership.
  • Growth mindset: Appetite for feedback and a “leave it better than you found it” approach to architecture and maintainability.

Compensation Range:

title: Quality Technician
description:
Position Information

Job Title:

Department/Location:

Quality Technician - Cellulose

Quality/Montgomery

Reports To Title:

Work Schedule:

Quality Manager

Weekdays 40 hours per week + flexibility for additional work if required





Job Purpose

  • Ensures day to day quality in the Montgomery facility of Cellulose product, ensure correct measurement and disqualification criteria, make sure the product meets quality expectation and initiate quality improvement.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Daily check the information in OSP from ATL, Water Tester and FKM from previous day
  • Review all records and check if all was done according to the procedures, using correct frequency and specification.
  • Verify if incidents were solved properly and review with ATL, Water Tester or FKM operator if there are any possible error or doubts.
  • Daily visual inspection of the product on each machine in any shift.
  • Review material in hold, including low-quality records and partner with the Quality Manager to implement the appropriate action.
  • Responsible for organizing any inspection of Cellulose casing with quality issue(s).
  • Responsible for the general upkeep and re-order of Quality devices in his/her area.
  • Manages and coordinates resolutions for Cellulose claims and related analyses in a timely manner.
  • Synthesizes data from Cellulose claims, providing identification of possible root cause(s).
  • Partners interdepartmentally with key stakeholders to implement preventative and corrective actions related to quality initiatives.
  • Responsible for entering claim related findings and resulting corrective actions into NAVISION.
  • Analyzing Quality data, tendencies
  • Weekly and Monthly Reports required by Quality Manager.
  • Develops and presents respective Claims Presentation for their responsible product family.
  • Responsible for the Cellulose additives room general upkeep, and inventory.
  • Responsible for coordinating and issuing schedule for respective area.
  • Provides staffing coverage within department as needed or requested by the Quality Manager.
  • Any other duties as assigned by the Quality Manager.

Qualifications


Education:

Bachelor's degree is preferred, but not required, in some engineering fields, such as industrial engineering, chemical engineering, etc.


Experience

2 years of experience in Quality areas, with knowledge of quality inspection and quality rejections.

Skills

  • Basic management in MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Basic knowledge of lab equipment and methods, basic knowledge of ISO system
  • Languages: Bilingual (English and Spanish) required (oral and written fluency).
  • Strong communication skills
  • Ability to find root cause of problem, Analytical abilities
  • Strong control of the process, good organization, and growth mindset
  • Other characteristics such as personal characteristics – responsible, high accuracy, resilient.


Competencies

  • Communication
  • Adaptability
  • Problem Solving
  • Teamwork


Working Conditions

Within the production facility the environment is controlled. There are times that require inside and outside working so ups and downs in temperature are normal. Must follow all safety regulations at all facilities and wear all proper safety equipment. Steel toe shoes, hearing protection, safety glasses, and goggles are required in certain areas of the plant. The facility is also a BRC food and food packaging facility so all requirements of the BRC must be followed.


Physical Requirements

Must be able to spend a considerable amount of time working on the production floor among a variety of different machines/chemical and physical laboratory. Work on feet for long periods of time. Some lifting required. Must be aware of your surroundings at all times. Must be willing to work in wet environments doing testing when necessary


Direct Reports

  • 4 Cellulose ATLs, 1 Consolidation ATL and 3 Cellulose Water Testers

This position is classified as Exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and is compensated on a salaried basis. title: Lead, Leadership Programs
description:
Overview
We have an exciting opportunity for a Lead, Leadership Programs. Reporting to the Director, Talent Strategy and Programs this role is responsible for the development, implementation, and continuous evolution of enterprise leadership talent strategies and programs. This role is located in Calgary and will operate as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and the HR team. The role leads strategic initiatives related to cross-functional mobility, succession planning and development, career progression, accelerated leadership development, and high-potential talent readiness in service of delivering on our business plan.
The role is accountable for designing and advancing integrated leadership talent practices that support the organization's current and future workforce needs. Using talent insights, workforce data, and best practices, the Senior Advisor identifies opportunities to strengthen leadership readiness, mitigate talent risks, and support business continuity. The position contributes directly to organizational talent outcomes by ensuring leadership talent strategies are aligned with organizational priorities and capable of supporting long-term growth and transformation.

Accountabilities
Organizational Leadership Strategy
Leads the development and implementation of leadership talent strategies that support organizational objectives and future workforce requirements. Identifies emerging leadership capability needs, assesses organizational readiness, and develops initiatives that strengthen how we prepare our leaders to lead through change. Partners with senior leaders and HR stakeholders to align leadership talent investments with business priorities and long-term organizational goals.
Succession Planning & Leadership Governance
Provides strategic leadership for senior leadership succession planning practices, frameworks, and processes. Monitors organizational bench strength, succession readiness, and critical role coverage while identifying opportunities for cross-functional movement, key risks and recommending mitigation strategies.
Leadership Pipeline & Talent Acceleration
Designs and implements strategies that identify, develop, and accelerate high-potential talent into future leadership roles. Oversees leadership pipeline health through the evaluation of talent flow, readiness, mobility, and development outcomes. Develops approaches that strengthen leadership depth and support the organization's ability to meet its performance objectives.
Leadership Development Programs
Leads the strategic design, build, and delivery of leadership development frameworks, programs, and experiences that build organizational leadership capability. Collaborates with training, broader talent management, HR business partners, and business leaders to establish leadership competencies, development pathways, and targeted interventions that support leader growth at all levels. Facilitates leadership programs as needed and evaluates program effectiveness and recommends enhancements to maximize business impact and participant outcomes.
Leadership Insights
Utilizes leadership talent data, workforce data and market trends to assess leadership pipeline health and organizational capability. Develops meaningful metrics, dashboards, and reporting tools that support decision-making and provide visibility into succession outcomes, leadership readiness, diversity within leadership pipelines, retention of key talent, and program effectiveness. Translates data into actionable recommendations for leaders and executives.
Stakeholder Consulting & Enterprise Influence
Acts as a trusted advisor to leaders, HR Business Partners, and executive stakeholders on matters related to leadership talent strategy, succession planning, talent development, and organizational capability. Influences decision-making through expertise, credibility, and evidence-based recommendations. Builds strong partnerships across the organization to drive alignment, adoption, and successful execution of talent initiatives.
Continuous Improvement & Innovation
Research emerging trends, leading practices, and innovative approaches in talent management, leadership development, succession planning, and workforce strategy. Recommends and implements enhancements that improve organizational effectiveness, strengthen leadership capability, and position the organization for future success.

Skills & Attributes

Demonstrated ability to think strategically, beyond immediate talent needs and develop long-term strategies that support organizational objectives and future requirements.

Strong understanding of organizational drivers, business priorities, headwinds, and the relationship between talent decisions and business performance.

Ability to build credibility and influence decisions at senior leadership levels through consultation, facilitation, data, and subject matter expertise.

Deep knowledge of leadership development, succession planning, talent reviews, career management, workforce planning, high-potential programs, and organizational capability development.

Ability to synthesize data, talent metrics, and external trends into meaningful insights that support strategic decision-making.

Skilled at leading complex discussions, facilitation, managing diverse stakeholder perspectives, and achieving alignment across organizational groups.

Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to establish trusted partnerships across all levels of the organization.

Demonstrated ability to challenge traditional approaches, identify opportunities for improvement, and implement innovative talent solutions.

Experience & Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Psychology, or related discipline.

Minimum 8-10 years of progressive experience in talent management, talent strategy, leadership development, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, or a related field.

Demonstrated experience designing and leading enterprise-wide talent management or leadership development initiatives.

Experience facilitating talent reviews, succession planning discussions, and leadership assessment processes with senior leaders.

Experience developing talent strategies informed by workforce analytics, organizational priorities, and future capability requirements.

Strong understanding of leadership development methodologies, talent identification practices, career pathing frameworks, and succession management principles.

Experience managing complex projects involving multiple stakeholders and organizational priorities.

Proven ability to influence strategic decisions without formal authority.

Experience working with executive leaders and providing consultation on talent-related matters.

Professional designation such as CPHR, CHRL, PCC, or related credentials would be considered an asset.

title: Commercial Excellence Coordinator
description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

As Training & Enablement Coordinator, you will be instrumental in organizing and delivering the training programs, logistics, and reporting that support Heartflow's Commercial Enablement, Strategic Sales, and Sales Training & Development functions. You will be a key contributor to the success of these teams by ensuring stakeholders — including VP-level leaders across commercial functions — have timely logistics, accurate reporting, and up-to-date content and platform support.

The ideal candidate is motivated, self-directed, and highly detailed. You will serve as the operational engine for the department — supporting the full lifecycle of training and enablement programs (including New Hire, Regional, and National events), overseeing software licenses, providing high-level support for content creation and multimedia, and pulling together the analytics and reporting that VP stakeholders across the three functions rely on to track progress.

Commercial Excellence Operations & Logistics

  • End-to-End Coordination: Partner with Commercial Enablement, Strategic Sales, and Sales Training & Development leaders to plan and execute a variety of programs and initiatives, including New Hire onboarding, Regional workshops, and National events. Provide on-site support for live classes and meetings as required.
  • Travel & Operations: Coordinate in-person and virtual meeting logistics — registration, travel, hotels, meeting space, catering, printing/shipping, and post-meeting surveys.
  • Executive Support: Provide light-touch calendaring, travel coordination, and expense report support for Commercial VP stakeholders as needed.
  • Communications Hub: Proactively manage the department inbox, triaging requests and providing timely communication and support to stakeholders — including VP-level leaders — across commercial functions.

Financial & Vendor Administration

  • Invoice & PO Management: Own the end-to-end purchase order process. Manage supplier approvals, initiate POs for new projects, and collect, submit, and track payments to vendors to ensure timely execution.
  • Expense Reporting: Submit, track, and report on all expenses related to educational events, ensuring accuracy and budget compliance.
  • License Management: Maintain and oversee licenses for our various platforms (ex: ACTO, Richardson, Canva). Ensure user seats are optimized, renewals are tracked, and the team has uninterrupted access to necessary software.

Platform & Data Support

  • Reporting & KPIs: Pull utilization and performance reports across Commercial Enablement, Strategic Sales, and Sales Training & Development, and package the data into clear, executive-ready summaries for VP stakeholders. Create and analyze post-meeting surveys to provide suggestions for program improvement.

Content & Multimedia Contribution

  • Content Support: Assist with the iteration of commercial-facing materials to ensure they remain up-to-date, clinically relevant, and brand / priority-aligned. Provide design support as needed for resources, presentations, and training collateral.
  • Video Production: Utilize Canva and video editing tools to create and edit high-level instructional content, meeting recaps, and training assets.

Skills & Background

  • Experience: 2–3 years supporting sales, marketing, or educational programs.
  • Operational Precision: Highly detail-oriented with a track record of managing logistics for multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Financial Aptitude: Experienced with the PO/invoice lifecycle, expense tracking, and vendor license management.
  • Analytical Aptitude: Comfortable pulling, organizing, and synthesizing data from multiple systems into clear reporting that a VP-level audience can act on quickly.
  • Technical Toolkit: Expert in Google Suite and MS Office (including Excel/Sheets for basic data analysis and reporting); proficient in Canva.
  • Communication: Strong ability to manage a department inbox, draft team communications, and collaborate cross-functionally, including with senior and VP-level stakeholders across multiple functions.
  • Self-Direction: A proactive problem-solver who can work independently and adapt to changing priorities and learn new technical tools and skills quickly to scale with business needs.
  • Education: BA/BS in Business, Communications, or a related field.

The base compensation range for this role is $60,000 – $75,000 depending on experience and geographic location. This role is also eligible for an annual bonus.

  • Design, build and maintain software and platform capabilities that power Fastly’s internal observability function and developer experience
  • Contribute to the development of our internal developer portal, helping engineering teams discover services, documentation, and operational tooling all in one place
  • Work with your team to break down project requirements into concrete tasks, and take ownership of your assigned work through to completion
  • Debug and resolve issues across the software stack, from datacenter hardware to the browser, often spanning multiple services and data sources
  • Communicate clearly about the status of your work and any problems you encounter. Write useful updates, ask good questions, and raise issues early rather than at the deadline
  • Collaborate with other engineers on the team. Provide thoughtful code review and share context and knowledge.
  • Participate constructively in team planning and retrospectives
  • Participate in on-call rotation as required, and respond to incidents within the team's SLA while on-call.

What We're Looking For:

Technical skills:

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with demonstrated ability to deliver quality work on reasonably well-defined projects with limited oversight
  • Experience in a statically typed, modern back-end language (Go, Java, Rust, etc.)
  • Experience in modern front-end frameworks (React, etc.), or a willingness to dive in and become proficient
  • Experience with SQL and database-driven applications
  • Experience working with Linux systems and the shell
  • Experience working with distributed systems or cloud-based services, and an interest in developing deeper expertise in operating and debugging them
  • Comfort with large and unfamiliar codebases: jumping into a system you didn't build, figuring out the context, and contributing with confidence. Our stack is broad, and you will regularly work in code you haven't seen before, including code written at Fastly and open-source codebases.
  • Strong debugging skills: forming hypotheses and narrowing down causes methodically. You’re willing to step outside your primary area of expertise to get to the bottom of something.

Ways of working:

  • Clear, thoughtful writing and communication. You understand that a precise Slack message, a well-written pull request description, or a clear explanation to a teammate is just as important as the code itself.
  • A service mindset. The people who use our tools depend on them to do their jobs. You care about their experience, you're approachable when they have questions, and you follow through and close the communication loop
  • A proactive disposition. You take ownership of your responsibilities. When you finish a task, you look for the next useful thing. When you see something that could be better, you say so.
  • Comfort working within lightweight agile processes. You participate constructively in planning and retrospectives, and you see team rituals as tools for coordination, productivity, and collaboration.
  • A desire to grow in your skills, knowledge, and scope. Enthusiasm for learning new technologies.

We’ll be super impressed if you have experience in any of these:

  • Backstage or other internal developer portal frameworks, open-source software in general
  • Enterprise-scale observability systems (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, Datadog, ELK, or similar
  • Cloud platforms (AWS/GCP), orchestration (Kubernetes), infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, Ansible, Chef)
  • Data science and data engineering, capacity planning, cost modeling, or FinOps practices
  • Network protocols and infrastructure, datacenter infrastructure, physical server administration
  • Training, teaching, or developing documentation and educational materials for internal tools

Work Hours:

This position will require you to be available during core business hours. It may also require occasional nights and weekends as necessary to support any on-call coverage.

Work Location(s) & Travel Requirements:

This position is open to Hybrid And Remote Work Locations.

The preferred locations for this position are:

  • San Francisco, CA
  • New York, NY

Fastly currently embraces a largely hybrid model for most roles which allows employees flexibility to split their time between the office and home.

There is a strong preference for Hybrid near a local office. However, we may be willing to consider remote candidates within the US.

This position may require travel as required by your role or requested by your manager.

SF / LA Fair Chance Ordinance Statement

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Salary:

The estimated salary range for this position is $155,370 to $186,444.

Starting salary may vary based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

This role may be eligible to participate in Fastly’s equity and discretionary bonus programs.

Benefits:

We care about you. Fastly works hard to create a positive environment for our employees, and we think your life outside of work is important too. We support our teams with great benefits that start on the first day of your employment with Fastly. Curious about our offerings?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance. Family planning, mental health support along with Employee Assistance Program, Insurance (Life, Disability, and Accident), a Flexible Vacation policy and up to 18 days of accrued paid sick leave are there to help support our employees. We also offer 401(k) (including company match) and an Employee Stock Purchase Program. For 2026, we offer 12 paid local holidays, 12 paid company wellness days.

Why Fastly?

  • We have a huge impact. Fastly is a small company with a big reach. Not only do our customers have a tremendous user base, but we also support a growing number of open source projects and initiatives. Outside of code, employees are encouraged to share causes close to their heart with others so we can help lend a supportive hand.

  • We value diversity. Growing and maintaining our inclusive and diverse team matters to us. We are committed to being a company where our employees feel comfortable bringing their authentic selves to work and have the ability to be successful -- every day.

  • We are passionate. Fastly is chock full of passionate people and we’re not ‘one size fits all’. Fastly employs authors, pilots, skiers, parents (of humans and animals), makeup geeks, coffee connoisseurs, and more. We love employees for who they are and what they are passionate about.

We’re always looking for humble, sharp, and creative folks to join the Fastly team. If you think you might be a fit please apply! A fully completed application and resume or CV are required when applying.

All job applications must be submitted through our official careers site at www.fastly.com/about/careers. title: Value Engineering Intern (Spring Semester 2027)
description:
Relay is the Intelligent System of Action for the physical economy. While the digital revolution has often left the deskless workforce behind, we are closing that gap by transforming analog frontline operations into a data-rich, AI-powered ecosystem. We aren't just selling radios, we're building the digital foundation for the 80% of the global workforce that doesn't work at a desk.

Why Join Relay?

  • A Proven Winner: Join a hyper-growth company trusted by over 10% of the Fortune 500, continuing to move upmarket with massive impact.
  • High Value, High Impact: With 47% of our revenue from $100K+ ARR customers and 135% Net Revenue Retention (NRR), you'll be joining a company rooted in value creation.
  • Market-Leading Innovation: The Relay platform captures 1 billion new data points weekly and features award-winning AI tools like TeamTranslate™, with 500% YoY growth.
  • World-Class Leadership: Our stellar leadership team is built to help us scale toward our next major milestones.
  • The Relay Culture: We're dedicated to helping you do the best work of your life (BWIML), investing in your growth, living out our CHASE values, and learning from talented teammates who make the work and the wins better every day.

Now, here's what we're building, and where you come in.

About the Role

Value Engineering at Relay is the bridge between frontline operational reality and enterprise investment decisions. Our Value Engineers parachute into a prospect's world, learn how they operate, and build the financial case that proves Relay's ROI at the C-suite level. This is analytical, customer-facing, high-stakes work. This internship puts you in the middle of it.

The Value Engineering Internship is a two-phase opportunity: a Spring semester engagement (January start, part-time) that potentially feeds into a full-time 40-hour/week Summer internship for top performers. Both phases are on-site at Relay's world-class Raleigh HQ, located near the Lenovo Center.

Strong performance creates a pathway to a return offer for a Summer or Fall 2027 internship and full-time consideration upon graduation, based on business needs.

You'll work directly with our Manager, Value Engineering, and the broader GTM org. This includes Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and senior leadership — on live enterprise deals.

About the Team

The Value Engineering team exists to close two critical gaps: leadership isn't always in touch with the factory floor, and new technology doesn't always translate into operational impact. We bridge both by quantifying Relay's value proposition, building investment-grade business cases, and acting as a forcing function for customer ROI. Our work shapes the enterprise sales motion, customer relationships, product roadmap, and company strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Support the development of executive-level business cases that translate frontline operational data into P&L-level ROI.
  • Map prospect workflows and analyze operational metrics to identify Relay's highest-impact use cases.
  • Build financial models that quantify the value Relay delivers across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, and healthcare.
  • Partner with AEs and CSMs on pilot strategies and account planning for key enterprise opportunities.
  • Conduct research on industry operations and competitive benchmarks to strengthen Relay's value narratives.
  • Assist in developing internal tools, ROI frameworks, and proofs-of-concept that scale across the sales org.
  • Synthesize customer and field insights to support product roadmap and pricing strategy conversations.
  • Contribute to the company's wildly well-attended intern showcase — presenting your work to Relay's full team at summer's end.

Required Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field.
  • Expected graduation between December 2027 and May 2029.
  • Minimum GPA of 3.7
  • No employer work authorization sponsorship available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship, now or in the future.
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building models and working with data.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication — ability to synthesize complexity into a clear, executive-ready narrative.
  • Available to work onsite at Relay's Raleigh HQ (near the Lenovo Center) for both the Spring engagement and the full-time Summer program.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework or project experience in operations research, systems engineering, supply chain, or financial analysis.
  • Exposure to manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, or hospitality environments through coursework, co-op, or personal experience.
  • Familiarity with data analysis tools (Excel, Python, SQL) and/or data visualization.
  • A genuine curiosity about how physical-world businesses operate and where technology creates real impact.

What success and impact look like in this role

By the end of the Spring engagement, you've shipped at least one analysis or framework that's been used in a live enterprise deal. By mid-summer, you're running financial models and contributing to business cases with real ownership — not just support. By the final showcase, you've presented work that a senior leader would put in front of a Fortune 500 prospect.

Top performers earn a return Summer or Fall 2027 internship offer and are on the radar for full-time consideration upon graduation.

What Makes This Internship Different

  • Executive exposure: Regular touchpoints with Relay's senior leadership team, including Q&A sessions, Breakfast with the CEO, and working sessions.
  • Real ownership: You'll own a project from kickoff to final presentation — not a shadow assignment.
  • Cross-functional cohort: Work alongside interns from across the business, not just your team.
  • Structured learning: Skill-building sessions covering financial modeling, operations strategy, sales craft, and professional development.
  • Intern showcase: Present your work to the full company at the end of the summer.
  • Raleigh HQ experience: Team lunches, volunteer Intern Impact Day, social events, and a front-row seat to how a scaling tech company operates.
  • Pathway that matters: This isn't a résumé builder for its own sake. Strong performers get return offers and full-time pipeline consideration.

Why Join Relay?

Our culture hinges on Relayers getting LIT up in an environment that fosters Learning, Impact, and Teamwork, where we CHASE the best work of our lives. BWIML - Best Work In My Life.

The future of frontline work is being built here. Come build it with us. We can't wait to hear from you.

Transcripts are accessible only to authorized hiring personnel and retained consistent with our data retention policies. Candidates who prefer not to have AI notetaking used may request to opt out without impact to your candidacy. For more information, please see our Candidate and Employee Privacy Notice linked here.

title: Research Coordinator
description:
The Hennepin Healthcare Research Institute's (HHRI) Restorative Neurotrauma Lab has a current opening for an experienced Research Coordinator to support the research being conducted by Drs. David Darrow and Sam Cramer in the Division of Neurosurgery at HCMC.

This role requires a consistent onsite presence in downtown Minneapolis, MN.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Research Coordinator will assist with study management, coordination, teaching, overseeing research, and patient recruitment. Systemically coordinate and organize protocols while maintaining communication with Institutional review Board as well as the FDA regarding IDE/IND process. Routinely coordinate daily activities associated with administering sponsored and non-sponsored research projects. Aid in grant application and accurately reconcile grant accounts. Manage hardware and software needed for research projects. Assist with submission of grant proposals, abstracts, and publications. Work with collaborators (across external academic institutions) and research staff (within HCMC/HHRI) to coordinate ongoing research projects and develop new projects.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Responsible for managing tasks associated with participant screening, recruitment, and engagement in research projects, which includes, but is not limited to:
    • Determining participant eligibility
    • Recruitment
    • Tracking enrollment dates and key patient milestones
    • Coordinates/conducts research participant testing and follow-up.
    • Completing and securely storing paperwork
    • Collects data in an organized and precise fashion and maintains data integrity
    • Coordinates multiple data collection efforts for one or more research projects which may include other collaborating agencies or institutions.
    • Orient, train or teach, and give work direction to new researchers on the project
  • Coordinate studies across collaborators
  • Act as a resource to other staff regarding study protocol and interpretations
  • Responsible for regulatory compliance in conjunction with the PI by providing study materials requested including, but are not limited to:
    • Develop and maintain project materials (e.g., patient database, case report forms, study worksheets, tracking logs, IRB required forms, etc.)
    • Accurately write and revise clinical protocols, consents, and other supporting documents
    • Assist the Principal Investigator with reaching project milestones and resource allocation to assure successful study conduct
    • Oversee progress and assure milestones are met for the research activities conducted by collaborators at external academic institutions
    • Organize, and coordinate meetings, conference calls, and training sessions
    • Management of patient advisory group
    • Consult with the Principal Investigator and co-investigators on appropriate management of participant problems and concerns.
    • Write and edit technical reports and manuscripts for publication or presentation.
    • IRB (submissions and renewals)
    • FDA IDE/IND processes
    • Create reports as mandated by sponsor/funder and manage digital log viewable by PI
  • Monitor fiscal and administrative activities satisfying guidelines established by both the institution and various funding agencies.
    • Preparation of budgets
    • Review/approve expenditures
    • Invoice submission
    • Budget/expenditure reconciliation
    • Supply orders
    • W-9 monitoring for study subjects
    • Liaison between the project team and funding agencies or significant parties.
    • Accurately reconcile grant accounts
  • Guide proposals through inception to submission stages. Plan future proposal submissions
    • Assist with submission of new grant proposals by completing funding agency forms
    • Collaborate with HHRI grant administration.
    • Works with other members of the research team on research design and problem solving.
  • Aid in the planning and writing of grants, abstracts, and publications.

EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS:

Education/Experience:

Any equivalent combination of education and experience that provides the required knowledge and skills is qualifying. Typical qualifications would be a baccalaureate degree and one to three (1-3) years of experience with the specified research field. Experience with electronic medical records (EPIC), regulatory documentation, writing and preparing grant proposals and managing research budgets, preferred. Experience implementing clinical research protocols, recruiting patients for research studies, data gathering, and maintaining research data.

Skill, Knowledge & Ability (SKA):

Requires interaction with a diverse population. Must demonstrate working knowledge of MS Office including: databases, spreadsheets (including pivot tables, basic statistical analysis, etc.), and word processing. Knowledge of research design, protocols, and analysis; knowledge of regulatory aspects of clinical research. Ability to work independently within guidelines, be organized, prioritize work effort in relation to project requirements. Skilled in problem solving and keeping detailed records and files. Effective written and oral communication skills. Displays high standards of attendance, punctuality, maintains confidentiality, and manages time effectively. Required skills includes: Self-motivated and ability to work independently.

Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Software Engineer, New Grad - Super Day!
description:
About Us:

Perpay is a certified B Corp and Philadelphia’s most impactful growth-stage startup. We are driven by a mission to significantly improve the financial stability of everyday Americans. For the past decade, we have established strong product-market fit and a profitable, efficient operating model across a suite of products, positioning Perpay as the premier financial partner for consumers with subprime credit.

With over 500,000 customers who have utilized more than $1 billion in spending power, we are at a pivotal moment. We are scaling our operations, building new offerings, and deepening our impact. We are looking for teammates eager to join us on this journey.

Our venture partners include First Round Capital and L Catterton.

Products we’ve built to make an impact:

  • Perpay Marketplace: Combines interest-free payments and modern e-commerce to reduce cost of ownership and promote healthy repayment behavior.
  • Perpay+: Leverages Marketplace repayment history to help members monitor and build credit with all 3 credit bureaus.
  • Perpay Credit Card: Expands access to the flexibility and benefits of a World Mastercard by removing common barriers like high security deposits and low approval odds.

Our team thrives on in-person collaboration, operating from our unique center-city Philadelphia office. This comfortable "home away from home" space offers river views and fosters rapid product development, strong relationships, and career growth. The energy from achieving big wins is palpable here. While we primarily work in the office, we offer sensible flexibility for personal needs, such as sick children or urgent errands, and coordinate official remote weeks around major holidays. If you are passionate about a meaningful mission, collaboration, equity, and generous perks, Perpay is the best place to be in Philadelphia right now.

This is a 🚀 Super Day Hiring Event 🚀 specific job posting.

What is Super Day?

It's an accelerated hiring event that will give recent graduates the unique opportunity to land this role in just one day! We will host it on November 12th at Perpay HQ in Philadelphia. Selected candidates will tour the office, meet the team, and experience a fast-tracked interview process. Attendance is invite-only, and applicants must complete all pre-work steps to be considered. Launch your career by applying below! *Application Deadline: November 2nd.

About the Role:

We are looking for motivated graduates (or equivalent experience) to join our Software Engineering team! You’ll contribute to our codebase, test & release features into production, and collaborate with other teams like product, design, data science, analytics, and operations. The ideal candidate has software development internship experience and is enthusiastic about learning and growing! We're particularly interested in working with candidates excited about joining a mission-driven startup. On our team, you’ll sharpen your skills, learn new tools alongside other new graduates, and learn from experienced engineers. Plus, our team organizes events and social gatherings outside of work hours. We believe having a fun and engaging work environment is essential to fostering a positive company culture and creating a strong foundation for career growth.

Much of our team is full-stack, so we look for team members excited to learn new technologies and work across all stacks, even if it’s not something you’ve done before! Our tech stack: JavaScript, React, React Native, Redux, Python, Django, Kubernetes, AWS, Docker, Terraform, and more.

Our greatest strength is our people, and we’d love for you to be one of them!

Responsibilities:

  • Develop, test, and release features for our customer-facing and internal platforms alongside the engineering team
  • Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to develop efficient and user-friendly solutions to support the complex needs of our business
  • Actively participate in design reviews, code reviews, and discussions to improve our software architecture and implement efficient processes within our engineering team

What You’ll Bring:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree or higher, or a recent graduate studying Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)
  • 1 to 2 previous Software Engineering internships with a focus on full-stack software development
  • Experience with at least one backend application framework such as Django or Flask
  • Experience with frontend technologies such as React, Angular, or Vue.js
  • Knowledge of RESTful API design and integration

title: Principal Technical Program Manager
location: New York, NY; Silicon Valley, CA
description:
Our Mission

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting. We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your Impact to the Mission

Zocdoc's most important asset is our people. As a Principal Technical Program Manager for Practice Solutions, you will own and drive the most complex, cross-functional technical programs across the business unit, the initiatives that span multiple engineering teams and product domains and that no single team can deliver alone. Practice Solutions powers how healthcare practices run their day to day across every patient access channel: phone, web, marketplace, and partner syndication. That includes Zo, our AI phone assistant, along with our provider directory and booking platform, intake and pre-appointment workflows, calendar and scheduling experiences, and the services that keep availability accurate across channels. You'll operate at the intersection of Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, and go-to-market leadership to deliver scalable, highly available, multi-tenant SaaS capabilities. You'll bring structure to ambiguity, drive sequencing across teams, surface architectural and operational risk early, and keep the trains running on time, all while raising the bar for how program execution happens across the entire business unit. This is a highly visible role with significant autonomy and influence.

You'll enjoy this role if you are…

  • Inspired by the opportunity to positively impact the healthcare experience for millions of patients and providers
  • A platform thinker who instinctively looks beyond individual features to understand how systems connect, scale, and evolve over time
  • Energized by building structure in ambiguous, high-complexity environments where multiple teams, products, and priorities intersect
  • Comfortable operating at both 30,000 feet and in the architectural details, able to reason about distributed systems, reliability tradeoffs, and multi-tenant SaaS constraints
  • Unafraid to drive movement and accountability at every level of the organization, regardless of title or tenure
  • Calm and decisive in high-stakes situations, especially when sequencing work across teams with shared platform dependencies
  • A strong influencer who can align engineering leaders, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders around shared outcomes even when ownership boundaries are unclear
  • A believer that diverse and inclusive teams and cultures are non-negotiable

Your day to day is…

  • Organizing and driving the business unit's planning cadence, coordinating inputs and stakeholders across engineering and product and keeping the cycle on track so strategy turns into a clear, committed, sequenced roadmap
  • Leading large, multi-quarter platform initiatives that span the Practice Solutions product scope, keeping each part on schedule and the whole program moving
  • Translating high-level business and product goals into structured program plans with clear sequencing, milestones, dependencies, and measurable outcomes
  • Building the reporting and transparency that give leadership a clear, honest view of status, dependencies, and risk
  • Partnering closely with senior engineering leaders to anticipate architectural and operational risks before they surface in production
  • Digging into technical issues at the seams between teams, triaging, framing the problem clearly, and pulling the right architects and engineers together to solve it
  • Surfacing tradeoffs between speed, scope, reliability, and technical debt, and facilitating clear, well-reasoned decisions at the right level
  • Clarifying ownership boundaries and reducing cross-team friction where systems, incentives, or customer journeys overlap
  • Establishing and refining lightweight mechanisms that improve transparency, accountability, and long-term platform health
  • Communicating program status, risks, and key decisions clearly to executive stakeholders and business unit leadership

You'll be successful in this role if you have…

  • A strong bias to action and an ownership mentality
  • 8+ years in Technical Program Management, Engineering Program Management, or a similar technical leadership role
  • A track record delivering large-scale, cross-functional initiatives in a product-led SaaS environment
  • A strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud architectures (AWS or equivalent), and event-driven systems
  • Demonstrated ability to reason about architectural tradeoffs without owning implementation, and enough technical depth to hold your own in a room full of senior engineers
  • Experience driving programs that span multiple engineering teams with shared platform dependencies
  • The confidence to drive accountability and momentum across all levels of an organization without relying on formal authority
  • Excellent communication skills, including clear written status and risk framing for both engineers and executives
  • A Bachelor's degree in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems) or equivalent practical experience
  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated, multi-tenant domain is a plus
  • Humility. You believe in treating all people with dignity and respect, regardless of title or tenure, and you approach tough conversations with empathy

Benefits:

  • Flexible, hybrid work environment at our convenient Soho location
  • Unlimited Vacation
  • 100% paid employee health benefit options (including medical, dental, and vision)
  • Commuter Benefits
  • 401(k) with employer funded match
  • Corporate wellness program with Wellhub
  • Sabbatical leave (for employees with 5+ years of service)
  • Competitive paid parental leave and fertility/family planning reimbursement
  • Cell phone reimbursement
  • Catered lunch everyday along with beverages and snacks
  • Employee Resource Groups and ZocClubs to promote shared community and belonging

Zocdoc is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Salary ranges are determined through alignment with market data. Base salary offered is determined by a number of factors including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skills. Certain positions are also eligible for variable pay and/or equity; your recruiter will discuss the full compensation package details.
NYC Base Salary Range
$195,000—$250,000 USD

About us
Zocdoc is the country’s leading digital health marketplace that helps patients easily find and book the care they need. Each month, millions of patients use our free service to find nearby, in-network providers, compare choices based on verified patient reviews, and instantly book in-person or video visits online. Providers participate in Zocdoc’s Marketplace to reach new patients to grow their practice, fill their last-minute openings, and deliver a better healthcare experience. Founded in 2007 with a mission to give power to the patient, our work each day in pursuit of that mission is guided by our six core values. Zocdoc is a private company backed by some of the world’s leading investors, and we believe we’re still only scratching the surface of what we plan to accomplish.

Zocdoc is a mission-driven organization dedicated to building teams as diverse as the patients and providers we aim to serve. In the spirit of one of our core values - Together, Not Alone, we are a company that prides itself on being highly collaborative, and we believe that diverse perspectives, experiences and contributors make our community and our platform better. We’re an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Applicants are considered for employment regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or any other class protected by applicable laws.

Company Summary

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.


Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.


Backed by deep engineering expertise and large-scale manufacturing capability, Stellar Energy helps customers deploy critical infrastructure faster and with confidence.

Summary Objective

The Program Manager is responsible for leading the successful execution and coordination of complex customer (hyperscalers) programs involving multiple manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and cross-functional teams. This role will lead the coordination between Project Management, Product Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Scheduling, Supply Chain, Logistics, and Aftermarket Services to ensure Customer’s projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with customer expectations. The Program Manager drives financial performance, communication, manages project risks, improves operational processes, and ensures alignment across internal stakeholders while supporting Stellar Energy's commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction.

Essential Functions

  • Lead the on budget and on schedule execution and coordination of complex customer programs involving multiple manufacturing locations, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Manage customer relationship throughout the project execution lifecycle, maintaining a clear understanding of project scope, schedules, technical requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams including Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Scheduling, Logistics, Procurement, Project Management, and Aftermarket Services to ensure project milestones and deliverables are achieved.
  • Develop and maintain project execution plans while monitoring progress against established schedules, internal financial goals, and customer commitments. Identify financial and schedule project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and proactively resolve issues impacting project execution or customer delivery.
  • Collaborate with Aftermarket and Service organizations to ensure service requirements are aligned with customer needs. Establish standardized work processes that improve coordination across manufacturing locations and support consistent project execution.
  • Drive communication across internal stakeholders by facilitating project meetings, providing status updates, and escalating issues when necessary.
  • Monitor project performance metrics and recommend process improvements that enhance execution efficiency and customer satisfaction.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on project coordination, supply chain integration, and operational excellence.
  • Build strong working relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal business partners to ensure successful project outcomes.


Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position will have direct supervisory responsibilities but is responsible for leading cross-functional teams and influencing project execution across multiple departments.
