  4. Final interview with our CEO - virtual (30 minutes)
  5. Offer & Onboarding 🎉
Please note that this process is subject to change at any point, based on additional requirements from the team.

Why join Stay22?
  • Prime Montreal Location: Work from our vibrant Little Italy HQ with a cafeteria allowance, full gym access, and a rooftop terrace complete with a seasonal basketball/pickleball court & hockey rink.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Health & dental coverage, RRSP matching, fully paid STM pass’, and regular team socials, events, and retreats.
  • Flexibility That Works: Flexible schedules, work-from-anywhere opportunities, year-end shutdown, and flex days.

(Stay22 is an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants are given consideration. If you have a disability or particular need that requires accommodation, please contact us at careers@stay22.com)

Your application will be reviewed by Nayo, our internal recruiter- even if you don’t meet every requirement but you’re excited, let’s talk.

__________________________________

À propos de Stay22

Basée à Montréal, Stay22 aide les créateurs ambitieux et les plateformes numériques à forte intention à transformer leur trafic existant en revenus additionnels, grâce à une technologie qui fonctionne discrètement en arrière-plan.

Aujourd’hui, plus de 6 500 créateurs et plateformes font confiance à Stay22, avec plus d’un milliard de dollars en transactions annuelles transitant par la plateforme. Initialement conçue pour le secteur du voyage, l’entreprise accompagne désormais des partenaires dans les domaines du commerce de détail, du lifestyle, de l’édition, des événements et du transport, alors qu’elle poursuit l’expansion de son infrastructure de monétisation pour l’économie moderne des créateurs.

À propos du poste

Nous cherchons un·e développeur·euse possédant une solide expérience DevOps et SRE, qui se joindra à notre équipe Plateforme en pleine croissance. Tu seras responsable de concevoir, de mettre en œuvre et de maintenir l'infrastructure de base d'une plateforme afin de soutenir efficacement les charges de travail applicatives.

Le rôle consiste à concevoir l'architecture de l'infrastructure, à automatiser le déploiement et la configuration, à gérer le déploiement du code applicatif et à assurer une performance et une disponibilité optimales grâce à la surveillance et au dépannage. De plus, tu analyseras les habitudes d'utilisation pour prévoir les besoins futurs en ressources et tu mettras en place des mesures de sécurité robustes, notamment la ségrégation du réseau, le contrôle d'accès, le chiffrement et les systèmes de détection d'intrusion. Tu assureras aussi, de façon proactive, la réponse aux incidents pour détecter et résoudre les problèmes potentiels, afin de garantir une plateforme sécuritaire, fiable et efficace, tout en maintenant et en appliquant les protocoles de sécurité qui protègent l'infrastructure contre les menaces.


Responsabilités principales
  • Développer, déployer et soutenir des artefacts ou des modules d'infrastructure infonuagique en tant que code, ainsi que des applications
  • Mettre en œuvre, maintenir, dépanner et optimiser des pipelines CI/CD pour plusieurs projets, et assurer une sécurité automatisée dans chaque pile technologique
  • Concevoir et soutenir la résilience et l'évolutivité à l'aide de GCP et d'autres plateformes infonuagiques, et intégrer des pratiques SRE et DevOps afin de réduire au minimum les interruptions de service et les efforts manuels
  • Configurer la surveillance des applications à l'aide d'outils de surveillance standard de l'industrie, et développer des solutions de surveillance sur mesure au besoin
  • Créer et gérer les environnements de développement, de préproduction et de production en assurant leur cohérence et leur conformité aux exigences des projets, et tenir à jour la documentation des processus et des procédures DevOps ainsi que des configurations d'infrastructure
  • Définir une vision à long terme pour la maintenance et la mise à l'échelle de l'infrastructure, y compris la planification de la capacité et des coûts du matériel, des logiciels et du stockage
  • Interpréter les politiques de sécurité et veiller à ce que la conception de la plateforme respecte les lignes directrices en matière de sécurité
  • Gérer les dépôts de code source, les stratégies de branches et le contrôle de version avec GitHub

Exigences
  • Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en informatique, ou expérience équivalente
  • 3 ans ou plus d'expérience dans la mise en œuvre de solutions de plateforme et DevOps
    • 3 ans ou plus d'expérience au sein d'une équipe DevOps très performante ou dans des rôles connexes
    • 2 ans ou plus d'expérience en surveillance de la performance, en alertes et en dépannage dans une entreprise
  • Expérience de l'infonuagique hybride et de la migration d'infrastructures entre différents nuages
  • Excellente expérience de la livraison d'infrastructure en tant que code avec Terraform
  • Expérience des technologies de conteneurisation (p. ex. Docker, Colima, Kubernetes)
  • Solides compétences en scripts ou en programmation dans des langages comme Python, JavaScript et Go
  • Expérience du soutien d'outils de pipeline (GitHub, CircleCI)
  • Compréhension des outils de surveillance et de journalisation comme Prometheus, Grafana ou la pile ELK
  • Connaissance des bonnes pratiques de sécurité et des normes de conformité, y compris le codage sécuritaire et l'analyse de vulnérabilités

Processus de recrutement
  • Premier échange avec notre conseiller en acquisition de talents – en virtuel (30 minutes)
  • Entrevue avec la gestionnaire d’embauche – en virtuel (45 minutes)
  • Entrevue technique avec des membres l’équipe d’ingénierie – en personne (60 minutes)
  • Dernière rencontre avec notre PDG – en virtuel (30 minutes)
  • Offre d’emploi et intégration 🎉
Le processus peut évoluer selon les besoins de l’équipe.

Pourquoi rejoindre Stay22 ?
  • Emplacement de choix à Montréal : Travaille depuis notre dynamique siège social situé dans la Petite-Italie, avec une allocation pour la cafétéria, un accès complet au gym, ainsi qu'une terrasse sur le toit comprenant un terrain saisonnier de basketball/pickleball et une patinoire de hockey.
  • Une gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : Couverture santé et dentaire, contribution de l’employeur au REER, titre de transport STM entièrement payé, ainsi que des activités d’équipe, événements et retraites réguliers.
  • Une flexibilité adaptée à ta réalité : Horaires flexibles, possibilités de travailler de n’importe où, fermeture des bureaux en fin d’année et journées flexibles.

(Stay22 est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. Toutes les candidatures qualifiées seront examinées. Si tu as un handicap ou des besoins particuliers nécessitant des aménagements, contacte-nous à careers@stay22.com.)

Ton CV sera lu par Nayo, notre recruteur interne, même si tu ne coches pas toutes les cases, on aimerait quand même te rencontrer.

title: Instructional Designer
description:
About Frontier

Frontier is a subsidiary of Fresh Prints. Fresh Prints is a New York-based, fast-growing, fully remote, 150-person company with most of our team based in India and the Philippines. A few years ago, Fresh Prints began helping other fast-growing companies build their teams. We got so good at it that we spun out a new company to focus exclusively on that — and called it Frontier.

At Frontier, we help companies grow full-time, cross-functional teams abroad. We hire the smartest people and place them into the best companies. In three years, we’ve never lost a client. If you’re interested in a Frontier role and you apply and are accepted, we’ll screen you through a couple of internal interviews and aim to get you an interview for a full-time job within the month.

Think of us as your personal talent agent — and good luck with the application! 😊

About Bundle

Bundle delivers live 1:1 leadership and manager training with expert instructors. No micro-lessons, no click-through tutorials, just real conversations that build skills people actually use. We work with enterprise and mid-market companies across manufacturing, healthcare, construction, and beyond, and we’ve hit our goals six quarters in a row. Now we’re building toward where performance management meets live leadership development.

Role Overview

We're hiring a Full-Time Instructional Designer to help us craft, refine, and scale the materials that power our training sessions. You will work closely with our core learning design team to apply sound adult learning practices and ensure every deck, plan, and resource meets Bundle's high standards for quality, engagement, and consistency.

This is a remote, hands-on opportunity perfect for a detail-obsessed designer who thrives in a fast-moving environment. You won't be building from scratch on day one; instead, you'll focus on formatting, updating, and tailoring existing content to match our proven frameworks while leveraging modern AI tools to streamline your workflow.

What You'll Do

  • Format and update presentation materials to seamlessly match Bundle's design templates.

  • Build learner-specific versions of existing training materials based on clear guidelines.

  • Execute light content edits and regular updates across existing learning assets.

  • Conduct quality control, reviewing all materials for design, formatting, and consistency against Bundle's Lesson Plans.

  • Apply adult learning principles (andragogy) to keep content clear, actionable, and engaging.

  • Utilize modern AI tools (including Claude and Microsoft Copilot) to enhance instructional design efficiency.

  • Manage files, resources, and documentation independently using Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and SharePoint.

What You Bring

  • Solid understanding of adult learning principles (andragogy) and how to apply them to professional training.

  • Strong presentation design skills (PowerPoint or similar) with a strict eye for visual layout and accessibility standards.

  • Hands-on experience actively integrating AI tools—specifically Claude and Microsoft Copilot—into your instructional design workflow.

  • Exceptional attention to detail, strong critical thinking, and sound judgment when evaluating content quality.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, SharePoint).

  • High level of autonomy with a proven ability to follow established guidelines and execute independently.

  • Clear, professional written communication skills in English.

Desired Requirements

  • Background in corporate learning and development (L&D) or higher education instructional design.

  • Experience designing skills-based or competency-based corporate training.

Why Join Bundle?

  • Flexible, 100% remote work structure

  • Opportunity to work directly alongside a collaborative learning design team

  • Fast-growing company environment with a validated product and clear trajectory

title: Embedded Software Engineer III
description:
GROW WITH US AND STAY EXTRAORDINARY:
Launch your career to new heights with Innoflight—one of San Diego’s fastest-growing Aerospace and Defense innovators. Here, visionary minds engineer the future of space technology through pioneering, compact, and cyber-secure solutions. From software-defined radios to cutting-edge cryptographic systems and avionics, everything we build powers the next era of New Space. Join our small, agile, and mission-driven team where your work has real impact and your growth has no limits. We’re not just reaching for the stars—we’re engineering them. Let’s innovate the infinite, together.

A DAY IN THE LIFE:
The Embedded Software Engineer III plays a key role in developing software solutions for satellite avionics and payload data processing systems. This position involves creating real-time system monitoring and power management software, preparing Linux board support packages for customer flight applications, and working with a variety of embedded systems, sensors, communication buses, radios, and communications security (COMSEC) equipment. Close collaboration with hardware and FPGA engineers is essential to deliver rugged, reliable, and integrated Low-Size, Weight, and Power (Low-SWaP) products to aerospace customers.

Active U.S. Security Clearance is required.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop Embedded Software Systems: Design and implement embedded C/C++ software for multi-core processors and FPGA-integrated systems (Xilinx, Microchip, Vorago), targeting ARM Cortex and RISC-V architectures.
  • Build and Customize Linux Platforms: Configure Linux systems including kernel and bootloader (U-Boot, GRUB) modifications to support flight applications and mission requirements.
  • Implement Secure Communications: Develop networking and cryptographic functionality (e.g., IP, TLS, IPsec, AES, RSA, ECDSA) and interface with buses and protocols like SPI, I2C, UART, PCIe, SpaceWire, and Ethernet.
  • Drive End-to-End Development: Translate customer and system-level requirements into robust software solutions, participating in design, documentation, integration, validation, and testing.
  • Collaborate and Present: Work closely with cross-functional teams, support system integration, debug software/hardware issues, and present technical updates to both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Manage Development Lifecycle: Track features, bugs, and build processes using industry-standard tools for version control and release management.
YOU’RE AWESOME AT:
  • Embedded Software Development: Expertise in embedded software design and implementation, particularly within aerospace applications.
  • Complex Document Analysis: Ability to read, interpret, and analyze complex technical documents and specifications.
  • Cybersecurity and Encryption: Familiarity with writing embedded C code that incorporates cybersecurity and encryption measures to ensure secure communications.
WHAT YOU’LL NEED:
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
  • 5 or more years of professional experience developing embedded software in C/C++ for Linux and/or RTOS-based systems.
  • Deep knowledge of embedded platforms, multi-core processors, and interfacing standards (SPI, I2C, UART, PCIe, etc.).
  • Experience configuring bootloaders (U-Boot, GRUB) and customizing Linux kernels for application-specific needs.
  • Proficient with networking protocols (IP, TLS, IPsec) and cryptographic systems (AES, RSA, ECDSA, ECDH).
  • Familiarity with version control and task tracking systems (e.g., Git, Jira) and modern software development workflows.
  • Strong technical communication skills and ability to present designs and progress to both engineers and stakeholders.
  • Experience with OpenCL, CUDA, or other parallel-processing frameworks is a plus.
  • Prior work with aerospace or defense systems and knowledge of COMSEC requirements highly desirable.
  • Active U.S. Security Clearance is required.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:
The starting base salary for this position ranges from $125,000 to $150,000 per year, depending on the candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to a competitive base salary, Innoflight offers a well-rounded compensation package that includes a Profit-Sharing Bonus and a Cash Performance Bonus to reward both individual and company performance. Additional benefits include:

  • 401(k) with 3% company match (automatic enrollment)
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, HSA & life insurance
  • 10 paid holidays + 120 hours PTO (starting in year one)
  • Access to ancillary benefits such as critical illness, accident, disability, legal and pet insurance.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE:

  • Flexible Work-Life Balance: Enjoy a 9/80 work schedule with every other Friday off—whether you use it to recharge, work on a passion project, or spend time with family, the choice is yours.
  • Continuous Learning & Development: We’re serious about professional development. From tuition reimbursement to internal "Ask Me Anything" sessions and weekly “Lunch & Learns,” we make learning a core part of the job.
  • Mission-Driven Culture: We aren’t just building tech—we’re enabling the next era of space exploration. Our Culture Ambassadors help lead initiatives around inclusion, positivity, recognition, and transparency. Here, your voice is heard, your work is respected, and your individuality is celebrated.

BE YOU, WITH US:
At Innoflight, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace where everyone belongs. We recognize that great talent comes in many forms, and you don’t need to meet every requirement to bring value to our team. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t check every box.

YOU SHOULD KNOW:
Potential new employees must successfully complete a background check which includes criminal search, education certification and employment verification prior to hire. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S as you must have the ability to obtain a security clearance. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa.

A NOTE TO STAFFING AGENCIES:
Innoflight does not accept unsolicited resumes from agencies, recruiters, or any third-party sources. Any such submissions will be considered property of Innoflight, and no fees will be paid in the event a candidate is hired from an unsolicited referral.

To California residents applying for this job, please read Innoflight’s CCPA Notice: https://www.innoflight.com/careers/california-consumer-privacy-act-notice-for-job-applicants.

title: Floating School Admin
description:
Bring your leadership experience to a school community where it will make an immediate impact.

Guidepost Montessori is seeking an experienced educational leader to join our team as a Floating School Admin Independent Contractor. This is an ideal opportunity for a retired or seasoned school administrator who enjoys mentoring others, building relationships with families, and helping schools thrive, without the demands of leading an entire campus independently.

This role offers the flexibility to step in where you're needed most, covering campuses during maternity leave or other staffing gaps, and supporting schools across a region when the need arises, all while partnering with an experienced Head of School.

About Guidepost Montessori

At Guidepost Montessori, we believe children thrive when they're given the freedom, support, and environment to become confident, capable, and independent learners. Our mission is to expand access to authentic Montessori education by building exceptional schools where children, families, and educators flourish together.

With more than 60 schools across the United States, we're committed to providing high-quality educational experiences while creating welcoming communities for every family we serve.

The Opportunity

As the Floating School Admin, you'll serve as a trusted partner to the Head of School, stepping in to lead daily operations at campuses across the region, whether covering a leave, supporting a school in transition, or filling a temporary leadership gap. You'll ensure an exceptional experience for children, families, and staff wherever you're needed.

We're looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, supporting teachers, connecting with parents, and bringing calm, experienced leadership to a busy school environment. This is a hands-on role where your judgment, professionalism, and ability to build relationships quickly will have an immediate impact.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with Heads of School to oversee daily campus operations, stepping in during maternity leave or other staffing needs across the region
  • Build strong relationships with current and prospective families and guide them through school tours and the admissions process
  • Support enrollment growth by managing inquiries and following up with prospective families in our CRM
  • Foster a positive, collaborative staff culture through coaching and day-to-day support
  • Resolve parent concerns with professionalism, empathy, and sound judgment
  • Coordinate community events and outreach to strengthen family engagement
  • Oversee operational needs such as vendor scheduling, supply orders, billing support, and general campus organization

What We're Looking For

Qualifications

  • Previous leadership experience in an early childhood education or school setting
  • Experience as a School Director, Assistant Director, Principal, Program Director, or similar leadership role
  • A proven ability to lead confidently with minimal direction
  • Strong organizational and operational management skills
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities
  • Experience supporting admissions, enrollment, or customer service
  • Comfortable using technology, CRM systems, and administrative software
  • A collaborative leadership style with a solutions-focused mindset
  • Passion for supporting children, educators, and families

Preferred Qualifications

  • Director Qualified in Early Childhood Education
  • Experience leading a preschool, Montessori, childcare, or private school
  • Familiarity with Montessori education
  • Experience with Salesforce or similar CRM platforms
  • Knowledge of billing or school management software
  • Strong connections within the local community or experience supporting community outreach initiatives

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to make a meaningful impact without carrying sole responsibility for a campus
  • A collaborative leadership partnership with an experienced Head of School
  • Competitive pay of $25-30/hr
  • The opportunity to support a mission-driven organization dedicated to transforming education

If you're an experienced educational leader who still enjoys working with families, supporting educators, and helping schools succeed, we'd love to talk with you about joining our team.

Guidepost Global Education and Guidepost Montessori are committed to a policy of Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO). We will not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, color, creed, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, alienage or citizenship, disability, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under applicable federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. Our leadership is dedicated to ensuring the fulfillment of this policy. When requested, we are committed to reasonably accommodate employees and applicants with disabilities or special needs that may require an accommodation.

title: Regional Vice President, Chicago Area
location: Chicago, IL, US; Chicago Heights, IL, US; US
description:
About This Opportunity
We're looking for a Regional Vice President, Midwest to lead a growing business, strengthen influential utility partnerships, develop exceptional leaders, and help shape the future of energy solutions across one of Cascade's most important regions. This is a rare opportunity to step into a visible leadership role with significant influence over business performance, market strategy, organizational growth, and client impact. The energy industry is evolving rapidly, creating significant opportunities for innovation and impact. Utilities are reimagining how they serve customers, strengthen grid resilience, manage demand, and advance ambitious energy and decarbonization goals. From energy efficiency and demand flexibility to electrification and emerging grid solutions, the Midwest is at the center of many of these transformations - and Cascade is helping lead the way.
As Cascade's senior executive leader in the Midwest, you'll lead one of Cascade's most significant growth opportunities while helping shape the future of energy solutions across the Midwest region. You'll guide regional strategy, shape investment priorities, build executive-level relationships, develop future leaders, and help identify and capture the next generation of growth opportunities.
This role goes far beyond operational leadership. We're seeking a leader who thrives on building businesses, influencing markets, developing people, and driving meaningful change. You'll represent Cascade throughout the region, bringing together clients, industry partners, policymakers, and internal teams to create solutions that generate lasting value for utilities, customers, communities, and the energy system as a whole.
At Cascade, you'll join a highly respected team of experts who are passionate about helping clients solve complex challenges while creating measurable impact. As an employee-owned company, we empower leaders to think boldly, act decisively, and build the teams, partnerships, and capabilities needed to succeed. If you're energized by the opportunity to lead a business, shape an industry, grow exceptional leaders, and leave a lasting mark on the future of energy, we'd love to meet you!
Future-Focused AI-Ready Culture
At Cascade Energy, we’re actively shaping how AI gets deployed in the real world, in our tools, our client engagements, and our daily work. Our approach has always been relationship-driven and expertise-led, and AI is how we multiply the impact of both. Successful Cascadians are curious and resilient. They embrace change, seek smarter ways to create impact, and take ownership of their own growth. We embed AI into our work in ways that are responsible and human-centered, and we actively develop our people to deploy it creatively and confidently.
We believe the future belongs to organizations that pair emerging technology with genuine human expertise. That future is being built here . . . come be a part of it!
What You Will Be Doing
Reasonable accommodation will be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.
Lead the Midwest business

Lead the Midwest business, aligning regional strategy, client commitments, financial goals, and Cascade priorities.
Drive business performance by aligning people, resources, and priorities around key objectives.
Lead directors, managers, and regional staff to deliver strong execution, accountability, and client outcomes.
Drive innovation and continuous improvement to strengthen client outcomes and operational effectiveness.
Ensure strong governance, risk management, and organizational readiness across Midwest programs and teams.

Own Midwest account strategy and client relationships

Build trusted executive relationships with utility leaders and key stakeholders
Lead regional account strategy to support client success, retention, and long-term growth.
Partner with Customer Engagement to position Cascade for renewals, expansions, and new opportunities.
Serve as an executive sponsor for major utility partnerships, helping resolve complex challenges and strengthen strategic partnerships.

Develop leaders and build organizational capacity

Develop leaders through coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
Build the organizational structures and capabilities needed to support long-term growth.
Lead a high-performing regional leadership team grounded in accountability, collaboration, and results.
Strengthen partner and delivery ecosystems to support business objectives and client success.

Shape market opportunities and industry influence

Translate market, policy, and industry trends into actionable business strategies.
Represent Cascade with utilities, regulators, policymakers, and industry partners across the region.
Expand Cascade's visibility, influence, and reputation within the Midwest energy community.
Advance emerging solutions such as demand flexibility, grid-interactive efficient operations, and electrification in partnership with product owners and experts.

This is a full-time, exempt position located in the Chicago, Illinois area. Regular travel is expected for client engagements, utility partner meetings, industry events, program reviews, team meetings, and companywide events, including overnight stays as needed.
Qualifications
Applicants for this role are required to have:

description:
York Space Systems is seeking a Senior Frontend Software Engineer who is passionate about building software that pushes the bounds of what's possible. Visualizing live satellite state across a constellation
Surfacing alerts during critical mission windows

You'll also drive frontend best practices across the team and help junior engineers grow their craft.

Prior space-industry experience is not required.

Remote Policy: Hybrid (4 days in office)

Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, pair programming, and design discussions
Contribute to sprint planning, technical scoping, and cross-team alignment on feature work
Help establish and advocate for frontend best practices and design system standards across the team

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field
6+ years of software engineering experience with a strong focus on frontend and web application development
Deep proficiency in modern React, including component architecture, performance optimization, and state management patterns
Strong expertise in TypeScript and its application in large-scale frontend codebases
Experience building and maintaining design systems and shared component libraries
Proficiency with common front-end tooling such as Yarn, Babel, and Material-UI
Experience with Git in a collaborative, multi-contributor environment
Familiarity with backend APIs and the ability to design and consume REST APIs effectively
Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and drive frontend code quality through reviews and design discussions
Proven ability to collaborate across engineering, UI/UX, and operational stakeholders
Exceptional problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate ambiguous requirements independently and drive to resolution
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including presenting technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
Active security clearance or ability to obtain one

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modern state management tools such as TanStack Query
Experience with WebAssembly (WASM) for performance-critical frontend workloads

title: Peer Specialist
description:
Position: Peer Specialist

The Peer Specialist plays a critical role in creating a welcoming and supportive environment for individuals seeking behavioral health and substance use disorder services at our Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC). The Peer Specialist is often the first person a service recipient encounters when entering the clinic, helping to foster connection, hope, and engagement from the very beginning of treatment.


Essential Duties:

  • Welcome and greet service recipients entering the CCBHC, helping to create a warm, respectful and recovery-focused environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

Position Title: REPAIR TECHNICIAN

Department: Transportation

Reports To: Transportation Fleet Services Supervisor

JOB DEFINITION:

Under general supervision, the Transportation Repair Technician inspects equipment for repairs and deficiencies, diagnoses malfunctions to determine cause, and adjusts, repairs, replaces, or modifies automotive equipment, parts and auxiliary systems. A position in this class may be delegated the additional responsibility for performing lead worker duties in the absence of the lead person. The Transportation Repair Technician is primarily responsible for diagnosing malfunctions, performing journey level repairs on gasoline and diesel equipment, including engine and transmission overhauls, and road-testing equipment to ensure safe operating conditions. Additional responsibilities include inspecting buses to note deficiencies as required by State law, putting on and taking off tire chains, performing preventative maintenance duties, and repairing seats. After completion of an initial orientation period, work is performed without direct supervision. Repair procedures are detailed in automotive and stationary equipment manuals and specifications prepared by the District or by equipment manufacturers. Assignments are to be received from a lead worker or supervisor in the form of verbal or written instructions. The Transportation Repair Technician works under the supervision of the Transportation Fleet Services Supervisor. The employee is required to hold a valid Oregon Class B Commercial Driver's License and a School Bus Driver's Certificate. The employee may be required to drive a bus route or shuttle as needed.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Conducts inspections of equipment in the field or in the shop to determine safety status or to identify potential causes of equipment malfunction.
  • Conducts visual inspections of equipment in the shop to identify items not on the complaint list which may need repair or replacement and determines items needing immediate attention.
  • Performs diagnostic inspections on automotive or other motorized or stationary equipment to identify electrical, mechanical, or other equipment problems.
  • Drives, and operates vehicle, or uses diagnostic test equipment to identify problems and malfunctions.
  • Must have basic computer skills to retrieve vehicle information as needed.
  • May be required to initiate an order for parts using parts books and other sources, including contacting vendors to determine availability of parts.
  • Performs major repairs in the shop and minor repairs in the field on a variety of gasoline or diesel powered equipment such as school buses, dump trucks, flatbed trucks, vans, cars.
  • Operates engine analyzer and tune-up equipment, and other electrical, electronic, or mechanical testing or equipment repair tools.
  • Repairs or replaces equipment components such as engines, automatic and manual transmissions, power trains, differentials, and axles including gears, and fuel injector systems, electrical or electronic ignition and electrical generation and transmission systems, air compression systems and lines, engine cooling and air conditioning systems, suspension systems, mechanical breaking systems, and air and hydraulic braking systems; cleans tools and equipment; keeps work area clean and orderly.
  • Applies safety procedures to all facets of work.
  • Maintains records of work performed by recording nature of repair, labor hours, costs and parts used in making repairs (i.e., work order).
  • Drives equipment in and out of repair shop.
  • Operates and road tests repaired vehicles to ensure proper operation.
  • Inspects buses to note deficiencies as required by State law.
  • Puts on and takes off tire chains.
  • Repairs seats.
  • Performs preventative maintenance on vehicles.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.
  • Fulfills performance standards identified in the evaluation process as required by the position.
  • Maintains confidentiality concerning district employees and district policies.
  • Fulfills working conditions and physical effort listed below.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is performed primarily in a transportation shop environment and may include work outdoors in varying weather conditions. The position requires standing, bending, kneeling, climbing, working under vehicles, operating hand and power tools, and lifting or moving parts and equipment consistent with assigned duties.

The employee may be exposed to mechanical hazards, moving equipment, loud noise, fuels, oils, chemicals, and other automotive materials. Adherence to safety procedures and regulatory standards is required at all times.

Work schedules may include regular business hours with occasional overtime or emergency repair responsibilities. The role requires technical problem-solving, attention to detail, and independent judgment in maintaining and repairing district vehicles. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

****

JOBS REQUIRING LIFT/ MANEUVER OF UP TO BUT NOT EXCEEDING 50 LBS:

Employees working in the transportation shop performing vehicle repair duties are provided a variety of equipment to assist in the lifting and maneuvering of parts and materials. Items exceeding 50 pounds in weight should be lifted or moved utilizing a team lift arrangement or tools provided specifically to move the equipment. Examples include hydraulic lifts, wheeled carts, and tire and break drum dollies.

*****

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

Knowledge:

  • Standard trade practices, automotive tools, and diagnostic equipment.
  • Construction and operation of automotive electrical systems.
  • Principles of construction and operation of internal combustion engines.
  • Methods and tools used in the repair of gasoline and diesel automotive and allied equipment including engines, transmissions power trains, fuel and ignition systems, air and mechanical brakes, and suspension systems.
  • Safety hazards and necessary precautions required to work around, in and under vehicles or to work with petroleum-based chemical, solvents and exhaust fumes.

Skills and Abilities:

Possess the physical ability to regularly attend work and fulfill the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Skillfully use tools and operate diagnostic and power equipment employed in the repair and adjustment of engines and components.
  • Locate and repair defects in motor equipment.
  • Weld lightweight and heavyweight metal using gas and electric welders as required.
  • Follow oral and written directions.
  • Accurately diagnose equipment malfunctions using mechanical, electrical, and electronic testing equipment.
  • Repair automotive equipment and auxiliary electrical, electronic, mechanical, or structural components.
  • Perform diagnostic or mechanical repair work independently at the journey level without direct supervision in the shop or in the field.
  • Read, understand, interpret and apply instructions and procedures in repair manuals to work performed.
  • Learn State repair and maintenance requirements for school buses.
  • Use welding and other shop equipment such as lathes and grinders.
  • Work safely around noisy machinery, gasoline and other petroleum products, exhaust and welding fumes, and work in heated and unheated areas.
  • Light repair of equipment in the field requiring exposure to adverse weather conditions.
  • Maintain a safe driving record.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with co-workers, supervisor, and vehicle operators.
  • Learn and participate in the work of co-workers as required in the position.
  • Maintain a high level of commitment to completion of all tasks.
  • Possess the appropriate Oregon Driver's License and maintain an insurable status for automobile and liability coverage.
  • Adhere to the district requirements for a drug-free workplace.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Must have a high school diploma, or equivalent. Must be able to meet industry journeyman standards for repair and diagnosis within two years after date of employment. Must provide a set of standard technician’s tools.

The position requires working knowledge of several technical procedures or work activity areas and ability to train others in such activity. In-depth knowledge of work-related School District policies and practices in necessary. Proficiency can be acquired in twelve to twenty-four months.

Must obtain an ODE School Bus Inspection certification.

CERTIFICATION AND LICENSING:

The employee is required to hold a valid Oregon Class B Commercial Driver's License issued by the Oregon State Department of Motor Vehicles and a School Bus Driver's Certificate. Obtain an ODE School Bus Inspection Certificate.

Expectations of Professional Conduct:

Employees of Bend-La Pine Schools are expected to adhere to all Bend-La Pine Schools policies and regulations, ensuring compliance with established procedures and expectations. They are to prioritize the well-being of students, aligning their conduct with the core values of public education and the mission, vision, and goals of Bend-La Pine Schools. This entails maintaining consistent and punctual attendance while adhering to site and/or district protocols for reporting absences.

Professionalism extends to personal presentation, with employees expected to maintain attire and grooming appropriate to their roles. While carrying out everyday tasks independently, it's essential to maintain professionalism in how you communicate, both verbally and nonverbally, with students, parents/guardians, the public, and colleagues. This includes valuing and respecting cultural and background differences. Employees of Bend-La Pine Schools are entrusted with fostering a respectful working and learning environment, upholding confidentiality regarding student, staff, and district information at all times.

The statements herein reflect the general nature and level of work expected in this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or qualifications.

Employees may be assigned additional duties as needed to support district operations, provide coverage, and ensure the effective functioning of the organization. This may include location changes to the assignment in order to address developing district needs.

description:

title: ELP STATION COORDINATOR 737-700
description:
The Station Coordinator is EAX's single point of coordination at ELP for the DHS 737-700 program. The role ensures the daily flight schedule is executed safely, on time, and in compliance with the contract by coordinating with the assigned flight crews, maintenance, ground handling, and the government customer on the ramp. The position is responsible for station readiness, performance, and records. The incumbent is the first-line response when anything on the ground threatens the schedule.

Key responsibilities

Daily station operations

  • Verify the daily station plan against the published DHS/ICE schedule: aircraft assignment, crew report times, gate/hardstand, fuel, catering, and lav/water service.
  • Lead pre-departure coordination with the Captain, the government flight/mission lead, and ground handling; confirm the aircraft is released and the ramp is ready before boarding begins.
  • Track every departure and arrival against the flight schedule; record delays with EAX delay codes and root cause, and notify OCC/dispatch immediately of any threat to on-time performance.
  • Manage irregular operations at ELP in coordination with EAX SOC: diversions, weather holds, AOG, crew legality issues, and schedule changes pushed by the customer.

Maintenance coordination

  • Serve as the station liaison between line maintenance, Maintenance Control, and SOC for the 737-700 tails assigned to the program.

Vendor and ground handling oversight

  • Oversee contract ground handlers, fuelers, caterers, and cleaners against EAX standards and each service agreement; audit performance and document discrepancies.
  • Verify fuel quality records, deicing/anti-icing capability (as applicable), and weight-and-balance inputs meet EAX procedures.
  • Confirm vendor personnel hold current EAX-required training (ground handling, hazmat recognition, fueling, security) before working EAX aircraft.

Security, safety, and compliance

  • Enforce the EAX aircraft operator security program at ELP, including aircraft access control, searches, and SIDA/AOA compliance with airport and TSA requirements.
  • Protect contract-sensitive information (manifests, schedules, PII) per DHS/ICE contract handling requirements; share only with authorized personnel.
  • Report hazards, incidents, and ground damage through the EAX SMS; participate in investigations and track corrective actions to closure.
  • Maintain station records for FAA, DOT, TSA, customer, and internal audits; keep the station manual current.

Customer and contract support

  • Act as EAX's on-site representative to DHS/ICE representatives and the airport authority; attend operational coordination meetings.
  • Provide the Director of Operations the data needed for contract performance reporting: OTP, completion factor, cancellations, and delay causes.
  • Flag contract scope changes, extra-service requests, and cost-bearing events for billing and contract review.

Administration

  • Prepare daily and weekly station reports; maintain the station contact roster, vendor list, and emergency response plan.
  • Manage station supplies, purchase requests, and vendor invoice verification within approved limits.

Qualifications

Required

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 3+ years in airline station operations, ground operations, dispatch/OCC, or line maintenance coordination; Part 121 experience strongly weighted.
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a DHS/ICE suitability or background determination as required by the contract.
  • Ability to pass a TSA Security Threat Assessment and fingerprint-based CHRC, and to obtain and hold an ELP SIDA badge.
  • Pre-employment and random DOT drug and alcohol testing under 49 CFR Part 40 / 14 CFR Part 120 (safety-sensitive function).
  • Valid driver's license; ability to obtain airport ramp driving privileges.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and flight-following or scheduling software.

Preferred

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in aviation management or a related field.
  • Supervisory or station lead experience at a charter, ACMI, or government-contract carrier.
  • Experience supporting DoD, CRAF, or DHS flight operations.
  • Boeing 737 NG familiarity (servicing, GSE, MEL/CDL concepts).
  • FAA Aircraft Dispatcher certificate or A&P certificate.
  • Hazmat, weight-and-balance/load planning, or fueling supervisor certifications.
  • Conversational Spanish.

Knowledge, skills, and abilities

  • Part 121 operational control concepts and the line between station coordination and dispatch/maintenance authority.
  • TSA aircraft operator security requirements and airport SIDA/AOA procedures.
  • Ramp safety, aircraft servicing, and GSE operation around narrowbody jets.
  • SMS fundamentals: hazard reporting, just culture, corrective action tracking.
  • Calm, decisive communication with crews, mechanics, vendors, and government representatives under schedule pressure.
  • Accurate, timely record keeping and reporting; comfort working from data (OTP, delay codes, completion factor).
  • Discretion with sensitive and personally identifiable information.
  • Ability to work independently at an outstation with limited on-site management.

Working conditions

  • Work is split between the station office and the ramp, in El Paso heat (routinely above 100°F in summer), wind, dust, and jet blast/noise; hearing protection required.
  • The work schedule is based on the requirements of the flight schedule, which includes early mornings, nights, weekends, and holidays; on-call for irregular operations and AOG events.
  • Occasional travel to other EAX stations or HQ in Greensboro, NC for training and surge support.
  • Must stand and walk on the ramp for extended periods, climb aircraft stairs, and lift up to 50 lb.
  • Safety-sensitive position subject to DOT drug and alcohol testing.

title: Data & AI Engineer II
description:
CareDx, Inc. is a leading precision medicine solutions company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of clinically differentiated, high-value healthcare solutions for transplant patients and caregivers. CareDx offers products, testing services, and digital healthcare solutions along the pre- and post-transplant patient journey, and is the leading provider of genomics-based information for transplant patients.

The Data & AI Engineer II will develop analytical applications, data pipelines, and AI-powered capabilities that support clinical research, statistical analysis, and data-driven decision-making. This role helps transform research workflows, statistical analyses, and machine learning models into reliable, secure, and user-facing software. The engineer will collaborate with data scientists, statisticians, engineers, clinicians, and product stakeholders to productionize analytical workflows, translate R-based analyses into maintainable Python, and deliver applications for internal and external users. The engineer will also contribute to AI-powered features that analyze structured and unstructured data, extract information from documents, synthesize analytical results, and help users interpret scientific and clinical information. Success in this role requires strong software engineering fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to independently deliver well-defined components and features with support on more complex technical decisions.

Responsibilities:
• Develop and maintain analytical applications using tools and frameworks such as Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Dash, and Django.
• Own the implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance of well-defined application features and data workflows.
• Productionize statistical models and machine learning workflows developed by data scientists and statisticians.
• Translate and refactor R-based research and analytical workflows into maintainable, tested Python code.
• Build and maintain data pipelines that support clinical data processing, analysis, visualization, and reporting.
• Develop interactive applications that enable data exploration, visualization, and decision support.
• Integrate applications with relational databases, APIs, analytical outputs, documents, and other structured and unstructured data sources.
• Contribute to AI-powered application features using techniques such as structured information extraction, retrieval-augmented generation, tool or function calling, and multi-step workflows.
• Implement validation, grounding, logging, traceability, and human-review mechanisms for AI-generated outputs.
• Collaborate with scientists, clinicians, product stakeholders, and senior engineers to translate requirements into practical technical solutions.
• Participate in technical design discussions and document implementation decisions, assumptions, and tradeoffs.
• Write reliable, readable, and testable code using established engineering patterns and team standards.
• Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve implementation quality and technical judgment.
• Monitor, debug, and improve application performance and reliability across data, model, AI, and application layers.
• Follow security, privacy, and compliance requirements for sensitive healthcare data, including HIPAA-aligned practices.
• Contribute to shared components, documentation, development tools, and engineering process improvements.
• Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, and technical challenges clearly and proactively.

Qualifications:
• Education: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience: 2+ years of experience in data engineering, backend engineering, full-stack development, analytics engineering, or a related role.
• Strong proficiency in Python for data analysis and software development.
• Experience working with statistical analysis, data science, or machine learning workflows.
• Experience transforming prototype, research, or analytical code into maintainable software.
• Experience building analytical applications using Streamlit, Plotly, Dash, or similar technologies.
• Experience developing backend services or web applications using Django, FastAPI, Flask, or a similar framework.
• Experience building and maintaining data pipelines that integrate multiple data sources.
• Familiarity with relational databases, SQL, APIs, and common data formats.
• Experience or demonstrated applied knowledge in at least one modern LLM capability, such as retrieval-augmented generation, structured extraction, tool calling, or agentic workflows.
• Understanding of core production considerations for AI systems, including grounding, hallucination mitigation, output validation, security, latency, cost, and human oversight.
• Experience with version control and collaborative development practices, including Git, branching, pull requests, and code reviews.
• Experience writing automated tests and debugging applications across multiple technical layers.
• Ability to independently deliver well-defined features while seeking guidance when requirements or technical risks are unclear.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Honest and transparent approach to feedback, collaboration, and accountability.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience in healthcare, biotechnology, clinical research, or another regulated environment.
• Experience working with sensitive or protected healthcare data.
• Familiarity with HIPAA-aligned application and data-handling practices.
• Experience with Azure, Databricks, or comparable cloud and data platforms.
• Familiarity with CI/CD practices and automated testing tools such as pytest.
• Experience with pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, statsmodels, or similar data science libraries.
• Experience deploying or supporting production web applications.
• Experience using modern AI-assisted software development tools, such as Codex or similar coding agents, for development, testing, debugging, and documentation.
• Domain knowledge in biological medicine, healthcare, or clinical data.
• Experience communicating technical work to scientific or clinical audiences.

Every individual at CareDx has a direct impact on our collective mission to improve the lives of organ transplant patients worldwide. We believe in taking great care of our people, so they take even greater care of our patients.

title: Public Sector Lead, Central Government
description:
The UK is making a wholesale shift to AI. The government's AI Opportunities Action Plan set out to "mainline AI into the veins" of the country, and the focus has now moved to delivery: the Incubator for AI () is shipping tools like the Humphrey suite into departments, a Sovereign AI Unit and AI Growth Zones are being stood up, and civilian departments are under real pressure to move from pilots to production. Scale can play a foundational role in building the reliable AI applications that shift depends on.

We're looking for someone to lead that work in central government. This isn’t about staying in the office and managing a team of sales people, its about building the business from the front. You'd own our commercial relationships across civilian departments, starting where the near-term pipeline is strongest: HMRC, DWP, and NHS.

This is a critical role reporting directly to the new Public Sector leader. You'd carry a number, win deals yourself, and build a small team behind you as the work grows. It suits someone who has sold into these departments before and knows how they actually make decisions, not just how the org charts look.

What you'll do

  • Own our commercial plan and pipeline for UK civilian central government
  • Find, shape, and close deals yourself, from the first conversation through to contract and into delivery
  • Use the relationships you already have across departments like HMRC, DWP, and NHS
  • Work the frameworks, tenders and teaming, and know which route to market is worth the effort and which isn't.
  • Be a credible counterpart to senior civil servants, and turn what they need into work we can deliver
  • Stay close to our product and delivery teams so what we sell is what we build
  • Hire and lead a small team over time, and help shape the wider UK public sector plan with the UK Public Sector Lead

What we're looking for

  • You've sold and delivered technology or transformation work to UK civilian central government, either from a vendor or from inside government
  • You know at least one major department well (e.g. HMRC, DWP, or NHS) and how it buys
  • You understand public sector procurement: frameworks, tenders, and buying that runs through a lot of stakeholders
  • You've opened doors, run complex pursuits, and owned the result
  • You have relationships with senior people across departments
  • You do your best work when things are ambiguous and moving quickly

People who tend to fit this have spent years leading UK public sector work at companies like Palantir, Google, AWS, Microsoft or Oracle, at consultancies and systems integrators like Accenture, Deloitte, EY, Bain or McKinsey, or in senior commercial or programme roles inside the departments themselves.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AI or data-heavy platforms
  • Regulated, mission-critical government programmes
  • You've built or run a small go to market team before

Why join

You'd be building this market, not maintaining it. There's no playbook to inherit, which is rather the point. The deals you win, and the way you win them, will shape how Scale works with UK government for years.

title: Crane Operations Foreman
description:
Position Summary

Parker Towing Company is seeking an experienced Crane Operations Foreman to support and lead daily terminal operations at our Ashland City, Tennessee facility. This hands-on leadership position emphasizes crane operations, cargo handling, crew supervision, and safe execution of lifting activities.

The Crane Operations Foreman serves as a key link between the Port Manager and the terminal operations crew. This position coordinates daily work assignments, directs employees during loading and unloading operations, ensures safe and efficient crane operations, monitors equipment and rigging conditions, and helps maintain productivity and operational standards throughout the facility.

The successful candidate will have significant experience operating cranes in an industrial, marine terminal, construction, heavy equipment, or similar environment and prior experience leading crews or supervising employees. The Foreman is expected to lead from the field and will regularly operate cranes and other terminal equipment as operational needs require.
Work schedules may vary based on vessel, barge, truck, cargo, and customer requirements and may include overtime, weekends, holidays, and occasional work at other Parker Towing facilities

Essential Responsibilities
  • Serve as the primary crane operator for the Ashland City terminal, safely loading and unloading barges, trucks, and storage areas.
  • Perform and oversee crane lifts involving steel, bulk materials, project cargo, and other commodities.
  • Perform and oversee barge loading, unloading, and cleaning activities, including preparation of barges for cargo operations.
  • Assist with barge positioning, line handling, securing barges, and other marine terminal activities.
  • Inspect cranes, rigging, and lifting equipment before use and ensure equipment is safe and ready for operation.
  • Select and properly use slings, chains, hooks, spreader bars, and other rigging based on the load and lifting conditions.
  • Direct and coordinate cargo handlers and equipment operators supporting crane and terminal operations.
  • Assign daily work and provide hands-on leadership to the terminal crew based on operational and customer needs.
  • Ensure employees follow proper lifting procedures, hand signals, radio communications, safety requirements, and terminal operating practices.
  • Operate forklifts, front-end loaders, skid steers, and other terminal equipment as needed.
  • Coordinate the safe staging, securing, storage, and movement of cargo throughout the terminal.
  • Assist with barge positioning, line handling, truck loading and unloading, and other terminal activities.
  • Lead pre-shift meetings, toolbox talks, and job briefings and assist with employee training.
  • Monitor crew performance and address safety, productivity, attendance, or operational concerns in coordination with the Port Manager.
  • Identify and report equipment issues, unsafe conditions, incidents, near misses, spills, and cargo damage.
  • Assist the Port Manager with daily planning, staffing, scheduling, equipment needs, and overall terminal operations.
  • Maintain safe and organized work areas and perform additional operational or leadership duties as assigned.
Travel Requirements

This position requires approximately 40% travel and the ability to travel between Parker Towing Ports & Terminals facilities throughout Tennessee and Alabama. Travel is an essential function of the position and will primarily involve providing crane operating support for emergency situations, staffing needs, equipment coverage, and other operational requirements.

The Crane Operations Foreman must be willing and able to travel on short notice when necessary. Travel may include overnight stays and work outside the employees’ regular Ashland City schedule.

Requirements
  • Significant crane operating experience in a marine terminal, industrial, construction, or heavy-equipment environment.
  • Prior foreman, crew lead, supervisory, or similar operational leadership experience.
  • Strong knowledge of crane operations, rigging, lifting practices, load control, and safe material handling.
  • Ability to lead employees while remaining actively involved in day-to-day crane and terminal operations.
  • Ability and willingness to travel approximately 30% throughout Tennessee and Alabama, including short-notice and overnight travel when operationally necessary.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including overtime, weekends, holidays, and varying start and end times.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel between company facilities.
  • Must live within 50 miles of the assigned port or be willing to relocate within the required distance.
  • Ability to work safely in an outdoor marine and industrial environment.

title: Winder - Evening
description:
Summary
Delta Star Inc. is looking for a skilled and hands‑on Winder to join our manufacturing team. If you take pride in building high‑quality components, enjoy precision work, and want to be part of a team that creates products that power communities across North America, this role is for you!
As a Winder, you’ll bring engineering specifications to life by manufacturing, assembling, and inspecting coils with accuracy and craftsmanship. Every coil you produce contributes directly to the reliability and performance of our transformers—making your work essential to our mission.

What You'll Do
In this role, you’ll transform raw materials into expertly wound coils that meet strict engineering and safety standards. From interpreting technical drawings to executing complex winding, brazing, and assembly tasks, you’ll ensure each component is built to the highest level of quality.
You’ll work closely with internal teams, maintain precise documentation, and support continuous improvement initiatives within the manufacturing process. Your attention to detail and commitment to accuracy will help keep production running smoothly and efficiently.

A Day in the Life
Every day brings hands‑on, technical work that requires both focus and skill. You may find yourself:

Winding copper wire around disc coils with careful precision
Measuring, recording, and inspecting your work to ensure compliance
Performing brazing tasks and identifying potential defects
Using lifting equipment to safely rotate large coils
Reading complex electrical and engineering drawings
Maintaining a clean, organized, and safe workspace

What We're Looking For
We're seeking a dependable and detail‑oriented individual who enjoys hands‑on technical work and takes pride in producing high‑quality components. You’re someone who works well independently, communicates effectively, and thrives in a team environment where precision and safety matter.
If you’re resourceful, mechanically inclined, and enjoy solving problems on the shop floor, you’ll be a great fit.

Schedule: Monday to Thursday, from 3:30 PM to 2:00 AM

Salary: $29.68 per hour, plus a $1.75 per hour evening shift premium.

Position Requirements

High School Diploma or GED required
1–2 years of experience in a similar role (asset)
2 years of experience in the electrical field (asset)
Valid overhead crane certification (asset)
Vocational diploma (DEP) in welding or electrical work (asset)

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong knowledge of hand tools and measuring instruments (metric & imperial)
Ability to read and interpret electrical and engineering drawings
Great problem‑solving skills and resourcefulness
Reliable, punctual, and team‑oriented
Extremely detail‑oriented and capable of executing precision work on delicate materials
Commitment to safety and proper handling of equipment

title: Principal Platform Engineer
description:
About Shift5

Shift5 delivers operational intelligence for onboard OT across defense, aerospace, and commercial transportation fleets. We capture and analyze databus data to detect anomalies, predict failures, and secure critical infrastructure against cyber threats.

The Role & Team

The Platform Engineering team owns four core capabilities: Operating Systems (BaseOS, Manifold, Yocto), Cloud & Infrastructure (AWS/GovCloud to edge), Developer Experience (CI/CD guardrails, internal tooling), and AI Enablement (secure AI orchestration and tooling).

As Principal Platform Engineer, you are the senior-most individual contributor on the team, serving as the primary technical anchor for architecture and a key multiplier for the engineering org. You will drive overall technical strategy, mentor senior engineers, and step into direct team leadership or people management as needed.

What You'll Do

  • Release Engineering & Delivery Backbone: Architect and operate end-to-end release infrastructure (Lunar) and GitOps delivery pipelines using ArgoCD, EKS, GitHub Enterprise, and GitHub Actions.

You are a motivated and team-oriented individual who is excited to start a career in cannabis cultivation and pest management. You have a positive attitude and enjoy working in a dynamic environment. What You'll Bring:

  • Reliable transportation and the ability to handle potential allergens, irritants, and elevated environmental conditions (such as high temperatures, humidity, and CO2 levels).
  • A High School Diploma or equivalent.

Even Better If:

Physical Requirements

title: Senior Investment Associate
description:

title: Clinical Scientist - Operations
description:
About Signant Health
At Signant Health, we help bring life-changing treatments to patients faster. We are a global evidence generation company that supports clinical trials with smart technology, scientific expertise, and hands-on operational support — so better data leads to better decisions in healthcare. We embrace AI and advanced technologies to enhance every aspect of what we do, from data analysis to operational efficiency.
Our teams work at the intersection of science, technology, and patient experience, delivering digital solutions powered by AI innovation that make clinical trials more efficient, more accurate, and more accessible around the world. Trusted by leading pharmaceutical companies and CROs, our platforms and services support studies across more than 90 countries and have contributed to hundreds of new drug approvals.
If you are motivated by meaningful work, global impact, and innovation in clinical research and digital health — including the opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI technologies — you will find purpose and opportunity at Signant Health.
About the Role
The Clinical Scientist in our Digital Health Sciences team will serve as a trusted scientific advisor to internal teams and external customers on the application of eCOA, eConsent, sensors, wearables, and other digital health technologies in clinical trials. You will bridge the gap between clinical science and technology, ensuring our solutions meet the rigorous scientific and regulatory requirements of modern clinical research. This role combines pre-sales support, scientific consultation, thought leadership, and product development input—offering variety, intellectual challenge, and the opportunity to shape the future of digital clinical trials.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

Analyze study protocols and relevant clinical documents to identify scientific and technological requirements; document findings and present scientific content in client meetings and pre-sales activities
Advise technical, operations, and client teams on eCOA and digital health solution design, ensuring designs align with clinical trial objectives and regulatory best practices
Provide scientific consultation and support for special projects and client-specific scientific requests, including internal research initiatives
Maintain current knowledge of industry best practices, regulatory requirements, and emerging standards for clinical outcome assessments and digital health technologies
Participate actively in industry forums, working groups, and collaborations with key opinion leaders to stay at the forefront of digital health innovation
Develop thought leadership materials, scientific content, and marketing resources that demonstrate Signant Health's scientific expertise internally and externally
Represent Signant Health at industry conferences, forums, webinars, and publications to build visibility and credibility in digital health science
Develop training and marketing materials to support sales, client success, and product education
Manage multiple concurrent projects efficiently while maintaining high-quality standards

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES
Essential:

Advanced degree (PhD preferred) in biological science, healthcare, or related field
1-3 years' experience in clinical trial technology, digital health, or related industry (client-facing experience preferred)
In-depth understanding of clinical research and the drug development cycle
Knowledge of clinical outcome assessments (COA) and/or experience with eCOA, eConsent, EDC, sensors, and wearable technologies
Proven ability to multitask, manage time effectively, and deliver in a fast-paced environment
Business-driven mindset with understanding of commercial drivers and growth objectives
Ability to translate between scientific requirements and technology solutions; comfort bridging science and technology
Proven ability to work effectively across teams in a matrix environment; strong team player with positive demeanor
Ability to rapidly develop expertise in new areas through research, networking, and collaborative learning
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills

Desirable:

Experience in commercial pre-award activities, including bid defense, capabilities meetings, or solution design and requirement gathering
Hands-on experience designing, implementing, or using ePRO/eCOA solutions in clinical trials
Track record of effective communication with both technical and non-technical audiences across all organizational levels

Why Signant Health?
At Signant Health, your work has real impact. Everything we build, support, and deliver helps advance clinical research and bring new treatments to patients faster — improving lives around the world. Our teams combine science, technology, and operational expertise to solve complex clinical trial challenges, and every role contributes to that mission.
We offer a collaborative, global environment where you can grow your career while working alongside experts across clinical, technology, data, and operations, with opportunities to learn, take ownership, and drive meaningful innovation — not just maintain the status quo.
If you are looking for purpose-driven work, smart colleagues, and the opportunity to help shape the future of clinical research and digital health, Signant Health is the place to do it.
At Signant Health, accepting difference isn't enough — we celebrate it, we support it, and we nurture it for the benefit of our team members, our clients, and our community. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer, committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or veteran status. Prior to their start date, all new hires are required to be verified through a thorough background check and identity verification to confirm eligibility for employment.
Unsolicited resumes submitted by agencies or third-party recruiters directly to hiring managers or any Signant Health employee will not be considered and will not obligate Signant Health to any fees or terms associated with the submission.
