title: Fitness Attendant
description:
Department: Parks & Recreation

Reports To: Wellness Manager and Coordinator

FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt


GENERAL PURPOSE:

The Fitness Attendant is responsible for building positive, friendly relationships with all the High Blue members and guests who use the cardiovascular and strength areas. Responsibilities also include training members on proper use of the equipment as well as preventative and general maintenance of the training equipment areas. Cleanliness and Safety are of the utmost importance to High Blue and its members, your responsibility in this area is highlighted below. Incumbent must demonstrate a strong personal commitment to the mission and goals of the Belton Parks & Recreation Department. Carry out their assigned responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws.


PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

The following duties are not intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties performed by the individual in this classification, only a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties as assigned.

  • Responsible for knowing members and introducing yourself to members. It is your job to create an atmosphere of a friendly community.
  • Responsible for logging duties performed during shift.
  • Responsible for communicating members needs to the Wellness Manager.
  • Give orientations to those members that request a tour of the facility.
  • Must be able to adjust and operate all Fitness Equipment and knowledgeable of fitness level in general.
  • Handle customer service inquiries and related problems.
  • Assist staff in preparing for weekend rentals, including private events and birthday parties.
  • Responsible for keeping fitness area safe and organized and clean. Must be able to demonstrate proper form and function when orienting members to the equipment.
  • Responsible for cleaning cardiovascular and strength machines when not in use.
  • Be knowledgeable of all Belton Parks & Recreation programs and services to answer questions and/or channel calls to the proper administrative and support staff.
  • Report any damage or maintenance needs to the Wellness Manager and document in the Maintenance sheet immediately.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Parks & Recreation Department Managers.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Required knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Some knowledge of equipment, materials and supplies used in building and grounds maintenance; some knowledge of equipment and supplies used to do minor repairs; some knowledge of first aid and applicable safety precautions.
  • Skill in operation of listed tools and equipment.
  • Ability to work independently and to complete daily activities according to work schedule; ability to lift heavy objects, walk and stand for long periods of time, and to perform strenuous physical labor under adverse field conditions; ability to communicate orally and in writing; ability to use equipment and tools properly and safely; ability to understand, follow, and transmit written and oral instructions; ability to establish effective working relationships with employees, supervisors, and the public.

Education and Experience:

  • High School diploma or GED equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience in customer service preferred.
  • Current CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications preferred.

Physical Requirements:

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk; and use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate objects, tools, or controls.
  • The employee is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear.
  • The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee occasionally works near moving mechanical parts. The employee occasionally works in highs, precarious places and is occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, fumes or airborne particles, and toxic chemicals. The employee is occasionally exposed to the risk of electrical shock.

title: Community Health Worker
description:
We are seeking a Community Health Worker who is passionate about making a difference in our community. At Lone Star Circle of Care (LSCC) we strive for exceptional, equitable patient care that leads to healthier communities. Our Community Health Workers (CHWs) collaborate with providers, patients, and community-based organizations to address clinical health concerns and Non-Medical Drivers of Health (NMDOH) that may impact overall health outcomes. CHWs connect patients to resources supporting LSCC’s vision to eliminate health inequities and facilitate wellness. This position participates as part of the integrated health care delivery team and will be required to float to LSCC facilities as needed. The Community Health Worker will collaborate with employees at all levels within the organization, must be able to maintain professional working relationships, and provide excellent customer service.

If you have the ambition and desire to work in a friendly and fun environment, LSCC is the place for you!

A Day in the Life of a Community Health Worker may look like this:

  • Responsible for establishing trusting relationships with patients and their families while effectively communicating LSCC’s mission.
  • Bridge community, cultural, linguistic, and educational barriers to emphasize importance of establishing a health care home.
  • Screen patients for NMDOH needs and connect and assist patients and their families with accessing appropriate resources, programs, and services based on their individual needs.
  • Connect and assist patients and their families with appropriate resources and services in accordance with their unique needs.
  • Document each patient visit/interaction in the electronic medical records system.
  • Continuously expand knowledge and understanding of available community resources, services, and programs.
  • Assist and provide referrals for services to community agencies as appropriate and motivate/teach patients to seek care.
  • Assist the patient with understanding care plans and instructions; motivate the patient to be an active, engaged participant in their health.
  • Support and educate patients in disease management and adherence to their care plan while decreasing dependency and promoting self-efficacy.
  • Support and educate patients in medication management and adherence to their care plan.
  • Coach the patient/family in effective management of their chronic health conditions and self-care.
  • Provide up-to-date and appropriate general health and wellness education to patients.
  • Provide support and notify the clinical team regarding any patient changes that may affect the established care plan.
  • Coordinate and maintain food pantry operations, as applicable to assigned clinic location, including inventory management, recordkeeping, supply monitoring, and overall pantry maintenance.
  • Assist patients with completing LSCC registration forms and applications.
  • Other duties as assigned.

We ask our Community Health Workers to possess a minimum of:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Valid Texas driver's license
  • Food Handler’s Certificate required upon hire or must be obtained within 10 days of hire
  • Texas DSHS Community Health Worker (CHW) or Promotor(a) Certificate required or obtained within 12 months

The following experience/skills are preferred:

  • Familiarity with local community and community resources
  • Knowledge of medical terminology
  • Bilingual English/Spanish language skills

Key Success Factors

Some key factors that will make an individual successful in this role:

  • The ability to problem solve
  • Organizational skills
  • Attention to detail
  • Team player personality
  • Time management

Benefits

LSCC offers a competitive benefits package, including:

  • Competitive salary;
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance;
  • LSCC paid Life insurance;
  • LSCC paid Short-Term and Long-Term Disability insurance;
  • Paid Time Off; and
  • 403b Employee Retirement Plan

title: Injection Molding Process Technician
description:
At M&M Industries, we take pride in producing high-quality plastic packaging solutions that make a difference in everyday life. Our success starts with the people who make it all happen — from the production floor to our technical and engineering teams.
The Process Technician is responsible for performing die, color, and material changeovers while starting up, maintaining, and optimizing injection molding machines. This role ensures that molding processes run efficiently, meet company quality standards, and achieve production targets. The Process Technician also supports troubleshooting efforts, assists with new mold trials, and maintains accurate records of process adjustments and results.
Schedule: 6:30 PM – 7:00 AM (Nights) — 2 on, 2 off, 3 on rotation
Process Technician Pay & Career Progression
Starting level is based on relevant experience and demonstrated technical skills:

Process Technician I: $21.91/hr
Process Technician II: $25.05/hr
Process Technician III: $28.19/hr
Process Technician IV: $31.32/hr
Process Technician V: $33.83/hr

Technicians may earn pay increases within their level at established milestones, including 90 days and one, two, and three years, based on performance.
Shift differential is available for qualifying shifts.
Key Responsibilities:

Follows all safety policies and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures to ensure a safe work environment.
Sets up and adjusts injection molding machines, auxiliary equipment, and tooling for production runs.
Monitors and optimizes molding processes to ensure consistent part quality and cycle efficiency.
Troubleshoots and resolves molding defects, process deviations, and equipment malfunctions.
Performs mold and material changeovers, ensuring proper setup, documentation, and communication with the team.
Maintains detailed records of process parameters, adjustments, and troubleshooting activities.
Uses a forklift and/or overhead crane to pull, change, or set molds safely and efficiently.
Maintains a clean and organized work environment in accordance with 5S principles.
Collaborates with the Engineering Team to develop samples for new molds and materials.
Performs machine testing, process validation, and assists in continuous improvement initiatives.
Utilizes knowledge of processing various grades of plastic to produce quality parts that meet customer expectations.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Competencies (Knowledge/Skills/Abilities):

Proficient mechanical aptitude and understanding of injection molding processes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word.
Comprehensive understanding of Food Safety, GMP, PRP, and HACCP requirements as they relate to food-contact packaging (where applicable).
Basic understanding of decoupled molding (preferred).

Education:

High School Diploma or G.E.D. (required)

Experience:

Required years of experience may vary based on qualifications, skills, and level within the role.

Licenses & Certifications:

Forklift Certification (required; in-house training provided)
RJG Training or Certification (preferred)

Physical Requirements:

Work is performed in a manufacturing environment that may be hot or cold and requires PPE at all times (safety glasses, ear protection, etc.).
Ability to lift and handle 45–55 pounds.
Ability to perform work in standing or sitting positions as required.
Ability to work in tight or confined spaces.

What We Offer
M&M Industries offers a competitive benefits package designed to support our employees and reward the work that drives our success. Full-time employees may elect medical, dental and vision coverage effective on their first day of employment. We also offer paid vacation/PTO and discretionary time off (DTO), with the amount and timing based on position and tenure; paid company holidays after 90 days; and a 401(k) with company match beginning on the first day of the month following 90 days of employment. Educational reimbursement is available after one year of employment. Eligible employees may also participate in quarterly profit sharing when company performance thresholds are met. Hourly employees who work on a recognized holiday receive time-and-a-half for all hours worked. Benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.

title: Relay Technician – Pearsall, TX / Hourly Grade 10
description:
Programs, installs and maintains protective relaying, batteries, battery charges, stand by generators, air conditioners and other substation equipment. Performs electrical tests and repairs concerned with maintenance and performance evaluation of in-service relays to prevent and remedy abnormal behavior or failure of transmission and distribution lines and equipment. Analyzes test results and interprets electrical diagrams to locate defective equipment.

Working Conditions

Lifts and carries up to 80 pounds and pulls, pushes or drags up to 80 pounds with or without assistance. Sits, stands, stoops or twists for extended periods of time. Works both indoors and outdoors in extreme temperatures including heat, cold, humidity, temperature swings and inclement weather, frequent exposure to dust, odor, electrical, mechanical, loud noise and toxic hazards. Operates hand tools, heavy equipment, light trucks and power tools. 20/20 corrected vision is required to perform visual inspection of small defects, small parts and operation of measurement devices and assembly of fabricated parts. Ability to travel to and from meetings or other business-related events. May be required to work after hours, weekends and holidays and respond timely to urgent or emergency situations. Ability to respond to call out requirements within 30 minutes.

Essential Functions

  • Proficiently uses hand, power tools, meters and other test equipment in energized substations to install, maintain, repair and program protective relays and associated wiring and equipment.
  • Applies, reads, understands, reviews and corrects schematic, wiring diagram blueprints and substation drawings and inspections.

title: Senior Director Finance
description:
SinaLite is a leading wholesale trade printer and custom packaging provider, serving 20,000+ print businesses, resellers, and entrepreneurs across Canada and the US. With 26 years of printing experience and over $45 million invested in cutting-edge print technology, we help our clients maximize their print profits — and we're just as invested in helping our own team grow. We were named a 2025 Regional Finalist in Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, and we're looking for our next Senior Director of Finance to help us keep raising the bar.


Compensation: $160,000 - $200,000

Location: 335 Steelcase Rd East, Markham, ON (In Office)


About the Opportunity

SinaLite and Willowpack are looking for a Senior Director of Finance to join our leadership team and take ownership of the financial strategy, discipline, and decision support required to support two growing manufacturing businesses.


This is a hands-on senior leadership role for an experienced finance professional who understands that strong finance leadership goes well beyond reporting the numbers. You will help shape business decisions by bringing greater visibility and discipline to cash, working capital, manufacturing costs, margins, investments, and financial risk.


SinaLite is an established wholesale printing business focused on protecting and expanding margins, while Willowpack is a rapidly growing packaging manufacturer requiring disciplined management of capital, working capital, and costs as it scales.

We're looking for a skeptical, analytical, and commercially minded finance leader who is comfortable challenging assumptions, getting into the details, developing a strong finance team, and giving leadership the financial clarity needed to make better decisions.

For the right individual, this role offers a clear opportunity to grow into a VP-level position within approximately two years.


What You'll Be Responsible For

Cash, Liquidity & Working Capital

  • Build and own a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity models.
  • Develop, measure, and report key working-capital metrics, including DPO, DIO, DSO, and the cash conversion cycle.
  • Partner with Operations, Sourcing, and the Controller to improve inventory, receivables, and payables performance.
  • Model the cash and working-capital impact of business growth and changing operating conditions.
  • Manage banking and lender relationships, credit facilities, and lease obligations.


Manufacturing Costing & Margin Management

  • Develop and maintain accurate job, product, and SKU-level costing across our manufacturing operations.
  • Ensure costing accurately reflects materials, labour, yield, scrap, and other production costs.
  • Partner with Sales to establish pricing guardrails, cost-based pricing floors, and margin expectations.
  • Provide clear financial reporting that allows leadership to understand the economics and performance of SinaLite and Willowpack independently.


FP&A & Strategic Decision Support

  • Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning.
  • Translate strategic objectives into measurable financial targets and forecasts.
  • Develop forward-looking, probability-weighted risk and opportunity assessments covering both profitability and cash.
  • Build financial business cases for capital expenditures, investments, and major strategic decisions.
  • Track investment performance and returns following implementation.
  • Provide leadership with scenario modelling and data-driven recommendations to support major business decisions.


Compliance, Controls & Government Funding

  • Oversee government funding opportunities, including applications, claims, compliance, and reporting.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable Canadian and U.S. tax, regulatory, and financial reporting requirements.
  • Strengthen internal financial controls, policies, and procedures appropriate for a growing manufacturing organization.


Finance Team Leadership

  • Assess the existing finance structure and identify opportunities to strengthen capabilities.
  • Recruit, coach, and develop finance and FP&A talent.
  • Ensure team members are positioned effectively across controllership, treasury, and FP&A responsibilities.
  • Build greater financial accountability across the organization.
  • Help operational and functional leaders understand the financial impact of their decisions.


Systems, Data & AI

  • Maximize the value of NetSuite and our broader financial reporting systems.
  • Identify opportunities to automate recurring reporting and financial analysis.
  • Use AI, analytics, and emerging technologies to improve the speed and quality of financial insights.
  • Champion a data-driven approach to decision-making throughout the organization.


Qualifications

  • CPA designation required.
  • 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including at least 5 years in senior financial leadership within a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong manufacturing cost accounting experience, including job/product costing, inventory, material yield, and scrap.
  • Proven experience managing cash and working capital through periods of rapid business growth.
  • Strong FP&A, forecasting, scenario modelling, and financial modelling capabilities.
  • Experience evaluating capital expenditures and developing investment business cases.
  • Demonstrated ability to hire, develop, and lead high-performing finance teams.
  • Experience working within an entrepreneurial, privately held, or founder-led organization.
  • Experience within printing, packaging, converting, or a related manufacturing industry is a strong asset.


What We're Looking For

The right person for this role is someone who:

  • Challenges assumptions — You don't accept a number simply because it was presented to you. You validate it, understand it, and speak up when something doesn't make sense.
  • Gets into the details — You can operate strategically while still being willing to dig into the numbers when necessary.
  • Thinks ahead — You identify financial risks and opportunities before they become obvious.
  • Communicates directly — You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations for leaders across Finance, Operations, Sales, and other functions.
  • Takes ownership — You approach decisions with a business-owner mentality, high integrity, and accountability for outcomes.
  • Builds strong teams — You develop talent, raise expectations, and create a finance function capable of supporting continued growth.
  • Is comfortable challenging leadership — You have the confidence and executive presence to pressure-test assumptions and provide a different perspective when the numbers support it.


Why Join SinaLite & Willowpack?

This is an opportunity to take on a highly influential finance leadership position across two distinct manufacturing businesses at different stages of growth.


You'll have the opportunity to directly influence how we manage cash, evaluate investments, improve manufacturing margins, scale Willowpack, and make strategic decisions across the organization.


We're also looking for someone who can grow with us. For a high-performing finance leader who demonstrates the ability to operate as a trusted financial partner to the President and leadership team, this role offers a pathway toward VP-level leadership within approximately two years.


If you're a hands-on finance leader who enjoys challenging assumptions, solving complex manufacturing finance problems, building strong teams, and turning financial data into better business decisions, we'd like to hear from you.


Accessibility

SinaLite is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible workplace in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA). We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities.

Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process. If you require accommodation, please notify us at hr@sinalite.com, and we will work with you to meet your needs in a timely and respectful manner.

Information received relating to accommodation will be addressed confidentially.

title: IT Support Engineer
description:
About Portal

Portal Space Systems is on a mission to expand humanity’s freedom of movement in space. We’re building the spacecraft that makes that mission possible. From our Bothell, WA headquarters, we design vehicles with the maneuverability, resilience, and adaptability needed for the next era of orbital operations. Every system we build is in service of a simple idea: space should be more accessible, responsive, and capable. Joining Portal means stepping into a team that believes in bold engineering, fast iteration, and the power of small groups to change what’s possible. If you want your work to directly shape the future of in-space mobility, join us.

Position Summary

The IT Support Engineer owns Portal’s IT help desk queue and is the first point of contact for employee technology issues and requests. The role is responsible for triaging, resolving, and following through on tickets across Windows laptops, Microsoft 365, identity and access, and the company’s SaaS and engineering applications, resolving as much as possible on first touch and managing escalations through to closure. The role applies Lean practices to support operations, using ticket data, standard work, and root-cause fixes so recurring issues are prevented rather than repeatedly worked. This position works closely with IT’s engineering staff, Portal’s managed service provider (MSP), and employees across every department, and reports directly to the Director of IT.

Core Responsibilities

Help Desk Queue Ownership & First-Touch Resolution

  • Own the HaloITSM ticket queue end to end: triage, prioritize, and keep every open ticket moving, including those waiting on the MSP, vendors, or other IT staff
  • Resolve issues on first touch wherever possible across Windows endpoints, Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Microsoft 365 (GCC High), and Portal’s SaaS and engineering applications
  • Work each problem far enough to add real value before escalating; when escalation is needed, hand off with steps taken, evidence gathered, and business impact, then follow the ticket to resolution
  • Keep requesters informed with proactive status updates, and confirm the fix with the user before closing the loop
  • Deliver new-hire day-one readiness (device, accounts, and SSO apps working) and complete offboarding requests accurately and on time

Lean Support Operations & Continuous Improvement

  • Work tickets in single-piece flow: carry each ticket through to done before pulling the next, with work-in-progress kept visible and limited
  • Build quality in at the source: treat reopened tickets, repeat issues, and incomplete handoffs as defects, and trace each back to its root cause
  • Pull the andon cord when something is abnormal: flag emerging patterns, outages, and security concerns immediately so they are contained at the source instead of worked one ticket at a time
  • Use help desk metrics (first-contact resolution, reopen rate, time to resolution, ticket aging, CSAT) to find bottlenecks and improve outcomes for users and the business

Endpoints, Access & Compliance Support

  • Deploy, enroll, and maintain Windows laptops and peripherals through Intune, and support conference rooms (Microsoft Teams Rooms), printers, and other office technology
  • Process access requests and changes under least-privilege principles, keeping ticket records complete enough to serve as audit evidence for NIST 800-171.
  • Support company-wide tool rollouts and changes through user setup, training, and adoption follow-up.

What You Bring To Portal

  • Hands-on experience supporting Windows users, Microsoft 365, and Entra ID accounts, with working familiarity with Intune device management
  • A structured troubleshooting approach: isolating the problem, testing one change at a time, and switching approach rather than staying stuck
  • Sound escalation judgment: knowing when a problem is theirs to solve, when to research further, and when a handoff is the fastest path for the user
  • Demonstrated ownership of outcomes: following up on open items, closing loops with users and vendors, and treating the whole queue as their responsibility rather than only their assigned tickets
  • Attention to detail in ticket notes, access changes, and asset records, where accuracy matters for both the next technician and the audit trail
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly from documentation, vendor resources, and hands-on exploration, with demonstrated self-directed learning and certifications; Portal runs many systems, and no one is expected to know them all on day one
  • Familiarity with, or interest in applying, Lean and Toyota Production System practices (flow, built-in quality, root cause analysis, visual management) to service work
  • Clear, courteous written and verbal communication with users at every technical level, from new hires to engineers to executives.

Basic Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in an IT help desk, service desk, or desktop support role
  • Hands-on experience supporting Windows 10/11 endpoints and Microsoft 365 users, including account and access issues in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)
  • Experience with Microsoft Intune or a comparable endpoint management platform
  • Experience troubleshooting a broad range of desktop software and SaaS applications
  • Experience working a ticket queue in an ITSM platform (HaloITSM, ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice, or similar)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 GCC High or other FedRAMP-aligned environments
  • Exposure to Lean, Kanban, Six Sigma, or ITIL practices in a support or operations setting
  • Experience writing runbooks or knowledge base articles
  • Experience training peers, onboarding new technicians, or acting as a queue or shift lead
  • CompTIA A+, Microsoft MD-102 (Endpoint Administrator), or ITIL 4 Foundation; or willingness to obtain within 6 months of hire
  • Experience supporting engineering users and applications (CAD/PLM tools such as Siemens NX or Teamcenter, license servers, high-performance workstations)
  • Experience in or genuine interest in aerospace or space technology

Pay Range: $75,000 - $105,000

Compensation and Benefits:

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

At Portal, your base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company equity at an exciting time of company growth as well as potential bonuses. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k)-retirement plan, paid parental leave, you may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 12 or more paid holidays per year as well as sick time.

ITAR Statement

This position may involve access to technical data and defense-related materials controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Eligibility to access ITAR-controlled items requires that candidates be U.S. persons, which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and other protected individuals as defined by U.S. law. Employment is contingent upon verification of ITAR eligibility and, where applicable, obtaining any required export authorization or license.

Equal Opportunity Statement

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
